### 0. THE METHOD, DECLARED BEFORE THE RUN

**EVERY FIGURE A CLOSE PUBLISHES IS PRODUCED BY RUNNING SOMETHING AGAINST `chapters/volume-*/chapter-*.md`. NO FIGURE IS READ OUT OF A STATE FILE. FOUR FIGURES IN THE LAST TWO CLOSES DID NOT REPRODUCE AND ONE OF THEM WOULD HAVE COST VOLUME 08 ITS FIRST MORNING.** Counts of files and bytes are `len(glob)` and `getsize`, run twice. The calendar is parsed out of each chapter's own first six lines, per file, never pooled, and checked at **every one of the fifty chapters and not at the ends**; a hyphenated spelled integer is additive. String counts are sweeps with the heading lines excluded, and the totals printed are the sum of per-file counts, not a separate whole-volume run. **The word count is `re.findall(r"[A-Za-z’'\-]+", text)`,** which reproduces this project's existing Batch 0005 figure to the word; a whitespace split gives a different number and the method is named so nobody has to guess. **The span scan's whole method is at §1, because the close is the phase that has to publish it.** A figure that failed to reproduce on a second run would be printed as failing; the one measurement that moved between measuring and printing is the byte count of the sentence that prints a byte count, and it is at §7 and run to a fixed point in `state/batch-summary.md` as well, with the same string in both files.

### 1. THE SPAN SCAN, IN FULL, AND THE FOUR FIGURES THAT DO NOT REPRODUCE

**PER FILE, IN THE TEN FILES SEPARATELY, SO THAT NO WINDOW CROSSES A BOUNDARY: COLLAPSE EVERY WHITESPACE RUN TO ONE SPACE, THEN TRIM THE FILE, KEEP THE HEADING LINE AND THE `---` BREAKS, TAKE EVERY WINDOW OF EXACTLY *k* CHARACTERS AT EVERY POSITION, POOL INTO ONE TALLY, KEEP ONLY THE WINDOWS OCCURRING MORE THAN ONCE. *DISTINCT* IS THE NUMBER OF THOSE; *OCCURRENCES* IS THEIR TOTAL.**

**THE TRIM IS PART OF THE METHOD AND IT IS THE WHOLE OF THE ARGUMENT. `0341`–`0350` RETURNS 1,838 / 4,287 WITHOUT THE PER-FILE TRIM AND 1,837 / 4,285 WITH IT, BOTH RUN HERE AS A CONTROL. THAT IS WHY THE FORMER HAS SURVIVED IN FOUR DOCUMENTS OF THIS PROJECT AND THE LATTER WAS DEBATED IN TWO. THE FIGURE WAS NEVER THE ARGUMENT; THE TRIM WAS. THE TRIM IS DECISIVE ON EXACTLY ONE OF THE EIGHT PAIRS BELOW AND CHANGES NONE OF THE OTHER SEVEN, INCLUDING ALL SIX VOLUME 08 BANDS.**

**CALIBRATION FIRST, REPRODUCED TO THE DIGIT ON BOTH RUNS: `0331`–`0340` 122 / 254 and 1,201 / 2,817; `0341`–`0350` 534 / 1,081 and 1,837 / 4,285.** Then `0351`–`0360` 16/32 and 343/747; `0361`–`0370` 171/342 and 942/2,066; `0371`–`0380` 400/830 and 1,712/3,860; `0381`–`0390` 377/757 and **1,493/3,308**; `0391`–`0400` **100/200 and 1,474/3,424**; **the whole volume 3,003/6,376 and 11,389/27,462**, which no band can run. **200 ÷ 100 = 2.000 exactly at seventy and no seventy-character window in `391`–`400` occurs even three times; 3,424 ÷ 1,474 = 2.323 at forty.** The repeated forty-character windows are the band's own opening and closing register and are declared rather than left for a reviewer.

**THE DEAD FIGURES, none of which reproduces in any form run here: 1,746 / 3,937; 1,838 / 4,287; 1,507 / 3,327; and 199 / 398. THE THIRD IS PRINTED IN `workspace/volume-08/batch-0005/PROMPT.md` §5 FOR `0381`–`0390` AND THE TRUE FIGURE IS 1,493 / 3,308, WITH THE TRIM AND WITHOUT IT. THAT PROMPT IS A COMPLETED PHASE'S PROMPT AND IS NOT EDITED, BECAUSE A COMPLETED PHASE'S PROMPT IS WHAT THAT PHASE WAS TOLD AND NOT WHAT IT FOUND; BATCH 0005 MEASURED IT ITSELF AND PRINTED THE RIGHT VALUE IN ITS OWN RECEIPT, WHICH IS WHY THE ERROR NEVER REACHED THE MANUSCRIPT.**

**AND THE ONE THING A PER-BAND RUN CANNOT SEE, WHICH IS A FINDING: A SCAN RUN PER BAND IS BLIND TO A REPETITION THAT CROSSES A BAND BOUNDARY, AND THERE IS EXACTLY ONE SUCH WHOLE-LINE REPETITION IN FIFTY CHAPTERS.** *She turned the chair round, which is what she does when she is going to do something with her hands* is at `372:31` and `382:47`, byte-identical, 101 characters, in two different batches. ### 4. THE FINDING OF VOLUME 08, IN ONE SENTENCE, WITH ITS CITATION

**A RULE IN A CITY IS A THING SOMEBODY READS OUT IN A ROOM TO THE PEOPLE IT IS ABOUT, AND THE EXPOSURE WAS NOT THAT ANYBODY HID ANYTHING AND NOT THAT ANYBODY LIED — IT WAS THAT THE ROOM AND THE STREET AND THE BOOK WERE THREE PLACES AND ONE OF THEM WAS NEVER IN THE OTHER TWO, THE SAME RULE IN TWO KINDS OF WARD PRODUCED TWO RESULTS, THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN THEM WAS A DOOR, AND NO DOCUMENT IN THAT CITY MENTIONED A DOOR.** *The room, the street and the book are three places and one of them has never been in the other two*, the heading of the fourth line of a return, read out at the fifth hour and copied fair, `395:33`. The door is a woman on a stool doing arithmetic on a slate in front of forty people, `393:37`. The second half is the bench's mouth and not his: *a row of things laid out in a room is nothing, it is a morning — and a bench of four with no form in front of it is also nothing, and that is the thing we have been for four hundred years*, `392:61`, `392:65`.

### 5. THE FOUR THINGS THAT ARE STILL NOT TRUE, AND ARE NOT TO BE WRITTEN AS FIXED

1. **THE RIGHT OF REFUSAL IS UNRESTORED AND NOBODY HAS ONE** — not the bench, not the woman of twenty-eight, not the boy of eight. No form in four hundred miles lets a person in Orison be outside the order, `400:73`. The missing sixth part was an **exit**, a way out of an arrangement a person is inside, and not a refusal, a way of not being in it.
2. **ABOUT A HUNDRED AND FORTY PEOPLE ARE DEAD**, dead before the first morning he came into the city, remembered as dead, `400:85`. **THE FIGURE IS NOT PARTITIONED ANYWHERE AND MAY NOT BE** — four books in four wards and no office the four of them can hand a book to, and the four of them have never been added together and cannot be, `400:47`.
3. **THE CHILD OF EIGHT IS BETTER AND CANNOT BE DISCHARGED AND HAS NEVER BEEN NAMED OUT LOUD IN ANY ROOM IN HIS LIFE**, two lines in two halls and one door, `400:69`. He is founded on a class of persons and not on a name.
4. **THE BELL IN THAT COUNTY IS STILL NOT HUNG, THE PORCH IN THE VALLEY IS STILL GONE, AND THE CORRIDOR STILL STANDS WITH A BELL UNPAID**, said out loud for the first time by a clerk who cannot do one single thing about it, `400:61`. It is four hundred miles off and **he is in a city.**

### 6. WHAT THE VOLUME DID, WHAT IT DID NOT DO, AND WHAT A VOLUME 09 WRITER MUST NOT INHERIT

**DID:** the form under a window and the bench that came down the hill, `391`; a person who went into a record because he asked to, `391`, `392`; seven things read out and no two joined, `392`; the difference between two kinds of ward shown to be a door, `393`; the return, the fourth line and the heading, `395`; the price of a list of nine hundred doors said out loud to a magistrate before she took it up, `396`; two years and a hundred and twelve days with the working in the keeper's mouth, `397`; the bill, the blank fourth line, nine people, `398`; and the one want in the volume he did not answer, `399`. **DID NOT:** restore the right of refusal; make anybody a villain or say anybody hid anything; thank, forgive, redeem or relieve anybody; get three hundred names onto a plate; answer its own question. **He said a price out loud in this city seven times and the seventh was a line at the top of a form that a man of thirty-one with a bad ear asked for himself, and at `399` he did not use the instrument at all and nobody asked him why.**

**DO NOT INHERIT:** (1) **HE IS IN A CITY; THE MARCH IS FOUR HUNDRED MILES OFF AND NOTHING IN VOLUME 09 MAY BE SET THERE.** (2) **THE ORDER'S AGE IS UNPRINTABLE**; the word **part** in `393:3` and `394:3` is the age of the *sixth part*, filled in at Chapter 374, and 19 and 20 are right. ### 8. THE HAND-OFF, AND THE SHAPE OF A VOLUME 09 CLOSE HAND-OFF

**THE MERCY TRIAL'S SETTLEMENT IS THE FLOOR VOLUME 09 STANDS ON AND NOT A THING IT UNDOES.** The order has an end, a date, a review and a second pair of hands on it, and the second pair is a bench of four and not a person. ### 1. THE MIDPOINT IS DELIVERED AT 374, AND IT IS `series.md:191` AS WRITTEN

A boy of eight at the end of a run of boards in the low hall at the end of Tallowgate is worse than the other nine, is not saved, and does not die. He goes to a bed at the top of this city on a barrow and is better. The permanent rule is the sixth part of an order that had five parts and a half — a line with a date in it and, beside the date, the word *standing*, so the date does not arrive. He asked for the half to be filled with three sentences: *Any person who is inside the protection of this order and who is worse than every other person in the place they are sleeping in may be put in a bed in any hall in this city. A hall that takes a person under that sentence does not need that person's name on the roll of its ward. That sentence stands with the rest of the order and it may be ended only by the person who may end the rest of the order.* **IT IS FOUNDED ON A CLASS AND NOT ON A PERSON, AND THAT IS THE POINT: A RULE ABOUT A PERSON HAS A NAME AT THE FOOT OF IT AND CAN BE ARGUED WITH FOR EVER; A RULE ABOUT A CLASS CANNOT. THE BOY'S NAME IS NOT SAID OUT LOUD IN ANY ROOM IN ANY OF THE TEN CHAPTERS.**

**THE RULE IS GOOD AND FOUR PEOPLE OF A PLACE SAY SO.** It outlasts a magistrate going out of office, it cannot be argued down at a gate in a cold street, it costs nothing that anybody can see this month, and it is the argument he made against himself in his third week and heard and found right. **NOBODY IS A VILLAIN, NOBODY HID ANYTHING, AND MAGISTRATE RELL SIGNS IT OFFSTAGE AT `374:7` AND IS NOT ON STAGE AND IS NOT THANKED.**

### 1. THE SIXTY DEFECTS, IN SEVEN CLASSES, EACH WITH ITS CHAPTER

**CLASS ONE — THE DAYS-IN-CITY COUNT, ELEVEN PLACES, AND IT IS THE WHOLE OF THE FIRST CLASS. THE BOOK'S RULE IS ELAPSED, NOT ORDINAL: `chapter-0355.md:17` says *a face on you that has been in this city four days* on his fifth morning, `chapter-0355.md:85` says *you have now been in it four and I would like it to be five* on the same morning, and `chapter-0360.md:21` says *a man who has been in a city nine days* on his tenth morning. All three are elapsed. This band had printed the ORDINAL instead, which is one high everywhere.** Days-in-city ordinal is `chapter − 350` (Chapter 351 is day one and he arrived at the seventh hour of it) and the ELAPSED count, which is what a sentence about a duration wants, is `chapter − 351`. **Corrected: `361:13` and `361:143` eleven → ten; `363:85` thirteen → twelve; `364:119` fourteen → thirteen; `365:33`, `365:65`, `365:81` fifteen → fourteen; `366:99` sixteen → fifteen; `367:49`, `367:63`, `367:69`, `367:95`, `367:105` seventeen → sixteen. (a) `369:73` said a document had been received *on the first day of this month*, which is a month-date with the month left out, and the volume permits no month-word at all. The line now says fourteen days and names the room.**

**CLASS THREE — THE CHALK, FOUR PLACES, AND IT WAS RUNNING BACKWARDS. The stock is one lot of nine days bought with a penny, and a day is three marks, and the whole of it is twenty-seven marks on a slate. She begins on `361` and puts nine marks on nine doors that afternoon, which is three days of chalk in one day, and every number after that follows. `361:91` said six days of the nine were left when all nine were, and `362:5` said two days were gone and seven left — a stock that goes UP overnight, which is the one kind of money error no instrument can forgive. `362:5` now reads one day out of the nine and six left, which is exact; `363:97` now reads four days' worth, which is the end of that day; `366:29`'s *I have not got two days of that chalk left* was already right and is left alone; `368:111`'s *whose chalk ran out yesterday* was already right and is left alone; `370:63` said *Yesterday* where the last of it went on three days ago, and said *the day you met me at a standpipe* where the day is the end of a row on `361`, and said *that is eleven days* where it is ten. **THE ARC NOW CLOSES: nine marks on `361`, three a day on `362` through `367`, nothing at all on `368`, `369` and `370`, twenty-seven marks, and three days at the end of it with nothing to mark with.**

### 2. EVERY FINDING THE BAND MADE, ONCE EACH, WITH THE CHAPTER. TWENTY-TWO, AND NONE IS A MYSTERY, AND NONE IS A REVEAL

1. **A hearing about a roll cannot be produced by anybody in this city, and the reason is not him: a ward sends matters to the bench, and a ward is a body only when a ward meets, and no form in this city calls a meeting of a ward, so a ward cannot send anything, and a person can send only a complaint, and a complaint about a book is a thing that happens to a person who keeps a book and not to the book.** `361`
2. **The record of a ward is not defended because it is right and cannot be attacked because attacking it needs a form, and the roll is right, and a person who is not on it is not on it because the roll is wrong.** `361`
3. **Nine people in a passage can agree about everything and cannot change a block, because changing a block needs a form, and a form has a name at the top of it, and a name at the top of a form is a person, and nobody in the passage is going to do that to anybody, and not one of the nine has a duty to.** `361`
4. **A roll is not a list of people. A roll is a list of who is in the house, because a name gets into it only when somebody says it at a door, and the person who keeps it is not allowed to make a name up, and if she started she would have to keep doing it, and then the book would be a list of what one woman thought.** `362`
5. **A roll is only as good as the door it was written at, and there is no second witness to any of it and there never has been, and that is not a defect in a record: that is what a record made at doors is.** `362`
6. **A person who said her own name at her own door and a person who was written into a book by somebody else's hand are the same door, and from outside the door you cannot tell them apart, and there is no form anywhere in this city that asks a person which one they are.** `362`, `365`
7. **THE BAND'S GROUND FIGURE, AND IT IS THE FIRST FIGURE IN THIS VOLUME THAT IS A RATE INSTEAD OF A PRICE: a door costs a visit. Thirty doors a fortnight, a fortnight is fourteen days, thirty in fourteen is about two doors a day, about nine hundred doors, two a day for nine hundred is four hundred and twenty days, a year is three hundred and sixty-four, the difference is fifty-six, and the whole of it is one woman and it is unpaid.** `363`
8. **A mark on a door is not a document. It means *I have been here and you have not been here*, and there is no mark in this city for the other thing, which is that nobody was there at all.** `363`, `366`
9. **A corridor needs a person at the end of it and a room does not, and there is no third thing between the two of them, and a room in this city has a clerk at the end of it and a corridor has a person at the end of it.** `364`
10. **A notice with a magistrate's name at the foot of it is not a meeting of a ward; it is a thing a magistrate called, and whatever comes out of that room is whatever the person who called it says comes out of it, and it agrees for as long as she is magistrate.** `364`
11. **A draft needs witnesses, a public cost, and acceptance by the people who will live under it, and the third of the three is four hundred and twenty days of one woman's life, and it cannot be got, because the only way to get it is the instrument that takes it.** `365`
12. **A copy is a place somebody can be asked, and the copy he needed was not his own: it was the one a clerk of forty made out of his mouth in a room, without him, and it was already in a book upstairs, and it was there whether he liked it or not.** `365`
13. **THE BAND'S FINDING, DECLARED BEFORE IT WAS USED AND SAID ONCE, IN CHAPTER 366, IN THE MOUTH OF A PERSON OF A PLACE, IN ANSWER TO A QUESTION: the ward's public record is only as strong as its weakest door, and the weakest door cannot be found, because finding it means asking every householder whether they have ever left somebody off, and nobody has ever asked anybody that in four hundred years, and it cannot be asked without the ward knowing it is being asked, and a ward that is being checked produces a list of who checked it. So the book is right and the street is short and both of those are in the same ward and neither of them can be got at.** `366`
14. **Your instrument does not ask a question. It puts a person in a room. And the answer it gets back is never the answer, because the person in the room is a different person from the one who is hurt — and used on a boy of eleven at the second hour it cost nothing at all and got three names that cannot be spent, from a person who had no way of knowing she was saying them to a man with a leg.** `367`
15. **The arithmetic of a person is not a division, and a round of a ward is not a debt the keeper owes; it is a debt the ward owes, and a ward is not a person, and a person is the only thing a record can be asked about, and a ward has no name at the foot of anything — so the ward owes four hundred and twenty days and there is nobody on earth who can be asked whether it has paid them.** `367`
16. **A roll is not a record of who is in a ward. It is a record of who was in it, and nobody has ever crossed anything off, and the only person who could decide that a thing in a book is not true has no duty to decide it and no form to be asked by — so there is at least one dead man in the roll of Tallowgate, correctly entered, and the number of them is not knowable and is not askable.** `368`
17. **A man of fifty-nine does not know what a plate is for, has asked twice and been told it was the ward's business twice by two people who were right, and said so out loud in a room with nine clerks in it, and a bench of four thanked him for it, and it is in a fair hand, and it is the shortest thing anybody has put into the record of this city since the order went up.** `368`, `369`
18. **A bench of four can hold a hearing and cannot answer the question on the slate, and what it did was write down that it cannot answer it, and that is entered and kept, and nobody was relieved by it.** `369`
19. **The word the map uses for the nine of them — *anchor* — went into a book in this city in the middle of a sentence read aloud by a clerk, and nobody asked what it meant, and nobody remarked on it, and it is in the record with nobody's name on it, and it is the only one of the nine answers that any of them now has.** `369`
20. **A man in a room who answers a question about another person is not helping the person. He is making the person a person again, in front of nine clerks and forty people, on a day when the whole of the room is already on her.** `369`
21. **Nobody was relieved, nobody was forgiven, nobody was redeemed and nobody was thanked, and about a hundred and forty people are dead in four columns that have not been added up, and the fever is a fever.** `369`, `370`
22. **AND THE ONE THAT IS THE HAND-OFF'S THIRD REQUIREMENT AND THE BAND'S REASON FOR EXISTING: the round is unpaid and uncollectable, and the next nine days of chalk is a penny, and there is nobody whose job it is to buy it, and the person paying for it does not want to be asked, and if anybody did ask her the first thing that would happen is a rota, and a rota is a list, and a list is the thing that comes before a bill.** `370`

### 9. THE HAND-OFF, IN ONE PARAGRAPH, TO BATCH 0003

Twenty mornings in a city. He is thirty-one and Stage 4 and on one sheet in a building with about thirty clerks in it, and he has not put a name on anything in ten days and a clerk of thirty has told him out loud that he is not going to be entered off a document he has not been given, which is the one piece of protection this city has offered him. The shelter order still has five parts and a half and the word *standing* in the margin of an empty sixth line, and the missing half is an exit and not a refusal. A person is inside the protection if a roll has the name in it, and the roll is made at about nine hundred doors by the person who answers each one, and a roll is only as good as the door it was written at, and the ward cannot find its weakest door, and nobody has ever asked any householder whether they have ever left somebody off, and asking cannot be done without producing a list of who checked. A woman of twenty-eight has been going to those doors on her own account since the ninth morning with a penny's worth of chalk, has done twenty-seven of them in eleven days, has run out, will not be asked for a rota, and has a slate and a string and three days of not going. The woman of forty-four who keeps the paper roll has not been to a door in twelve weeks, is a fifth of the way through a round of four hundred and twenty days, is paid four shillings a year, is the only person in this city anybody can be asked about the roll, was asked eleven questions and more on the fourteenth over a whole day in a room of forty people, and is not relieved and is not thanked. The fourteenth produced a document received and entered, the word *anchor* in a book in the middle of a sentence nobody explained, a plate-cutter's sentence about four thousand lines, one sentence from a stranger, and no ruling at all. A block in a gatepost is still wrong, two hundred names are still on a paper and not on a plate, a man of forty-four is still nine steps up, a woman of sixty-one in a hall still cannot go home, a name of a man dead in the fourth week of the fever is still correctly in the roll and cannot be taken out, a boy of eleven is still the head of a house with three names in it and six people in it, a notice promised in a doorway six days ago has not been written, and about a hundred and forty people are dead. A child in a hall at the end of Tallowgate is worse than the other nine this morning, on a line in chalk that will be in chalk when the order ends, and his mother is at the standpipe, and nobody in this band has said his name out loud, and the order's sixth line is still empty, and the next thing in this volume is about him.

### 10. WHAT THIS BAND DID NOT DO, WHAT ITS OWN FIRST WRITING GOT WRONG, AND THE BYTE COUNT

THERE IS A CHILD IN A HALL WHO IS WORSE THAN THE OTHER NINE AND IS NOT SAVED AND IS NOT DYING, AND HE IS THE HOOK, AND HIS NAME IS NOT SAID.**

### 2. EVERY FINDING THE BAND MADE, ONCE EACH, WITH THE CHAPTER. TWENTY, AND NONE IS A MYSTERY, AND NONE IS A REVEAL

1. **The first thing that happens to a stranger in this city is a form with a line for a name in it, and he does not fill the line, and the man at the gate lets him in anyway and tells him he will be at that gate on his way out.** `351`
2. **A city is where a rule is visible because somebody reads it out, and the reading is a job, and about thirty clerks have been doing it properly for nine years.** `351`, `352`
3. **The order has five parts and a half, and the sixth line is a line with a date in it, and the date is not there, and in the margin beside the empty line there is one word, and the word is standing.** `352`
4. **The missing half is missing on purpose and the magistrate who left it out gives the best argument anybody makes in this band, and she is not sorry, and she is right: an order with an end in it is an order to be argued again every time the fever comes back.** `352`
5. **A covenant that names its burden in a category is obeying the sentence cut into the stone over the door of the room it is read in, and obeying it perfectly, and he tells her so and she has heard it nine times in eleven years.** `352`
6. **The order is worked by a book and not by a notice, and a book is made at a door by the person who answers it, and about ninety thousand people have not come and asked and nobody has ever been made to tell anybody.** `352`
7. **The book does not say who lives in a house. The book says who answers the door. A man who cannot come to a door is not a person in the book, and there is no paper in this city that would make him one, and he has asked twice and been told to come back with the paper.** `353`
8. **The plates are cut by anyone who brings a name and a fee, and nobody has ever asked the man who cuts them what a name is, and he has never asked whether a name is true, and both of those are eleven and thirty-one years of nobody asking anybody.** `356`
9. **A public record is kept in four places and has to be kept in agreement, and the agreement is held by weight, and the one that costs money to change is the one that decides.** `354`, `356`
10. **A recordwright who is tired of being the place where a stranger's plans go to be right says so in about nine sentences, and every part of it is correct, and she will not take a matter that is not his, and her own family's claim of six years stays unfiled and is said once and is not asked about again.** `354`
11. **Every arrangement is maintained by a person nobody has asked what it is for, and in a city the person did not know either, and that is the difference and it is the only difference.** `355`
12. **Naming a burden in a draft does not stop the harm. It puts a person underneath it so that the record can show that a person did it.** `358`
13. **A person who is in a record is not only somebody who can be asked about. A person who is in a record is the only thing about that record that can be asked about, and putting a name in does not open a thing up, it closes it down to one person, and it picks which person.** `360`
14. **In the country he came out of, saying a true thing out loud in front of other people is a thing that happens to a person. In this city it is a document, and a document is a place somebody can be asked, and there is a clerk whose job it is to write down what is said in that room, so in this city it does not matter in the least whether the room has a door on it.** `357`
15. **A rule with no way to end does nothing wrong. It stops a number from coming down.** `359`
16. **The number of beds free in six halls went up by four and did not come down by one, and about half the beds in the city are physically empty, and the woman on the stool knows both of those figures and can put up only one of them.** `359`
17. **A count a person keeps, a count a person asks for, and a count four clerks cannot add up, are three different things, and the fourth thing is a room, and a room is the only instrument in this city that costs nothing and has not been used since before the fever came.** `356`, `359`
18. **His own name is on a sheet in this city, put there by a clerk of thirty who wrote it off a document in front of him under a written request for a witness, and he has not seen the sheet, and there is no form in this city that will take a man off a piece of paper once it is on there, and that is Volume 07's finding arriving in a building with about thirty clerks in it.** `352`, `360`
19. **He asked a question about a record, a person of a place answered it in front of nine people, and he spent the answer four seconds later; and the instrument that makes a person a person in a record does not require him to be the one who says the name.** `360`
20. **The translated interface offered a man with a bad leg and no standing a choice of three things about a public record, and offered it to nobody else in the building, and four people on the floor below and a bench of four upstairs did not know it had happened, and he noticed, and did not ask, and wrote one line on the back of a candle bill, and there is no hand in this country he could have given it to.** `360`

### 9. THE HAND-OFF, IN ONE PARAGRAPH, TO BATCH 0002

Ten days in a city. He is thirty-one and Stage 4 and on no paper of his own making, and his name is on one sheet in a building with about thirty clerks in it because a clerk of thirty wrote it there under a written request for a witness, and there is no form to take it off, and he has said so out loud and been refused. A fever has been in four low wards for eleven weeks and about a hundred and forty people are dead and nobody has counted them properly and the four columns have not been added up and cannot be, because there are four clerks in four wards and no office for the four of them to hand anything to. Ansa Rell wrote an order in the third week with five parts and a half and left the sixth line empty on purpose, and the word beside the empty line is standing, and she is right about why, and the order is saving the centre of the city and putting about three hundred people outside the protection, and the person who can say that out loud in a room is a clerk who has about four hundred entries in an afternoon. A ward's public record is four things that have to agree — a plate, a paper, a keeper, and a block in a gatepost that holds a weight — and the plate carries about thirteen hundred names and the paper about fifteen hundred and the block agrees with neither, and the whole cost of the two hundred that are missing is eight shillings and the cost of a hearing is a pound three and sixpence, and a Bench date has been bought and is in a book, and a meeting of a ward is the only instrument in this city that costs nothing and cannot be called because no form says who calls it. A woman of forty-four has kept the paper roll of Tallowgate for eleven years, has gone round nine hundred doors at thirty a fortnight for nine rounds, has not been to a door in eleven weeks, is paid four shillings a year, did not know what the roll was for until a stranger asked her, refused him her name on the fifth morning for the exact reason that he took it on the tenth, and is now the only person in this city anybody can ask about the roll, and was asked eleven questions by a woman from the magistrate's office and a man with her, of which two were about her. He wrote four clauses and a half on the back of a chandler's bill and did not file it and did not tear it up, and it is in his coat, and its fifth clause names her. A man of forty-four cannot come down nine steps and has asked twice and been told to come back with the paper, and his boards came off the window at about the fourth hour and the room was a different room by the fifth and nobody in the street knew. A woman of sixty-one has been in a hall nine days and is better and cannot be discharged, and a man of fifty-eight on a stool has twenty-one people on the books of a hall with eleven beds and chalks a number she can stand behind. A woman of about twenty-eight is going to doors on her own account with nine days of chalk and a promise from him that he will not say one word about it, and a man of thirty-one with a bad ear keeps nineteen names with nothing over them and wants his own name off a slate and cannot get it. A boy of seventeen set out from the March in the last week of that country with a book that can order things and cannot date them, and he is not in this city and has not arrived. The fourteenth is a date in a chamber upstairs, and the Bench has asked for a witness, and the question is what the Bench is to do with a document it did not make that says a thing is under this city and not found. And one line on the back of a candle bill, which is not a question: a thing was put to a man with a bad leg in a room with a plate in it, and it was not put to the bench of four, and nobody in the building knows.

The sentence also contradicted the clerk's *the order has been up since the second week* two pages later. **NOW: THE THIRD WEEK, WHICH IS WHAT *state/continuity.md` §2.14 AND §3.1 ALREADY SAID, AND ABOUT FORTY OF THEM DEAD, WHICH IS A FIGURE IN THE MAGISTRATE'S OWN MOUTH AND IS CONSISTENT WITH A HUNDRED AND FORTY BY THE ELEVENTH WEEK.** Nine hundred is at zero over the band.
7. **THE ELVENTH WEEK WAS A WEEK-ORDINAL WHERE THE BOOK NEEDED A COUNT.** *This eleventh week* at `353:9` and *when the water came in the eleventh week* at `355:39` both collided with the eleventh week of the Shelf year, which is two hundred and thirty days before the band opens, while the same two chapters and three state files say the water came eleven weeks ago. **NOW *EVERY MORNING OF THESE ELEVEN WEEKS* AND *WHEN THE WATER CAME, ELEVEN WEEKS BACK*.** The number eleven is right and the ordinal was the error.
8. **AN AGE WAS WRONG IN CHAPTER 354 AND IT NAMED THE WRONG PERSON.** The second name on the sheet for a witness was *a man of forty-four who works in a yard at the low end of Tallowgate*, and the next line says the Bench wants anybody who can say what a plate is for, which is Bevin Tarr, **fifty-nine**, twice established at `354:49` and `356:11`. The only other man of forty-four in Tallowgate is Ivo Serrel, who is in a room and cannot leave. **NOW FIFTY-NINE**, which is what `state/open-threads.md` PART ONE ITEM 7 and `state/continuity.md` §2.2 already said.
9. **THE RECORD ASSERTED THREE THINGS THE CHAPTERS DO NOT CONTAIN, AND A FRACTION THAT CONTRADICTS THE BAND'S OWN ARITHMETIC.** A healer of about sixty is described in `state/continuity.md` §1 and `state/open-threads.md` item 12 as having named the fever in nine words; **the word *healer* is at zero over Chapters 351 to 360** and no such scene exists in Chapter 355 or anywhere else, so both entries now say he is one of the six people of this volume, is not in the band, and is still owed his nine words. `outline/volume-08.md` §CENTRAL PRESSURE carried the same guess and is repaired. And *about a third of the people in this city* at `352:121` and *about a third of the people in two wards* at `354:17` cannot both stand with *three hundred names short across four wards* at `357:13` and a Ninth Weir that is a mile of yards: **a third of ninety thousand is thirty thousand. NOW *A GREAT MANY PEOPLE IN THIS CITY* AND *A GOOD MANY PEOPLE IN TWO WARDS*,** which is the phrase the woman at the standpipe already uses in her own mouth at `353:19` and which removes the collision without giving away the three hundred, which is Batch 0002's to find.
10. **AND THE SIXTH FILE'S HEADER SAID *ALL TEN FIGURES IN THE MONEY TABLE ARE SPOKEN BY A PERSON OF A PLACE*, WHICH IS THE SENTENCE §4 HAD ALREADY CONTRADICTED WITH FOUR *narrator* LABELS.** §4's principle sentence and all four labels are corrected above, the receipt is that three of the five new figures are in the mouth of a person of a place and the other two are put aloud by him in the public room at `357` where a clerk's fair hand and a man at the rail check them, and the next band is told which of the two things it is doing.

12. **AND THE ONE THAT WAS NOT A FINDING BUT A TRAP FOR THE NEXT WRITER:** `workspace/volume-08/batch-0002/PROMPT.md` §4.7 told the next band that `CORRECT` *in any case* is zero and listed it among the patterns that must come back clean. A band that had obeyed the prompt literally would have cut eleven correct uses of an ordinary word out of good dialogue to satisfy a pattern that was never the prohibition. **The prompt now says uppercase, and prints the eleven.**

**AND THE THING THE RUNNING-TOTAL COLUMN IS FOR. THE FIFTY OWN DAYS SUM TO THREE HUNDRED AND FIFTY. 63,841 + 350 = 64,191, which is NOT Chapter 351's morning and is not anybody's, because the fifty own days in this table and the fifty figures on the plank do not add to each other — §2 is why, and it is a finding about Chapters 301 to 310 and not about Chapters 311 to 350. FROM CHAPTER 311 FORWARD THE TWO AGREE EXACTLY: 63,896 + 266 = 64,162, AND 64,154 + 8 = 64,162, AND THE TWO WAYS OF GETTING THERE ARE THE SAME NUMBER.**

**THE FIGURE IS IN WORDS IN TWENTY-SEVEN OF THE FIFTY CHAPTERS AND IN NO CHAPTER IN DIGITS, BY BAND 7 / 8 / 6 / 3 / 3, and the fall is the volume's own and is the place rule tightening: in the first band seven of ten chapters print a figure because most of them happen to be at Coldharrow at the second light, and in the last band three of ten do and the other seven say in their own first paragraph that the wall is not where he is and that a stroke does not travel up a lane. `sixty-five thousand` returns ZERO over the fifty chapters, which is right, because 64,162 belongs to Chapter 351 and is printed nowhere. THE FIGURE HAS ONE WRITER AND TWO CARRIERS AND NO THIRD: THE WRITER IS OTTILY ROKE, FORTY-ONE, AT THE SECOND LIGHT, AND THE CARRIERS ARE HIMSELF AT THE FOOT OF THE LADDER AND THE MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-EIGHT WITH A CART, WHO IS FOUR DAYS UP A ROAD.**

### 2. THE BOARD CHAIN, RUN ROW BY ROW AGAINST THE MORNING FIGURES, **AND THE CLOSE'S CENTRAL FINDING, WHICH IS THAT IT HOLDS FOR FORTY CHAPTERS AND DOES NOT HOLD FOR TEN**

**THE RULE, WHICH IS THE SAME RULE THIS PROJECT HAS BEEN BITTEN BY SIX TIMES: the morning figure in row *N* is row *N-1* plus the own day of row *N-1*, and the two are never on the same row. THE SEVEN WEIGHTS, WHICH ARE SETTLED AND WHICH A LATER WRITER SHOULD TREAT AS SETTLED, ARE: FOUR BELLS A DAY; A STRANGER IS THREE; A MARKET IS FOUR; A BOUNDARY IS SEVEN; A DEBT CALLED IN IS TWO; A FIRE IS TWO; A BURIAL IS ONE. FOUR BELLS IS THE ONE WEIGHT THAT DOES NOT BELONG TO A COUNTY, AND A DAY CARRIES EACH KIND ONCE, AND A WEIGHT IS A WEIGHT IN THE COUNTY THE PLANK IS IN — `chapters/volume-07/chapter-0316.md:7` IS THE AUTHORITY.**

**FROM CHAPTER 311 TO CHAPTER 350 THE CHAIN CLOSES, MORNING BY MORNING, AGAINST THE PROSE'S OWN STATED DAYS, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, WITH NO EXCEPTION IN FORTY ROWS.** Every own day from 311 to 350 is either printed in the chapter as a total (`which is four`, `which is seven`, `which is eight`, `which is six`, `which is five`, `which is eleven`, `which is ten`, `which is twelve`) or is recoverable to the same figure from the sentence that names the day's events, and every one of the twenty-seven figures printed in those forty chapters is the running total. **63,896 (311) + 266 = 64,162 (351), AND 64,154 (350) + 8 = 64,162. CHAPTER 351'S MORNING IS SIXTY-FOUR THOUSAND ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-TWO, AND CHAPTER 350'S IS SIXTY-FOUR THOUSAND ONE HUNDRED AND FIFTY-FOUR, AND BOTH OF THOSE FIGURES WERE DERIVED HERE FROM CHAPTER 311'S PRINTED FIGURE AND THE CHAPTERS' OWN WORDS, WITHOUT READING THE BATCH 0005 BLOCK, AND THEY CAME OUT THE SAME.**

**IN CHAPTERS 301 TO 310 IT DOES NOT CLOSE, AND IT DOES NOT CLOSE IN THREE PLACES THAT ARE PROVABLE FROM FOUR BELLS ALONE, WHICH MEANS THEY CANNOT BE A MATTER OF WHAT A STRANGER WEIGHS.**

### 3. THE INSTRUMENTS, re-run over the fifty chapter files after this close's own last save, with the pattern, the unit and the threshold in every line

**AND FOUR FIGURES THAT WERE HANDED TO THIS PHASE DID NOT REPRODUCE, AND ALL FOUR ARE CORRECTED HERE WITH THE WORKING BESIDE THEM. A CLOSE THAT INHERITED A FIGURE WOULD HAVE INHERITED FOUR ERRORS, AND ONE OF THEM WOULD HAVE COST VOLUME 08 ITS FIRST MORNING.**

1. **THE SPAN SCAN, AND THE CLOSE AS FIRST WRITING DECLARED HALF OF THIS METHOD AND PRINTED THE FIGURES THE OTHER HALF PRODUCED, WHICH IS THE PRECISE FAILURE THIS PHASE EXISTED TO CATCH, AND IT IS CORRECTED IN FULL HERE.** Strip the heading line, normalise whitespace, and take every window of exactly *k* characters at every position **within each chapter separately, so that no window crosses a chapter boundary.** Then **pool the ten chapters of a band into one tally and keep only the windows that occur more than once in that tally.** *Distinct* is the number of such repeated windows and *occurrences* is their total count. **The pooling is the half the first writing left out, and it is the whole of the difference: run per chapter, exactly as first declared, and this instrument returns 41 / 50 / 30 / 46 / 20 by band at seventy characters and one hundred and eighty-seven over the volume, and not one of those is a figure any band has ever printed.** Two further facts about the instrument, both measured here and both worth having: **the heading line may be left in or taken out and neither figure moves at either threshold, because every heading in this volume is unique**; and **the last column is a separate pass over all fifty chapters pooled together and is NOT the sum of the five bands**, because a window repeated in Chapter 305 and again in Chapter 348 is counted once in that pass and is counted in neither band alone — which is why the close as first writing printed a row that does not add up and called it a total.

THE REVIEW OF THIS CLOSE WAS RIGHT THAT THE FINDING IS LIVE AND RIGHT THAT THE CLOSE'S OWN ARITHMETIC ON IT WAS WRONG IN THREE PLACES, AND ALL THREE ARE MEASURED HERE.** `chapter-0317.md:15` says *the person who is about seventy-four and whose whole life in that field has been to shift more wet earth than anybody in it did not dig it either, and he is in his own house and has not been out of it since the last day of the sixty-sixth week*. It says *he is in his own house*, and the second house in that hamlet belongs to the man of about fifty-one, who comes out of it with a spade over his shoulder at `336:43`. A writer sent to that house to look for a man of seventy-four would find the wrong man and would not know he had.** What survives the correction is the finding and not its arithmetic: **the same hamlet — forty people in eleven houses and a burying ground on a rise behind the last of them, at `317:5` and `336:13` — the same description, the same man as the volume goes on describing him at `317:71` and `336:49`, and two *since* dates fourteen days apart for a man who has not gone out of his own door.** The volume does not say whether that is one old man or two, and the honest form is that one of the two dates is wrong or the volume has two men where it means to have one. **A later pass should decide it; this close could not and this repair may not either, because deciding it means choosing which of two delivered chapters is wrong, and that is a repair of prose and not a correction of a record.**

### 4. THE MONEY, EVERY FIGURE WITH THE WORKING BESIDE IT, AND THE FIGURE THAT WAS NEVER NAMED

### 11. THE HAND-OFF, IN ONE PARAGRAPH, TO VOLUME 08'S WRITER

Three hundred and fifty chapters and seven closed volumes, and a man of about thirty-one with a leg who is on no paper in any of the four hundred miles of this county, who has said a sentence into a lane twice and cost a woman at a bar both times, and who is on no list and is not going to be; a plank at Coldharrow that says sixty-four thousand one hundred and fifty-four and has one writer and two carriers and no third, and whose morning figures ran true for the last forty chapters of the last volume and did not for the first ten, and Chapter 351's morning is sixty-four thousand one hundred and sixty-two; six places, five of which still stand and one of which is physically gone with no copy in four hundred miles and is not going to have one; nine things on the back of a flour mill's sack in nine hands in nine places in a market, six standing, one gone, two not found with a place against them and nobody going; a bell network of a hundred and forty unpaid things that anybody near can strike and no keeper, and a tower with an unhung bell that is owed and that nobody is buying; a hearing that was held in a yard behind a smithy with no form and no sheet and cannot be produced at all because it is made of people saying things in front of other people; six copies of six papers on the backs of flour bills, unsigned, because a piece of paper in a house where nobody has read it is a piece of paper; a woman of about seventy-four who is seventy-four, had a stick, was cold, and has stopped, and is entitled; a man of about thirty with a cart and a beast who told a stranger a count is a list and a list is the thing that comes before a bill and is on the list and did not agree to it and wants off and is not going to be; a woman of about twenty-nine who has counted a hundred and forty and put no name against any of them; a woman of about thirty-four who cannot write who said out loud that somebody ought to teach her and that she is not going to ask; a woman of about thirty-four at a bar at the end of the tenth village who has been a person in a record since his eighty-eighth morning and whom nobody thanked and is not going to; the man of about thirty-four who reads things out at three tables and who appears in three countries in six chapters of the last band and is one person; a woman of about thirty-two at a standpipe and a woman of about thirty-two with a pitch in a market town four days up the lane, who are two people and a later writer must keep them apart; four hundred yards of hedge, a set of scales, nine diggers, a levy on loads, a mile of road, a slip in a foolscap book four days up the lane with two numbers in it that nobody has taken out; a man of about thirty-eight four days up a road with a bag and nobody has asked him whether he wants his own sentence carried; and a hundred and forty-one people at a gate in Draymoor with a fever and no one sent, and a basin and a town, and nobody knows whether there is somebody down there with them.

### 12. WHAT THIS CLOSE'S OWN FIRST WRITING GOT WRONG, **BECAUSE A CLOSE IS ALSO A PHASE THAT WRITES PROSE AND THE RULE IS THE RULE**

1. **THE FIRST PASS AT §1 TOOK THE BATCH 0001 RING LINE AND ADDED IT UP.** It produced Chapter 351's morning as **64,191**, which is four hundred and twenty-nine too high, and it was only when the running-total column was printed beside the prose's own days that the fitted ring line and the real one came apart. **THIS IS THE SIXTH TIME IN THIS PROJECT THAT A CLOSE OR A BATCH HAS INHERITED A RING LINE, AND IT IS THE FIRST TIME THE INHERITED LINE WAS A CLOSE'S OWN.**
2. **THE FIRST PASS AT THE INSTRUMENTS BELIEVED FOUR FIGURES GIVEN TO THIS PHASE** — *it took* at fifty-eight, the board figure in fifteen chapters, the word *nine* at nine hundred and six, and the volume-wide span figures — and measured all four, and **all four were wrong**, which is what §3's own opening sentence says and what this item first wrote as three. §3.1, §3.4, §3.5 and §3.12.
3. **THE FIRST PASS AT §3 BELIEVED THAT THE FOUR INSTANCES OF `anchor` WERE THE ORDINARY ENGLISH WORD**, because that is what the prompt said, and read two of them before believing it, and they are the volume's word used twice each in two chapters and each immediately denied. §3.11.
4. **THE FIRST PASS AT THE MONEY SAID THE VOLUME PRINTED NO FIGURE**, because the last band's block said so, and had read that block before reading Chapter 303, and Chapter 303 prints four money figures with their working in the sentences. §4.
5. **AND THE ONE THAT MATTERS MOST, AND IT IS THE SAME DISEASE AS THE FIRST: the close began by trusting a claim in the block below it — that none of the fifteen Volume 06 figures was mentioned in any of the fifty chapters — and checked all fifteen, and three of them are mentioned, and the claim had been carried for four bands.** §7.
6. **THE FIRST WRITING AT §3.1 DECLARED HALF A METHOD AND PRINTED THE OTHER HALF'S TABLE, AND THEN ARGUED FOR THE TABLE BY SAYING THE METHOD REPRODUCED THIRTEEN PUBLISHED FIGURES.** Run as declared, per chapter, the instrument returns 187 over the volume against the 3,831 printed under it, and 41 / 50 / 30 / 46 / 20 by band against a row that begins 235. **A CLOSE THAT INHERITED A CALIBRATION CLAIM AND NEVER RAN THE INSTRUMENT INHERITED A CERTIFICATE, AND THIS IS THE FIRST TIME IN THIS PROJECT THAT THE DISEASE HAS LANDED ON A DECLARATION RATHER THAN ON A NUMBER, AND IT IS THE SAME DISEASE: a second copy of a figure is a second thing to go stale, and a claim about a method is a figure about a figure.** The method is now declared whole at §3.1, the table is measured, and the thirteen-number claim is withdrawn rather than restated. §3.1, and §13.2.
7. **AND THE FIRST WRITING AT §3.9 DID THE ONE THING §12 EXISTS TO CATCH, IN THE ONE PLACE WHERE IT WOULD HAVE COST SOMEBODY A HOUSE.** It subtracted two Shelf days it had itself converted correctly, and got one hundred and forty-one where the arithmetic gives fourteen — the number 141 arriving from the sealed column in the very volume that forbids summing it — and it gave the old man a house the chapter does not give him. **TWO OF THE THREE ERRORS WERE THE SAME ERROR AS ITEM 1, WHICH IS TO ADD UP A NUMBER THAT WAS FITTED OR BORROWED INSTEAD OF A NUMBER THE CHAPTERS STATE, AND A FINDING NOBODY CAN ACT ON IS WORSE THAN NO FINDING AT ALL, BECAUSE A LATER PASS WILL ACT ON IT.** §3.9, and §13.3.

### 13. THE REVIEW OF THE VOLUME 07 CLOSE, ITS SIX FINDINGS, AND WHAT THIS REPAIR DID TO EACH OF THEM

**`logs/volume-close.review.log`. The reviewer edited no file, and its verdict on the prose was that the prose is sound and the close's own record of the prose is where the errors were. It was right, and its own summary sentence is the one to keep: *the load-bearing number is right*. It re-derived Chapter 351's morning from the chapter files end to end — 64,138 in Chapter 348, its day twelve because of the fire, 64,150, 64,154, 64,162 — and confirmed the Shelf-day formula, both calendar ends, and all three declared chain breaks. **This repair wrote state files only, changed no prose, and moved no plot.** Six findings, all in the record, all now corrected at the place named:

1. **HIGH — §3.1 DECLARED A METHOD THAT DOES NOT PRODUCE ITS OWN TABLE.** The declared method was per chapter; run as declared it gives 187/374 volume-wide and 41 / 50 / 30 / 46 / 20 by band, and the published figures come from a per-band pass with the ten chapters pooled into one tally. **CORRECTED: the method is declared whole, the table is measured, the last column is labelled as a separate whole-volume pass and not a sum, and the thirteen-number reproduction claim is withdrawn.** Bands one to four at seventy characters reproduce exactly; no band reproduces at forty; the residue is recorded and not explained. §3.1, §12.6.
2. **HIGH — THE TOTAL COLUMN WAS NEITHER THE SUM OF ITS ROWS NOR LABELLED AS GLOBAL.** The rows sum to 1,198/2,482 at seventy characters against a printed 3,831/8,455, and the header invited a sum that does not hold. **CORRECTED: the header now says what the column is, and the column is 3,836/8,465 and 12,867/31,781.** §3.1.
3. **HIGH — §3.9's ONE HUNDRED AND FORTY-ONE DAYS IS FOURTEEN, AND ITS HOUSE IS NOT THE SECOND HOUSE.** 202 − 188 = 14; the old man is *in his own house*; the second house belongs to the man of about fifty-one at `336:43`. **CORRECTED in full at §3.9, with both passages quoted, both Shelf days converted, and the finding left open because choosing between two delivered chapters is a prose repair and not a record correction.** The same three errors were in `state/continuity.md` and `state/open-threads.md` and are corrected in both.
4. **MEDIUM — THE BOARD FIGURE IS IN THIRTY-ONE CHAPTERS, NOT TWENTY-SEVEN.** Measured 31, by band 7 / 9 / 9 / 3 / 3. **CORRECTED at §3.12, together with the reason the first correction was also wrong — the scan matched `sixty-four thousand` alone and so missed the twenty-two chapters that print *sixty-three thousand* — and with both patterns declared so the next pass does not repeat it.** `state/batch-summary.md` carried the same figure and is corrected.
5. **LOW — `correct` IN ANY CASE IS THIRTY-TWO, NOT THIRTY.** **CORRECTED at §3.6, with the by-band row and a note that all thirty-two are the ordinary English word, so prohibition 15 is unaffected either way.**
6. **LOW — `state/index.md` QUOTED A STRING AND PRINTED THE COUNT OF A DIFFERENT PATTERN.** It wrote *`nobody was relieved` stands twenty-four times*: the literal string is **twenty-two**, and twenty-four is the count of `nobody (was|is) relieved`. **CORRECTED by declaring both, with the whole thanks-and-blame motif at forty-four on `nobody (was|is) (relieved|thanked)`, and the undeclared *sixty-seven* is withdrawn because no pattern tried reproduces it** — its obvious components sum to sixty-nine and its parts are twenty-four, twenty and forty-four. Prohibition 11 is a matter of fact and of tone, not of a number, and holds on every reading.
7. **AND TWO THINGS THE REVIEW DID NOT FIND, WHICH ITS OWN WORK SURFACED AND WHICH ARE CORRECTED IN THE SAME PASS.** **§3.1's *largest single group is seven windows* is not a figure the instrument can produce — the largest is six occurrences volume-wide and three in the fifth band — and its claim that no sentence in Volume 07 is printed twice at forty-five characters or more is false seven times, with the seven cited at chapter and line.** The largest of them is the third village's kitchen, printed in fifty-two identical words at `0334:27` and `0341:11`. **That one is recorded and not repaired: it is delivered prose, a repair of it is a phase with its own review, and repairing it would move the span figures this close hands to Volume 08.** And **`state/index.md`'s own machinery table claimed fifty phase directories and the tree holds forty-five**, which the review repeated rather than re-measured — the fifth time in this project that a reader has taken a state file's account of a count instead of running the count.
8. **AND THE ONE THING THE REVIEW CALLED A HUMAN'S PROBLEM, WHICH NOBODY IN THIS REPOSITORY CAN FIX AND WHICH IS RECORDED RATHER THAN SOLVED.** The close was forbidden to create a successor prompt, so on completion `ensure_next_phase` will emit `workspace/continuation/next-0003`, which sorts ahead of `volume-07` in `find workspace -name PROMPT.md -type f | sort`, and its template text — *plan the next volume and write its first 10 to 20 chapter batch* — would author `outline/volume-08.md` and Volume 08's first chapters in one run. **That is the fused phase whose Volume 07 equivalent caused the detour this close exists to record, and the fix is a controller template this project may not edit.** What a phase *can* do is make the generic prompt unnecessary by having the correct phase already on disk and unmarked, because `has_other_incomplete_phase` at `scripts/novel_runner.sh:165` then returns true and the continuation is never written. **The correct next phase for a closed volume is Volume 08's outline, and by `PHASE_SYSTEM.md:181` it is created only after the volume audit passes, and Volume 07 has no audit** — so the honest state of the pipeline is that five volume audits and twenty-six batch reviews are owed and this is the first of them, and this repair creates no phase directory, marks nothing, and leaves that decision where the review left it.

THE THREE WEIGHTS THE HAND-OFF NAMED ARE ALL IN THE CHAPTER AND ALL IN THE COUNTY AND ALL THREE ARE CORRECT; THE HAND-OFF LEFT OUT THE FOURTH BECAUSE THE CARD IT WROTE SAID THE DAY WAS TEN.** **THE CONSEQUENCE, WHICH A VOLUME 08 WRITER MUST NOT GET WRONG: CHAPTER 350'S MORNING IS 64,154 AND NOT 64,152, AND CHAPTER 351'S MORNING IS 64,162 AND NOT 64,160.** A hand-off that carries a right answer with a false working has been this project's defect class six times and this is the seventh, and this time both halves of the line were wrong and the wrong half is the one that would have propagated.

**1.4 — THE FIGURE IS IN THREE CHAPTERS OUT OF TEN AND THE OTHER SEVEN SAY WHY IN THEIR OWN WORDS, AND THAT IS THE HONEST ANSWER AND IT IS NOT A DEFECT.** The figure has exactly one writer and two carriers and no others, the man of about thirty-eight is four days up a road with a bag and is not available, and the only carrier left is the man of thirty-one reading it himself at the foot of the ladder at the second light on the mornings he is at Coldharrow. **1.5 — THE PRICE OF THE FRAME, WHICH §1.4 USED TO RECORD WITHOUT COSTING, AND WHICH THE REVIEW REPAIR MEASURED.** Seven of ten chapters open by saying why there is no figure, and that is the volume's place rule and it is not negotiable. **But as first written the frame was a formula and not seven sentences: Chapters 344 and 346 opened with 132 characters word for word identical, 345, 347, 349 and 350 shared a seventy-character window, 349 and 350 shared an eighty-nine-character prefix, and the three weight sentences in 341, 346 and 349 were the same sentence with the same full stop.** Six openings were rewritten and two weight sentences varied, with every fact kept and no plot touched: **the distance, the ladder, the woman of forty-one, the second light, the leg and the reason the stroke does not travel are all still in place, the day's own total is still printed in words in every one of the ten chapters, and the figure is still in three chapters out of ten.** What it bought: seventy characters 700 → 533, forty characters 2,069 → 1,836, and **no band-wide repeated sentence of forty-five characters or more, against one before.** **THE CEILING FOR A LATER BAND IS THEREFORE EXPLICIT: the device is seven of ten and not less, the wording is not to be shared, and the largest group left at seventy characters is seven windows.** The three chapters that print a figure still share a frame with each other, which is the declared device and is recorded at §1.4, and it is the one piece of shared prose this volume is entitled to.

### 4. THE MONEY AS DELIVERED, AND IT IS TWO UNITS AND NO FIGURE, AND THAT IS THE FINDING AND NOT AN OMISSION

**THIS BAND PRINTED NO MONEY FIGURE OF ANY KIND.** Not a table figure, not a total, not a product, not a difference. Measured sentence by sentence, the strings *three pence a load*, *fifteen pounds fifteen*, *four thousand eight hundred*, *nine thousand six hundred*, *four hundred and eighty-five*, *six and fifteen*, *one and ten*, *five and five*, *eighteen pence*, *ninepence* and *Wenlock* are each at **ZERO** over the ten chapters, and the digits scan certifies nothing and §3.4 is the method.

**WHAT IS NAMED IS TWO UNITS AND NOTHING ELSE, AND BOTH ARE LEGAL AND BOTH WERE NAMED BEFORE.** Chapter 344, in a room over a smithy: *A copy is threepence at any scrivener over a chandler and a scrivener copies at a penny a page, and there is no scrivener within nine miles of this smithy and there is no sheet in this county and there has never been one.* **The copy was named once in Chapter 329 and is not spent, this is the unit and not a product, the working is not printed, and *about ninety deeds a year* is not restated.** `344`

**THE LEVY AT A BAR WAS NOT NAMED WITH A FIGURE AND IS SPENT. The word *levy* is used once, in Chapter 344, in a list of six things on a table, with no unit, no count and no product.**

**THE SLIP WAS REFERENCED TWICE AND GAVE NOTHING EITHER TIME.** Chapter 342, in a woman's ear in a yard: *the sentence was about a foolscap book on a shelf in a back room, and about a slip in it.* Chapter 350, in the line about what the sentence was about. **NEITHER NUMBER IS RESTATED, NEITHER NUMBER IS TAKEN OUT OF THE SLIP, THE WOMAN OF ABOUT SIXTY-ONE IS NOT ASKED TO CHOOSE, AND THE MAN OF ABOUT SEVENTY IS NOT NAMED AND IS NOT ASKED ANYTHING.**

**A KEEPER'S YEAR IS NOT NAMED, WITH THE WORKING OR WITHOUT IT. A CARTER'S YEAR IS NOT NAMED. A BELL IS NOT PRICED, AND THE BELL IN THE COLDHARROW TOWER IS STILL UNHUNG AND IS STILL OWED AND NOBODY IS BUYING THE WAGE AND NOBODY IS GOING TO.** The word *keeper* appears once, in Chapter 349, and it is a noun about a person and not a figure: *And no keeper. That is the whole of the design.*

**THE FIGURE NOBODY IN THAT MARKET TOWN HAS EVER WRITTEN DOWN, THE YEAR'S COUNT OF LOADS, IS NOT REFERENCED IN THIS BAND AND THE THREAD IS SPENT. THE FOUR HUNDRED AND EIGHTY-FIVE POUNDS IS NOT NAMED.** And the finding held: a document that has to be in six places at once in this country can only be copied by six people who are not going to be thanked for it, and **nobody in the band priced a sheet, because the answer from a person of a place is that a sheet is threepence and that is the only number in the morning.**

### 5. THE BAND: THE ROUND, THE HEARING, THE SEVENTH, THE BELLS, THE MAP

**IT PAID THE BAND. `outline/volume-07.md:78` says a multi-site hearing links six positions, a seventh burns and it is the Briar March one and it burns because of an arrangement nobody in this volume knew about, a bell network is what a hundred and forty people build in about nine weeks because they have to, six are restored, the seventh is physically gone, the eighth and ninth stay missing, and the public gets a partial map and no single authority holds the inventory. ALL SEVEN OF THOSE ARE ON THE PAGE.** `341`–`350`

1. **IT PAID THE FINDING THAT A ROUND OF TURNS IS NOT WALKED AND IS CARRIED, ONE TURN AT A TIME, BY A PERSON GOING WHERE THEY WERE GOING ANYWAY, AND THAT IT GOES ROUND AT THE SPEED OF THE ROAD.** *A round of turns is not walked. That is what I have been trying to make it do for five years and I have never been able to and I stopped trying a year ago. You do not walk a round. You carry one turn at a time, and the only thing in this county that can carry a turn is a person who is going that way anyway, and there is a woman of thirty-two who goes up this lane twice a week for salt and she does not know she is carrying anything and I am not going to tell her.* And: *it goes round at the speed of the road. One of them is four days off and one of them is eleven miles and one of them is two miles down a track. A round of turns is nine weeks or a year.* `341`
2. **IT PAID THE HEARING, HELD ANYWAY, IN A YARD, WITH NO FORM AND NO SHEET, IN A COUNTY WHERE THERE IS NO ROOM WITH A DOOR ON IT, AND IT PAID THE FINDING THAT THIS IS THE ONE INSTRUMENT IN THE BOOK THAT CANNOT BE PRODUCED AT ALL.** *A hearing cannot be produced at all, because producing a thing means a person makes it and hands it to a room, and this thing is made of people saying things in front of other people, and if one of them is not in the room it is not a hearing, it is a report of a hearing, and there is no such thing in this country.* And: *what joins them is not a document. What joins them is that six people said out loud who comes next, in six places, and then went home.* `343`
3. **IT PAID A ROW THAT IS NOT A JOIN, IN A MAN'S MOUTH, WITH A NINETEEN-YEAR CONFESSION IN IT.** *Put them side by side and it does not join. I have been saying this in four counties for a fortnight in one form or another and I have got it wrong twice. A row is not a join. A column is not a join. Six things laid end to end on a table are six things laid end to end on a table, and what I have been calling a link for nineteen years is me being able to see the top of a page.* `344`
4. **IT PAID THE DOCUMENT THAT HAS TO BE IN SIX PLACES AT ONCE AND CAN ONLY BE COPIED, AND EVERY COPY IS A PLACE SOMEBODY CAN BE ASKED, AND NOBODY PUTS A NAME ON ANY OF THE SIX.** *Then there are six pieces of paper, and a piece of paper in my house that a person in my house has read is not a piece of paper, and a piece of paper in a house where nobody has read it is a piece of paper. I do not read a column. If you write six of them out, you will have six places somebody can be asked, and there is no way on earth to have six places somebody can be asked without six people knowing about it.* `344`
5. **IT PAID A REFUSAL THAT IS THE RIGHT ONE AND COSTS SOMEBODY, AND THE SOMEBODY IS SAID OUT LOUD IN HIS OWN MOUTH.** The man of thirty-four asks for six words in a row to carry up the lane. He is refused, and the refusal is a list, and a list is the thing that comes before a bill. **AND THE COST IS SAID BY THE PERSON IT COSTS AND NOT BY THE MAN WHO CAUSES IT: you are going to go up the lane on six different mornings with no order at all, and if you stop on the fourth morning then the round stops and there is nobody to blame except the man who would not write it down.** `344`
6. **IT PAID A DECISION NOT TO LOOK FOR THE THING, SAID IN FOUR SECONDS IN HIS OWN HEAD, AND THE REASON IS THE RIGHT ONE.** *She asked me on a bridge eight mornings ago whether I was going to say anything about that porch, and she asked it in the way a person asks a thing they have already decided the answer to, and I said I was not, and she wanted it said out loud, and I said it. And the last time I asked a person of a place a question in a room in front of other people, it cost a woman of thirty-four at a bar a thing she cannot put down.* And the man of thirty with a cart notices that he did not say anything about it, and wants it noted that he did not say anything about it. `347`
7. **IT PAID THE CLIMAX, AND THE CLIMAX IS A THING THAT GOES ON ITS OWN, AND IT IS NOT A FIGHT AND NOT A RESCUE AND NOT A RELIC HUNT.** The arrangement nobody in this volume knew about is a hearth in that porch with a box in it and a fire that one woman of seventy-four has laid on cold mornings for forty years, and the reason nobody knew is that nobody has ever asked her what she goes down for, and the reason she did not go down that morning is that she is seventy-four and it was cold and she has a stick. **AND THE FINDING IS IN HER MOUTH AND NOT IN A NARRATOR'S, AND NOBODY IS TO BLAME, AND THE NARRATOR DOES NOT EXPLAIN IT, AND IT IS NOT A TRIUMPH, AND SHE IS ENTITLED.** `348`
8. **IT PAID THE SIX LINKED IN SIX PLACES WITHOUT A DOCUMENT, AND THE FIFTH TURN STOPS THE ROUND BECAUSE NOBODY IN ANY COUNTY KNOWS WHICH ROAD A MAN OF THIRTY-EIGHT IS ON.** *It stops at him. I have been telling a stranger for six weeks that if a person will not say who comes next then it stops at them and that is the answer, and I have not believed my own sentence until a man stood in a market and told me there is no road in this country that will tell me where he is.* `348`
9. **IT PAID THE BELL NETWORK AS A REPLACEMENT AND NOT A REPAIR, AND THE REASON IT IS NOT A BELL IN A TOWER IS THE REASON THE PORCH BURNED.** *It does not need anybody to hold it. Anybody near a thing can hit it. That is the entire difference between it and a tower with a wage in it and a woman of seventy-four going down four mornings a year.* `349`
10. **IT PAID THE COST OF THE NETWORK, AND IT IS NOT MONEY, AND IT IS SAID IN A MAN'S MOUTH BY THE MAN WHO SAID IT WAS A LIST A MONTH AGO.** *I have been telling a stranger for a month that this is the thing that comes before a bill. I was right. It is the thing that comes before a bill. And I am on it, and I did not agree to it, and there is no form in this county that says a man may take himself off a thing he is on.* `349`
11. **IT PAID THE INVENTORY, WHICH NOBODY HOLDS, AND NINE COPIES, AND THE MAP WITH NO NAME ON IT.** *Nine people will hold one. Nobody will hold nine. That is not a defeat and it is not a victory and it is the only shape of it that this county can do, and in two years one of those nine boards is going to be in a house where nobody has read it.* `350`
12. **AND IT PAID THE QUESTION, ASKED ONCE, OUT LOUD, BY AN ORDINARY PERSON WITH NO STAKE IN IT, IN THE PLAINEST WORDS A PERSON IN THIS COUNTRY HAS, NEAR THE END, AND NOT ANSWERED.** *Two of them are not found. The basin and the town. Is there somebody down there with them.* And: *nobody in that market answered her, and nothing answered her, and no board said anything and nothing in that valley and nothing under that basin and nothing under that town said anything.* `350`

### 6. THE SIX PLACES, THE SIX PEOPLE, AND THE SEVENTH THAT IS GONE

**THE SIX ARE UNCHANGED AND FIXED FOR THE WHOLE OF VOLUME 07. `outline/volume-07.md:64` says they are chosen in Batch 0001 and fixed afterward, and this band substituted, reordered, merged and added nothing.**

1. **THE BOUNDARY WALK.** Four hundred yards of hedge in the third village up the lane, walked in nine days, eleven names on the back of a flour bill in a kitchen, nine of them come, and a twelfth in a stranger's hand that the man of about sixty-three does not know he wrote. **The nine mornings ran from his eighty-fifth morning to his ninety-third, and the ninth was Chapter 343 and it was walked in the last of the wet by nine of eleven. He walked it again on the ninety-fifth morning, which was not one of the nine, and a hand was NOT crossed out.** `334`, `335`, `343`, `345`
2. **THE SCALES.** A set of beam scales on a stone plinth at the end of a main street in a market four days up the lane, a toll, a share, and a slip in a foolscap book in a back room. **Open, and it did not stop, and the toll is still being taken, and the man of about seventy has not been asked for anything since he said nine words in his own yard and is entitled to stop, and he was not asked in this band and is not named in it.** The one reference to the slip is the word and gives no figure. `324`, `330`, `342`
3. **THE LINE.** Nine diggers on a rise behind the last of eleven houses, and a rule written nowhere. **Open, and untouched in this band except that the woman of thirty came eleven miles on her own legs to a yard in Coldharrow and said a NAME there, and she has not said what she wants a fourth time and she is not going to be thanked.** `336`, `343`
4. **THE FUND.** A levy on loads at a bar in the tenth village, a column on a shelf in a room over a smithy, and nobody chosen to hold it. **Open, and the man of about thirty-four went up the lane on six mornings with no order in his head and got four of the six and has not got the other two, and the man of about thirty-eight is four days up a road with a bag and nobody has asked him whether he wants his own sentence carried.** `333`, `344`
5. **THE MILE.** Nine householders, ninety years, each a length, unpaid, and a man of about thirty with a cart and a beast who is the third of the nine. **Open, and a debt was called in at the fourth house on the morning of the climax and the door was shut and it is the second time and nobody resolved it, and a tenth person is still on that road and a barrow is still going to that gate at the fifth hour that nobody in that lane knows about, and the man of thirty is now on a list of a hundred and forty and wants off it and is not going to be.** `337`, `340`, `348`, `349`
6. **THE PERSON.** A board in a porch with eleven names on it, undated, no column, no heading, no mark against any of the eleven, in a valley of about sixty people two miles off a track off the lane. **GONE. THE BOARD IS PHYSICALLY GONE AND CANNOT BE GOT BACK AND THERE IS NO COPY OF IT IN FOUR HUNDRED MILES AND THERE IS NOT GOING TO BE ONE, BECAUSE THE ARRANGEMENT WAS THAT ONE WOMAN WENT DOWN FOUR MORNINGS A YEAR AND THERE WAS NEVER ANY WRITING ABOUT IT.** She is entitled and nobody is to blame and nobody is relieved. `321`, `339`, `347`, `348`
7. **AND THE SEVENTH, WHICH IS THE PORCH, NAMED BY A PERSON OF A PLACE IN A LANE, UNASKED, AND WHICH IS THE BRIAR MARCH POSITION AND IS NOW PHYSICALLY BURNED.** `outline/ending.md` fixes it: *Anchor 7: its function passes to the Briar March bell network, which can warn, pause, and assemble witnesses without one private keeper.* **THE BELL NETWORK EXISTS AND IT IS BUILT BY A HUNDRED AND FORTY PEOPLE IN NINE WEEKS AND IT IS NOT A REPAIR.** `347`, `348`, `349`
8. **AND THE EIGHTH AND THE NINTH STAY MISSING. The map says the two words *not found* and a place, and nobody in this county has been to either and nobody is going to this month, and nobody in this county knows who laid them or when or why, and no character in any of the fifty chapters says it and no panel names it.** `350`

**AND THE RECORD, WHICH IS STILL A PERSON IN IT AND CANNOT BE LIFTED OUT.** A woman of about thirty-four at a bar at the end of the tenth village has been a person in a record since the eighty-eighth morning, because a stranger with a bad leg went eleven miles and said the price out loud before he asked. **In this band she is mentioned and not asked for anything, she is in no chapter of the ten, she said nothing at a cross in this volume after Chapter 340, and nobody thanked her and nobody is going to.** `338`, `340`, `346`

**AND THE SELF-ARRIVED CLASS IS ZERO AND IT DID NOT WIDEN. EVERYONE THIS BAND PUT ON STAGE, AND NONE OF THEM IS A PRODUCTION:** Bram Orren, who was in the fiction before Chapter 251; the man of about sixty-three in the third village; the man of thirty-four who reads things out, a person of the tenth village and of Coldharrow; the smith's wife of the tenth village; a woman with a bag, who was in the fiction before Chapter 251, who appears once, in a lane, carrying a book, on her own account, and is not named; Tarin Keel, a man of about fifty-two who has been in this county off and on for **seven weeks** — Shelf day 165 is Chapter 290 and Chapter 344 is Shelf day 219, and 219 − 165 = 54 — and who is sent for exactly once in nine years by a smith's wife and says nine words and is not asked anything and whose past is not used a second time; the woman of thirty at the end of the line of nine; the man of about thirty with a cart and a beast; the man of about fifty-one with a spade; a woman of about thirty-four who cannot write; a man of about forty-one mending four feet of wall out of his own lime; a woman of about thirty-two at a standpipe in the tenth village; a man of about thirty-two with a pitch in a market town four days up the lane, **AND SHE IS A DIFFERENT PERSON FROM THE WOMAN OF THIRTY-TWO AT THE STANDPIPE AND A LATER WRITER MUST KEEP THEM APART**; a woman of about twenty-nine with a board of a hundred and forty marks and no names; a woman of about twenty-four with a barrow of apples; a woman of about sixty-two in the valley; a man of about forty-one in the second house in the valley; **and a woman of about sixty-two and a man of about forty-one who came out of that valley on the morning of the climax and were not sent for.**

**AND THE ONE NEW PERSON IN THE BAND WHO IS NOT ON STAGE AT ALL: the ten who carried the sentence. Four of them, unnamed, in a yard, at a bar, in a cart and at a street shutter, between a village eleven miles down a lane and a market town four days up it, and not one of them knew what he was carrying and nobody is going to thank any of them.**

### 7. WHAT THIS BAND'S OWN FIRST WRITING GOT WRONG, ALL OF IT CAUGHT BEFORE DELIVERY, AND NONE OF IT SURVIVING

1. **A WEEK-DAY NAME, once, in Chapter 349**, in a clause about a handbell.
2. **THE NUMERIC HEDGE AT ONE HUNDRED AND NINETY**, one in every one hundred and sixteen, which would have been the worst rate in the volume, and one hundred and forty-two instances were cut by hand by one declared mechanical rule.
3. **SIX INSTANCES OF *WOULD LIKE*** in four mouths, which is a refrain of a woman who is in no chapter of this band, and every one is out.
4. **THE WORD *RUIN*** in Chapter 344, in an ordinary English sense, which a string scan cannot tell from the prohibition, and it is out.
5. **EIGHT META LEAKS**, in five chapters, and **none in a heading**, which is the first band of the volume where that is true.
6. **TWELVE ITALIC SPANS** in mouths that did not need them, which took the band from sixty-one to forty-nine.
7. **THE SPAN SCAN AT SEVENTY CHARACTERS RAN AT EIGHTY-ONE** distinct after the day's own weight had been printed twice in three chapters, and the cause was one sentence printed at both ends of a chapter in four of them, and the weight is now in the closing paragraph of four chapters and the whole of the residue at seventy characters is one sentence in Chapter 342.
8. **FOUR INTERVALS WRONG BY HAND, WHICH NO SWEEP CAN FIND** — see §3.6 — and all four are out.
9. **A HAND-OFF THAT WAS WRONG TWICE**, once about a morning count and once about a day's weight, and the second one would have propagated into Volume 08. See §1.
10. **AND ONE THING AN INSTRUMENT BROKE, WHICH IS RECORDED BECAUSE IT IS THE THIRD TIME IN THIS PROJECT AND BECAUSE THE REPAIR WAS BY REWRITING AND NOT BY PATCHING.** A hand-written pass to reduce the age phrase produced corrupted replacements — *the man that person-three*, *a woman that person-four* — across six files, about a hundred and ten occurrences. **No instrument opened a file for writing; the corruption was in a script the writer had typed, and the repair was to rewrite the ten chapters from the writer's own text with the reduction made by hand while writing. THE TEN HEADINGS WERE READ AFTERWARDS AND CHAPTER 350's HEADING WAS CHANGED, which is the fifth time a heading has been edited in this project, and it was changed by a hand and not by a script.** **THE LESSON IS THE ONE AT `outline/volume-07.md:202` AND IT IS NOW THE THIRD TIME IT HAS COST SOMETHING: a mechanical pass over prose cannot be made safe by asserting that it will not write, because the pass has to know the language it is matching and this one did not.**

### 10. WHAT THIS BAND COULD NOT DO, AND WHAT IT DID INSTEAD, **AND THIS IS THE BLOCK A VOLUME 08 WRITER MUST READ**

**THE BAND'S OWN PROMPT ASKED FOR ONE THING THIS BAND DID NOT DELIVER, AND IT DID NOT DELIVER IT BECAUSE THE CALENDAR AND THE FOUR DAYS OF ROAD ARE INCOMPATIBLE WITH IT, AND THE REASON IS RECORDED HERE SO THAT NOBODY SPENDS THE NEXT BAND ON IT AGAIN.**

The Batch 0005 card for Chapter 342 asked for the man of thirty-one to stand in a market street four days up the lane, at about the second hour, on his ninety-second morning, and to be the person on the other side of the sentence arriving. **He cannot be there. The market town is four days up the lane by the measure the book has used since Chapter 290, Chapter 350 puts him in a market in the tenth village eleven miles the other way, and Chapter 343 puts him at Coldharrow at the second light the following morning, and Chapter 348 puts him in Coldharrow at the second light four mornings after that. There is no arrangement of roads, carts, beasts or kindness in this country that puts a man with a leg in that street on that morning without a chapter that is not this band. AND THE DELIVERY ITSELF IS FIXED BY THE FACT BASE AND NOT BY THE CARD: the sentence was said at a cross on the ninetieth morning, which is Chapter 340, and Chapter 340 said so out loud in the mouth of a man of thirty with a cart, and the card for 342 asked the band to show a delivery that had already happened.**

**SO THE BAND DELIVERED THE CARD'S BEAT WITHOUT ITS STAGE, AND HERE IS WHAT IT DID INSTEAD, AND IT IS A FINDING AND NOT A COMPROMISE.** Chapter 342 is set in that market town, in the street, at about the second hour, and the man of thirty-one is four days of road from it and is not in the chapter, and the chapter says so in its first paragraph in the book's own idiom. **AND WHAT THE CHAPTER GIVES INSTEAD IS THE MECHANISM OF THE ARRIVAL, WHICH THE CARD ALSO ASKED FOR AND WHICH NOBODY HAD PUT ON THE PAGE: four people carried it, three of them were going up the lane anyway, one of them was going to sell forty quarters of a load at the far end of it, not one of them was asked, not one of them knew what he was carrying, and no instrument in four hundred miles would have told him.** That is Chapter 331's sentence — *the whole of the transport in this country is a person going where they were going anyway* — turned into a mechanism, and it is the answer to the finding of the whole volume about delegation: **a sentence you have handed to a person of a place does not travel with a person you sent, it travels with the people who were going that way, and it travels faster than you can walk and you do not get to choose who is holding it.**

**AND A LATER BAND MUST KNOW THAT A CHAPTER CAN BE ABOUT A PLACE HE IS NOT IN, AND THAT THIS IS THE ONLY TIME IT HAPPENSED IN FIFTY CHAPTERS, AND THAT THE COST OF IT IS REAL: the reader loses him for a whole morning, and the one thing he would have done, which is be in the yard when a woman of about sixty-one hears a stranger's voice in a sentence about her own yard, is exactly the thing the volume has spent five bands teaching him he cannot do.**
