The dispatcher takes the first in `sort` order, so the controller would have marked this batch done and then run the Volume 08 plan-and-write prompt — **and `workspace/volume-07/volume-close/` would have sat behind it, unmarked, until something marked it, and the volume-close record for Volume 07 would have been written after Volume 08's first ten chapters were already on disk.** That is the exact failure `state/index.md` machinery item 1 records having already happened once, when `workspace/volume-06/plan-0001/` was named in a state file for six phases and had never existed, except that this time the file existed and was the wrong job. **A volume-close prompt must sort before any prompt for the volume it closes, and `volume-07/volume-close` does, because `b` sorts before `v` and `volume-07` sorts before `volume-08`.**

WHAT IS LEFT, AND IS NOT TO BE REWORDED, is a declared set: the day's own weight in words in every chapter and in the closing paragraph of four of them, which is the ceiling this project set at `state/batch-summary.md:86` and which the delivered band had broken at nine in ten;** the figure-reading frame; the *there is no form in this country that says a man may* motif in six new variants; the sentence about a man who would have had to be standing at the foot of a ladder at the second light; and the four hundred yards of hedge, which is a thing with four hundred yards in it and is stated in six chapters and is canon.

THE WHOLE OF WHAT IS LEFT IS THAT, AND THE FIGURES THAT WERE CUT WERE HOURS AND MINUTES AND YEARS AND COUNTS OF PEOPLE, WHICH IN THIS BOOK ARE THINGS A PERSON MADE AND CAN BE ASKED ABOUT.** **THE TARGET OF UNDER ONE HUNDRED AND TWENTY-FIVE IS MET AND THE BAND IS BETTER THAN THE THREE BEFORE IT AND IT IS NOT CLEAN AND MUST NOT BE REPORTED CLEAN: Batch 0001 was two hundred and six in twenty-two thousand seven hundred and seventy-six words, one in every one hundred and ten; Batch 0002 was eighty-eight, one in every two hundred and fifty-three; Batch 0003 was one hundred and eighteen in twenty-two thousand four hundred and fifty-nine words, one in every one hundred and ninety, and the rate of the case-insensitive count and the rate of the case-sensitive count were different and both were printed; this band is ninety-two, one in every two hundred and thirty-nine.** **AND THE CONSEQUENCE, WHICH A LATER BAND SHOULD BE TOLD: the prose is now tighter and the ages are now exact where they were not, and the cost of the cut was that this county's towns, lanes and kitchen tables are described in flat counts instead of hedged ones, and a reviewer who thinks that has cost the book its texture should say so, because it is the one thing in the reduction that was not obviously a gain.**

### 4. THE MONEY AS DELIVERED, AND IT IS NOTHING, AND THAT IS THE FINDING AND NOT AN OMISSION

**THIS BAND PRINTED NO MONEY FIGURE OF ANY KIND.** Not a table figure, not a unit, not a product, and not a difference. Measured sentence by sentence: the strings *three pence a load*, *fifteen pounds fifteen*, *four thousand eight hundred*, *nine thousand six hundred*, *four hundred and eighty-five*, *threepence*, *six and fifteen*, *one and ten*, *five and five*, *eighteen pence*, *ninepence* and *Wenlock* are each at **ZERO** over the ten chapters.

**AND THAT IS THE BAND'S MONEY, AND IT IS SPENT NOW, AND IT MAY NOT BE SPENT AGAIN IN BATCH 0005.** What this band needed a price for was a levy, a sheet, a boundary, a load and a wage, and it went and asked a person of a place about all five, and the answer in every case was that there is no price on it in this country. The man of thirty-four who reads things out for a living says in Chapter 333 that there is no sheet in the county and no scrivener within nine miles of a smithy. The woman of about thirty-four at a bar says in Chapter 338 that there is nothing in the county that lets a person refuse a thing that costs nothing, which is the only free thing in this band and the price of it is that she cannot say no. **THE FIGURE THE B3 REPAIR LEFT OPEN — NOBODY IN THAT MARKET TOWN HAS EVER WRITTEN DOWN THE NUMBER OF LOADS IN A YEAR, AND THE HONEST VERSION OF THE ARRANGEMENT BEGINS WITH A MAN WRITING A YEAR ON A SLIP — WAS HAD AND REFUSED IN CHAPTER 340, AND IT WAS HAD FROM A PERSON OF THAT PLACE, STANDING NEXT TO HIS OWN BAG, AT A CROSS, IN A LANE, AND IT IS THE ONE PERMITTED REFERENCE TO THE SLIP IN THIS BAND AND IT IS SPENT.** He says there is a number on a slip on a shelf in a back room four days up this lane, that it is not written down anywhere in that county and it is in no hand in it, that somebody has to write down a year of loads, that it is about a week of a clerk's work, and that there is no clerk in that county and nobody there has anybody to do it. **He gives neither figure and nobody asked him to. A BATCH 0005 CARD MAY NOT REPEAT THAT REFERENCE AND MAY NOT NAME EITHER SLIP FIGURE.**

### 5. THE BAND: THE DELEGATION, THE MAN OF FIFTY-TWO, AND THE BOY OF SEVENTEEN

**IT PAID THE BAND'S THREE THINGS, AND ALL THREE ARE ON THE PAGE, AND `outline/volume-07.md:76` IS THE AUTHORITY THAT THEY ARE THE THREE.**

1. **HE TRIES TO CARRY ONE OF THE SIX HIMSELF AND CANNOT, AND THE REASON IS NOT A LEG AND NOT A DISTANCE.** Chapter 334, in a kitchen, in front of nine people, and it is the only time in thirteen days he tried anything in a room. **A boundary is four hundred yards of hedge walked in nine days by eleven names of whom nine come, and there is nothing on it that is a fact except the hedge and the nine days and the coming, and a man who carries it is a man who has to be there on nine mornings, and the ninth morning is the fifth day of the walk and he is going to be standing at a bridge with one rail on it.** And Chapter 336, on a dry morning on a rise behind eleven houses, in the open: **he stands at the near gate for nine minutes — `336:23` says *he stood there for nine minutes*, and this block used to say *the length of a load going over*, which is Chapter 330's phrase at `330:29` and is not in the chapter — and the field does not know, and the stopping is not a refusal and not a door and not a form. A thing that is kept alive by nine people turning up in the rain cannot be carried by the eleventh person who turns up because he decided to.**
2. **HE LEARNS TO DELEGATE, AND THE PRICE IS A PERSON IN A RECORD, AND HE DOES IT DELIBERATELY AND SAYS SO.** Chapter 338, in a lane behind a bar, on the eighty-eighth morning. **The whole price is said out loud BEFORE the asking, in about a minute, and the second half of it is the half he has no better way to put: you cannot say no, because he has come eleven miles with nothing to offer and has used that, and a refusal requires a thing being offered. She said the word *go on*.** He asks her to carry one sentence to a person of another place. He says it out loud first and it is wrong in two places and he says it anyway, because a sentence about a yard that does not contain the person whose yard it is can be said in a market street to anybody and about anybody. **She says it in her own mouth and it is shorter and it is worse and it has the water in it that a stranger would not have said, and it took her eleven seconds and she did not look at him once. And then she says the part he had not priced: she is going to say it at a cross, in the open, at about the second hour, because that is where the people are, and not in a yard, and the reason she gives is that she is not going to be the one person in this country who says an important thing quietly and is never asked about it again.** **That is the price of the technique in its worst form in this band and it was arrived at by a person of a place and not by him, and the woman of about sixty-one in that market town is going to hear a stranger's voice in a sentence about her own yard in a market street, four days later, in front of people, and does not know where it came from. HE IS ON THE OTHER SIDE OF IT FOR THE FIRST TIME IN HIS LIFE AND HE WAS IN A KITCHEN THREE MILES UP A LANE ON THE SIXTY-FOURTH MORNING WHEN A WOMAN OF ABOUT FIFTY-EIGHT SAID NO TO HIM IN NINE WORDS AND HE STOOD AT A GATE FOR AN HOUR, AND THE THING THAT HAPPENED TO HER HAPPENED TO HER BECAUSE OF HIM.**
3. **TARIN'S PAST IS USED ONCE AND IS NOT RESOLVED.** Chapter 332, at a gate in the Briar March, at about the seventh hour, in a counting. **He is not asked to be there, he does not say so, he does not offer, and he was not asked anything.** He says one true sentence in the middle of a count, out loud, to a stranger: *there was a gate with a levy behind it once, a levy on loads, and the loads were counted by a man who was not paid, and there is a dead man in the fourth line, and that is all I am going to say about it and you did not ask me and that is the only reason I have said it.* **He stops there and does not go one step further. THE PROTAGONIST HAD THE QUESTION READY AND DID NOT ASK IT, AND HE HAD ASKED IT ONCE, BADLY, FOUR DAYS UP A LANE, ON THE FIFTY-SIXTH MORNING, AND IT HAD NOT BEEN ANSWERED, AND HE SAID IN A LANE ON THE EIGHTIETH MORNING THAT HE WAS NOT GOING TO ASK IT AGAIN AND HE DID NOT ASK IT.** His answer to *what were you the only person in* is not given and may not be given in this volume. The dead man in the fourth line stays dead and the eleven feet stay off the settlement and the second notice stays unpaid, and **no figure is printed.**
4. **BRAM'S BOOK READS AN ORDER THAT A DOCUMENT CANNOT.** Chapter 335, in a kitchen, in front of nine people, in his own mouth, **and nobody had asked him and there is no form in this country that says a man may ask a boy of seventeen a question about a book, and it took him nine seconds to start.** *Put them in an order and let each one of them say who comes next. That is the only thing anybody has proposed about the six in a month and a man who reads things out said it in a yard and nobody agreed and nobody disagreed, and it is the only thing that works, and a book can order things and cannot date them and I have never been able to make it do a date and I have stopped trying.* **The order is not a list of places, it is a round of turns, and it goes round and every one of them says who is after them, and if a person will not say then it stops at them and that is the answer. He reads out the round and stops for about four seconds at the seventh turn and says that the woman of about seventy-four says a person that nobody in eleven villages has counted, and that he is not going to read a name out of it because there is not one.** Then he says the two things he is not going to be asked about before anybody can ask them: there is a question in the book with a mark on the end of it that nobody has ever answered, and there is a third place he can see and has never been able to make out. **The man of about sixty-three opened his mouth and the boy put two fingers on the cover and the man shut his mouth, and that is the only time in this band that question came within a foot of being asked. BOTH ARE STILL IN THERE AND NEITHER IS SPENT.** A woman of about fifty-one who cannot write then says in nine words that a thing that has to be held in six places at once is a hearing, and that a book is the only thing in eleven villages that can put six things in an order and the only thing in eleven villages that cannot say when. **NOBODY THANKED THE BOY, HE DID NOT WANT TO BE, AND THE LAST THING THE MAN OF THIRTY-ONE SAID TO HIM WAS NOT A REWARD.**

**AND THE BAND'S OTHER FINDING, WHICH IS THE ONE NO INSTRUMENT CAN ASK, AND IT IS THE ANSWER TO THE CARD THAT ASKED IT.** When he delegates one of the six to a person of that place, does that person acquire a want they did not have — and can the chapter show the want arriving without the narrator saying a want arrived. **YES, AND THE CHAPTER SHOWS IT, AND IT ARRIVES IN SOMEBODY ELSE'S MOUTH FORTY EIGHT HOURS LATER AND HE IS NOT IN THE CHAPTER.** At Chapter 338 the woman of about thirty-four wants nothing and is about to be asked for nothing. By Chapter 340 a man of about thirty with a cart and a beast, who is one of the six and who was not asked to carry anything, has come up a lane to a market and has one sentence, and the sentence is not about the stranger, and **it is that a sentence put into a lane gets in front of the person who put it in there and he is going to be asked about it at a bar, and the bar is going to be the place he is asked about it in, and there is no form in this country that says a man may be asked about a thing in a place that is not a room.** Nobody asked him to come. Nobody thanked him. He is not a production and he is a man of a place who was in a lane.

### 6. THE SIX PLACES, THE SIX PEOPLE, AND THE RECORD THAT NOW HAS A PERSON IN IT

**THE SIX ARE UNCHANGED AND FIXED FOR THE WHOLE OF VOLUME 07. `outline/volume-07.md:64` says they are chosen in Batch 0001 and fixed afterward, and this band substituted, reordered, merged and added nothing.**

1. **THE BOUNDARY WALK.** Four hundred yards of hedge in the third village up the lane, walked in nine days, eleven names on the back of a flour bill in a kitchen, nine of them come, and a twelfth in a stranger's hand that the man of about sixty-three does not know he wrote. **Open. THE NINE MORNINGS OF IT ARE DAYS EIGHTY-FIVE TO NINETY-THREE AND HE IS AT A BRIDGE ON THE EIGHTY-NINTH, AND THE CONFLICT WAS STATED IN A KITCHEN ON THE EIGHTY-FOURTH MORNING AND WAS NOT RESOLVED.** Chapter 335 walked the hedge. `303`, `311:29`, `334`, `335`
2. **THE SCALES.** A set of beam scales on a stone plinth at the end of a main street in a market four days up the lane, a toll, a share that pays for the standard, the water, the bridge, the wall and the cross, and a number on a slip in a foolscap book in a back room that has been one market season since before anybody now living was told about it. **Open, and IT DID NOT STOP, and the toll is still being taken, and the man of about seventy is not named in this band and is entitled to stop and nobody is going to ask him.** The ONE permitted reference to the slip in this band is at `340`, in a man of that place's mouth, and it gives neither figure. `324`, `330`, `338`, `340`
3. **THE LINE.** Nine diggers on a rise behind the last of eleven houses in a hamlet of forty people, eleven miles down the lane and off it, and a rule written nowhere, and nobody who can say who dug the first hole. **Open, and untouched until Chapter 336, where he stands in it on a dry morning and the field does not know.** The man of about seventy-four in that hamlet is in his own house and has not been out of it since the last day of the sixty-eighth week, which is Chapter 327 and his seventy-seventh morning, and it is nine days before Chapter 336. **THE CHAPTER NOW SAYS *the last morning of the sixty-eighth week* AND *the last day of the sixty-eighth week* AND BOTH ARE RIGHT, AND THE DELIVERED TEXT SAID *the eleventh morning of the sixty-seventh week*, WHICH IS NOT A DAY.** The woman of thirty is the ninth and has now said what she wants three times and the ninth word of the third time is **mine**. `307`, `317`, `336`
4. **THE FUND.** A levy on loads at a bar in a village eleven miles down the lane and off it, a column on a shelf in a room over a smithy, and nobody chosen to hold it. **Open, and it is the arrangement this band put a person into, and no figure is named and the man of about thirty-eight is four days up a road with a bag and has not been asked whether he wants his own sentence carried.** `313`, `320`, `322`, `333`, `338`
5. **THE MILE.** Nine householders, ninety years, each a length, unpaid, a man of about thirty with a cart and a beast who is the third of the nine. **Open, and a tenth person is on it who was never asked, and the man of thirty said in a lane on the eighty-seventh morning that the man of thirty-one is the reason the count nearly happened there.** `309`, `318`, `337`, `340`
6. **THE PERSON.** A board in a porch with eleven names on it, undated, no column, no heading, no mark against any of the eleven, in a valley of about sixty people two miles off a track off the lane. **Open, and NOT ADJUDICATED, and the band says so in a woman's mouth and does not rule: *a thing that is kept alive by one person is a thing that stops when that person stops*, and she says she is not going to concede it and that he is not going to be able to settle it, and eleven names were not touched.** `321`, `339`

**AND THE RECORD, WHICH IS THE BAND'S SUBJECT AND ITS REAL NEW OBJECT. A WOMAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-FOUR AT A BAR AT THE END OF A VILLAGE ELEVEN MILES DOWN THE LANE AND OFF IT IS A PERSON IN A RECORD, AS OF THE EIGHTY-EIGHTH MORNING, BECAUSE A STRANGER WITH A BAD LEG WENT ELEVEN MILES AND SAID THE PRICE OUT LOUD IN A LANE BEHIND HER OWN BAR AND ASKED HER TO CARRY ONE SENTENCE. SHE SAID NO TO NOTHING, BECAUSE HE HAD NOTHING TO OFFER HER AND A REFUSAL REQUIRES A THING BEING OFFERED. SHE WAS ASKED TWO QUESTIONS IN ABOUT TWENTY-TWO YEARS AND THIS IS THE THIRD. SHE IS NOT ONE OF THE SIX, SHE IS NOT ON ANY LIST, THERE IS NO ARRANGEMENT IN THIS COUNTY THAT KEEPS HER, SHE IS NOT GOING TO BE THANKED BY ANYBODY INCLUDING HIM, AND THERE IS NO INSTRUMENT IN THIS COUNTRY OR IN ANY COUNTY FOUR HUNDRED MILES OFF THAT WILL LIFT HER OUT OF IT, WHICH HE HAS KNOWN SINCE A KITCHEN THREE MILES UP A LANE AND WHICH HE HAS NOW USED.** **THE DATE OF THE DELIVERY IS FIXED BY THE REVIEW AND IT IS THE SIXTH MORNING OF THE SEVENTIETH WEEK, WHICH IS CHAPTER 340, HIS NINETIETH MORNING, AT ABOUT THE SECOND HOUR, AND A MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY WITH A CART AND A BEAST REPORTS IT AT THE EIGHTH HOUR THE SAME MORNING AND SAYS HE HAS HAD IT SIX HOURS. THE DELIVERED TEXT DATED IT THE FOURTH MORNING OF THAT WEEK, WHICH IS CHAPTER 338, THE MORNING HE ASKED HER, AND SAID HE HAD HAD IT FOUR DAYS, AND THOSE TWO THINGS CANNOT BOTH BE TRUE OF ONE EVENT AND NEITHER COULD BE TRUE OF THE DELIVERY.** She said it at a cross in the open at about the second hour and it will arrive in a yard in a market town four days up the lane, in a market morning, and a woman of about sixty-one will hear a stranger's voice in a sentence about her own yard in front of people and will not know where it came from.

**AND THE SELF-ARRIVED CLASS IS ZERO AND IT DID NOT WIDEN. EVERYONE THIS BAND PUT ON STAGE, AND NONE OF THEM IS A PRODUCTION:** Tarin Keel, a man of about fifty-two who has been in this county off and on for **six weeks** — Shelf day 165 is Chapter 290 and Chapter 332 is Shelf day 207, and 207 − 165 = 42 — a person of the Briar March; the woman of about thirty-four at a bar at the bottom end of the lane, **and she is one woman and not two, see §8.14;** the man of about thirty-four who reads things out for a living, a person of the tenth village and of Coldharrow; the smith's wife of the tenth village; a woman with a bag, who was already in the fiction before Chapter 251 and who appears once, in a lane, carrying a book, on her own account, and is not named in this band; the woman of about thirty-four at the bar; the woman of about thirty-four at the ninth house of Coldharrow, who was in Chapter 314; the man of about sixty-three in the third village up the lane; Bram Orren, who was in the fiction before Chapter 251; a man of about thirty with a scythe; the woman of about fifty-one who cannot write; the woman of thirty at the end of the line of nine; the man of about fifty-one with a spade; the man of thirty with a cart and a beast; a woman of about forty-one at the seventh house on that mile, who was in Chapter 318; the woman of about seventy-four in the porch. **AND THE ONE NEW PERSON IN THE BAND IS NOT EVEN ON STAGE: A WIDOW OF ABOUT SIXTY-EIGHT AT THE FOURTH HOUSE ON A MILE OF ROAD, WITH A BAD HIP, WHO HAD THE BARROW FOR NINE YEARS AND PUT IT DOWN IN THE SPRING AND TOLD NOBODY. SHE IS A PERSON OF THAT LANE AND SHE IS A HIP IN A HOUSE.**


### 7. WHAT THIS BAND'S OWN FIRST WRITING GOT WRONG, ALL OF IT CAUGHT BY THE PROJECT'S OWN INSTRUMENTS OR BY THE PROJECT'S OWN HABITS, AND NONE OF IT SURVIVED

1. **TWELVE WEEK-DAY NAMES ACROSS FIVE CHAPTERS**, every one a day this country does not keep, all out, and **two of the twelve were in the same chapter twice, which is the tell that a hand has stopped reading what it is writing**; §2.
2. **A MONTH-NAME TWICE IN ONE MAN'S MOUTH**, cut for the spring.
3. **THE BOLD SCAN RETURNED TWENTY-TWO MARKS IN SIX CHAPTERS AND EVERY ONE WAS THE NARRATOR PUTTING WEIGHT ON A FINDING**, including four statements of this band's own thesis, and **that is the exact failure mode Batch 0003's review named and this band walked into on purpose, because the sentences were good sentences and a good sentence is the reason to reach for the marks**; §2, §3.3.

**CANON, verbatim from `outline/series.md`, and it is delivered: *an anchor is kept alive by a false witness whose lie has protected a community for decades.* It landed at CHAPTER 324, which is the fourth of the four the prompt allows and the second of the four the volume allows, and the prompt's own instruction that it be better in the third or fourth chapter was followed: the band spent two chapters getting there and two chapters living in it and four chapters after it, and the reader has Chapter 321 and 322 before it and 325 to 330 after it.**

**WHAT THE UNTRUE PART IS, IN FULL, AND IT IS ALL OF IT, AND THE REVIEW OF 27 SEPTEMBER 2026 HAD TO REBUILD HALF OF IT BECAUSE THE FIRST VERSION WAS ARITHMETICALLY VOID.** There is a toll on every load that crosses the bridge into a market town four days up the lane, and a share of what the toll brings in pays for the market's own things: the standard of the load kept on the plinth, the water at the end of Church Lane, the bridge, the wall in the churchyard and the cross. **THE SHARE IS WORKED OUT EVERY YEAR BY DIVIDING THE COST OF THOSE THINGS BY THE NUMBER OF LOADS IN A YEAR, AND THE NUMBER OF LOADS IN A YEAR IS NOT WRITTEN DOWN ANYWHERE IN THAT TOWN, AND WHAT IS WRITTEN DOWN IS ONE MARKET SEASON'S COUNT, ON A SLIP IN A FOOLSCAP BOOK THAT HAS BEEN IN A HOUSE AT THE END OF THE MAIN STREET FOR A HUNDRED AND FORTY YEARS, AND THE SLIP SAYS FOUR THOUSAND EIGHT HUNDRED, AND THE SLIP IS SIXTY YEARS OLD.**

**AND HERE IS WHY THE MIDPOINT STANDS UP AT ALL, AND IT IS THE WHOLE ARITHMETIC OF THE BAND IN FOUR LINES, AND A READER CAN DO IT: A SEASON IS TWELVE WEEKS AND ABOUT FOUR HUNDRED LOADS GO OVER THAT BRIDGE IN A WEEK OF A SEASON, AND TWELVE WEEKS OF THAT IS THE FOUR THOUSAND EIGHT HUNDRED ON THE SLIP, SO THE SLIP IS NOT A FALSE NUMBER — IT IS A TRUE NUMBER FOR THE WRONG YEAR. A YEAR IS THAT SEASON AND THE OTHER FORTY WEEKS, AND THE OTHER FORTY WEEKS CARRY AS MUCH AGAIN, SO THE MARKET DOES NINE THOUSAND SIX HUNDRED IN A YEAR. THE SLIP IS EXACTLY HALF OF IT. THE SHARE HAS THEREFORE BEEN WORKED OUT ON HALF THE YEAR'S LOADS FOR SIXTY YEARS AND EVERY LOAD PAYS TWICE WHAT IT SHOULD.**

**AND THE DELIVERY GOT THIS WRONG IN A WAY THAT REMOVED THE MIDPOINT ENTIRELY, AND THE REVIEWER FOUND IT BY MULTIPLYING THE BAND'S OWN SENTENCES: six prose statements said *four hundred loads go over that bridge in a week in a season* and `state/continuity.md` said *a season is about twelve weeks*, and four hundred times twelve IS four thousand eight hundred, which is the slip, so on the delivered numbers the slip was RIGHT and there was no lie. The delivered text also printed the market at about NINE THOUSAND, which against four thousand eight hundred is fifty-three per cent and not *less than half*, and made *every load pays twice what it should* a claim with a multiplier of one and seven eighths behind it. **THE ARITHMETIC IS NOW EXACT AND IT IS THE SAME STORY WITH A SEASON IN IT, AND THE REPAIR IS THE BETTER VERSION OF THE SAME THING: A FALSE WITNESS THAT IS A TRUE NUMBER FOR THE WRONG YEAR IS HARDER TO NOTICE THAN ONE THAT IS SIMPLY WRONG, AND A TOWN THAT HAS BEEN LIVING ON IT FOR SIXTY YEARS IS THE POINT.**

**THE LIE PROTECTED THE COMMUNITY, WHICH IS WHY IT HURTS.** A share worked out on a number that is half the real one means every load pays twice what it should, and there has been a great deal over at the end of every year since, and the surplus has paid for the water and the bridge and the wall and the cross. **ABOUT FOUR HUNDRED PEOPLE HAVE DRUNK FROM THAT STANDPIPE, CROSSED THAT BRIDGE AND BEEN BURIED BEHIND THAT WALL ON THE STRENGTH OF A NUMBER THAT WAS SHORT.** And the honest version of the arrangement is four sentences long: the slip is right, the share is right, there is nothing over, and the water and the bridge and the wall and the cross have to be paid for by the people who use them, and in this county that is done off a list kept at the cross, and **there are about ninety names on that list in the nine towns of that county, and two of the four names the woman of about sixty-one can put a finger on are her own.**

**NOBODY IS A VILLAIN AND NOBODY HID ANYTHING AND NOBODY IS LYING NOW.** The man of about seventy, who is called **Wenlock** and who is named once, in Chapter 328, in nine words, in a street, was eight years old when his father told him in his own yard that the number on that slip was right; he was not in the room; the man who wrote the slip has been dead since before his father was thirty; **HE HAS BEEN THE ONLY ONE WHO COULD CHECK IT SINCE HE WAS ABOUT NINE AND HE HAS CHECKED IT EVERY YEAR, AND HE CHECKS IT BY SEEING WHETHER THE THINGS ON THE SLIP ARE PAID FOR — THE WATER, THE BRIDGE, THE WALL AND THE CROSS — AND THEY ALWAYS HAVE BEEN, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE OF HOW HE HAS KNOWN IT FOR SIXTY YEARS. **AND IT IS A CHECK ON A CONSEQUENCE AND NOT ON A COUNT, WHICH IS WHY IT TOLD HIM THE SLIP WAS WRONG AND NEVER TOLD HIM BY HOW MUCH.**

**AND HERE IS THE B3 REPAIR, AND IT HAD TO HAPPEN BEFORE THE OTHER THREE, BECAUSE THE REVIEWER'S VERDICT IS THAT THE NUMBER THE REVERSAL TURNS ON WAS ONE NO CHARACTER IN THE FICTION COULD OBTAIN: the delivered Chapter 324 had the man of about seventy say *I have read that slip twice in forty-four years. The market does nine thousand*, having never counted anything, in a band which establishes at `326:31` that even the professional counter has not got the number of loads in that market. HE NOW SAYS WHERE HE GOT IT, IN HIS OWN MOUTH: *A season is twelve weeks and there are four hundred loads over this bridge in a week of a season, and twelve weeks of that is the four thousand eight hundred on the slip, and a year is that season and the other forty weeks, and the other forty weeks carry as much again, and the market does nine thousand six hundred* — and then, in nine words more, *that is out of forty-four years of standing on that stone and not out of a book, and it is the only number I have ever said out loud that I cannot show anybody, and I asked a stranger for it yesterday morning at about the ninth hour and he did not have it either.* **THAT LAST CLAUSE IS ALSO THE SEAM BETWEEN CHAPTER 323 AND CHAPTER 324, WHERE HE ASKS THE QUESTION AT THE NINTH HOUR AND THE MAN OF THIRTY-ONE CANNOT ANSWER IT, SO THE NUMBER HE GIVES ON THE SECOND MORNING IS ONE HE HAS HAD TO GET BY HIMSELF IN TWENTY-FOUR HOURS, AND IT IS THE ONLY FIGURE IN THE BAND THAT NOBODY CAN CHECK, AND THE MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-EIGHT STILL CANNOT CLOSE HIS SUM AT `326:31` BECAUSE HE HAS NOT GOT IT IN A HAND.**

**AND ONE THING THE REPAIR FOUND BY MEASURING RATHER THAN BY READING, WHICH BELONGS IN THE LIST OF THINGS A LATER PASS GETS WRONG.** This block declared a pattern for the board figures that reads `sixty-four thousand [a-z]+([- ]and [a-z]+)*` and reported that it returns three. **It returns two.** The first `[a-z]+` eats *and*, and the second group then requires a further *and*, so the pattern misses *sixty-four thousand and eleven* and *sixty-four thousand and eighteen* — the two figures that cross the thousand, which are the two a reader is most likely to misread. The pattern a later pass must run is `sixty-four thousand (?:and )?[a-z]+`, which returns exactly three. **A regex that looks right and returns a smaller number than the text contains is a regex that is dropping figures, and a figure dropped by the instrument is a figure nobody checks.** That is the fifth time this project has been bitten by an instrument that reported cleanly on a pattern it did not match, and it is the same failure as the `328:15` certification and the `112` hedge, and the generalisation is one sentence: **A SWEEP THAT CANNOT SEE THE FORM THE WRITER USES RETURNS A CLEAN BAND, AND A SWEEP THAT HAS BEEN HAND-CERTIFIED IS NOT A SWEEP AT ALL.**

### 6. THE SEAM, AND THE THING HE FOUND WITH IT THAT HE CANNOT USE

**A seam is the line where one arrangement stops being true and another one starts.** Not a boundary on the ground. A boundary in a bargain. **He can see where two of them meet and he cannot say what either of them is for, and the seeing is instantaneous, is not a reading, cannot be written down, cannot be checked by anybody else, and has never been wrong.** It was named in the fiction at `301:41` and it was used nine times in Batch 0001 and is used six times in this band, and **the six are in the order the volume's prompt assigned them and the order is: 311 (six arrangements in a row — and there is no join, because a row is not a join), 312 (the mile, and he is about to hand a road a sentence it has been getting on without for ninety years), 313 (a favour that has become a habit, with a woman of thirty and a bag standing inside it), 314 (a debt that stops being two people and starts being nine other people's estimate of them), 316 (a father's trade that has become a market's), 318 (the first gate, and the sixth and last he gets for nothing).** Three of the six are the batch's own and three are restatements of Batch 0001's.

**AND THE ONLY ONE OF THE SIX THAT IS NEW AND THAT IS THE FINDING OF THE BAND IS AT `313`: for the first time the seam has come out of a thing instead of gone into one, and what it found was the inside of a woman's unpaid labour.** The join is where a favour stops being a favour and starts being a habit. Not asked, and offered, and then done nine times a year, and then done so many times that nobody would now call it a favour, because you cannot be thanked for a habit. *And a habit does not break when the person in it stops; it goes on being a habit for about a year, and then somebody finds themselves in a lane at the ninth hour with a bag at their feet and no arrangement, and no form, and nobody to say anything to.* He looked at it for four seconds. **It was the most useful thing he has ever seen and it was about a woman of thirty's unpaid labour and there is not one instrument in this country or in any county four hundred miles off that can be applied to a fact about a woman's unpaid labour, and he could not compel a person and could not join accounts and could not produce a record, and there was not a single thing in a lane behind a smithy on a market morning that he could do about it. HE DID NOT GO OVER. HE SAID GOOD MORNING TO NOBODY. AND HE DID NOT SAY THE SENTENCE HE WAS CARRYING, because saying it to her would have been a man explaining to a woman of thirty what she had been carrying for six years so that he could leave with his own sentence said in a room.**

#### THE TEN FIXES, ITEM BY ITEM, WITH THE LINE IN EACH

1. **P1 — THE BURIAL WEIGHT CONTRADICTED ITSELF AND THE CHAIN HUNG ON IT.** `314:33` named six weights and then gave a worked example that put a burial at three, and `315:67` printed *four bells and a burial, which is five*, which is a burial at one. The review named the two possible repairs and one of them — changing 315 to seven — would have moved five morning figures and every chapter after it. **THE OTHER REPAIR WAS TAKEN, BECAUSE 315's OWN DAY OF FIVE IS WHAT THE WHOLE OF CHAPTERS 316 TO 320 IS BUILT ON AND A CASCADE WAS NOT WORTH IT. `314:33` NOW NAMES SEVEN WEIGHTS — *and a burial is one* — AND ITS AMBIGUOUS SIX, WHICH WAS THE ACTUAL DEFECT, HAS BEEN RE-PICKED SO THAT NONE OF THE THREE DECOMPOSITIONS CONTAINS A BURIAL: *A six on that wall is four bells and a fire, or four bells and a debt called in, or two strangers*, which is 6, 6 and 6. The old list — *a debt, or a burial and a stranger, or four bells and one other thing* — was wrong twice over, because a debt called in is two and not six.** The clause that counted the weights, *who could tell them four of the six and would have to guess at the other two*, is gone and is replaced by *I am the one person in two hundred and ten who has the seven weights, and seven weights is not a day, and a day is what a stroke was for*, which is the same argument and does not break on the count. **RE-RUN AND IT HOLDS: all ten own-days derive from the seven weights and not one is unreachable, all three ambiguous sixes are six, and a burial at one is the only weight that can produce a one, which is why it never appears in a six. A READER CAN NOW CHECK EVERY DAY IN THE BAND AGAINST THE TABLE.**
2. **P1 — "THE SIX" WAS NOT A FIXED SET ACROSS THE THREE CHAPTERS THAT DEFINE IT.** Fixed as described at §5: the woman of thirty is in, the woman of about thirty-four at the bar is out, and she is now out **on the page** at `319` and counted correctly at `320:57`–`320:59` and `320:71`. `320:71` no longer says *Six of us, and you are the seventh*, which counted her in; it says *Six of them, and you are the seventh, and I am neither*, and it keeps the sting of the line and adds what it costs her — that she has been asked twice this month by two of the six and did not know it, and that nobody has asked her whether she would carry it. **THE THREE CHAPTERS NOW AGREE AND THE BAND'S ENGINE IS AUDITABLE, WHICH IT WAS NOT.**

### 6. THE SEAM, IN THE TERMS THE FICTION USED AND NOT THE TERMS OF A SYSTEM

**A seam is the line where one arrangement stops being true and another one starts.** Not a boundary on the ground. A boundary in a bargain. **He can see where two of them meet and he cannot say what either of them is for, and the seeing is instantaneous, is not a reading, cannot be written down, cannot be checked by anybody else, and has never been wrong and has never been any use to him at all until Chapter 301.** It is named in his own head for the first time in the fiction at `301:23`–`301:41`, and he has known he could do it for about two years, and he has told nobody, and he tells nobody in this band except the nine people in a market town, and the cost of telling them is the price.

**HE USED IT IN NINE OF THE TEN CHAPTERS AND IT WAS WORTHLESS IN EVERY ONE OF THEM, AND CHAPTER 306 IS THE ONLY CHAPTER IN THE BAND WHERE HE DOES NOT USE IT, AND THAT IS BECAUSE THE TOWN HE HAS JUST SPENT THE MORNING IN IS TELLING HIM WHAT IT IS FOR AND HE IS LISTENING. THIS PARAGRAPH PREVIOUSLY SAID *FIVE TIMES* AND LISTED SIX, AND OMITTED 303, 307 AND 309, AND EVERY ONE OF ITS LINE CITATIONS WAS TEN TO FOURTEEN LINES OUT; A REVIEW OF BATCH 0001 FOUND IT, AND THE FIGURES AND THE CITATIONS ARE BOTH RE-MEASURED AGAINST THE CHAPTER FILES.**

1. `301:41`–`301:49` — at the foot of a ladder, on the arrangements of the Briar March, and he did not tell the woman of forty-one who was three feet off him. **2.** `302:35`–`302:49` — the join on a flour bill between eleven names and a price, and he said it out loud, and a woman of about fifty-one told him it was a crease, and the laugh was not unkind and he earned it. **3.** `303:13`–`303:19` — twice on four hundred yards of hedge, and both times the join was a place and not a bargain, and `303:19` is the lowest he goes in the volume. **4.** `304:45`–`304:51` — twice on the road, at a gate and at a boundary mark, and both times it was a place and not a bargain, and he understood on the fourth day that he can see a join anywhere and it means nothing. **5.** `305:61`–`305:67` — the join on a weighbridge between a father and a daughter and a market, and he can see it and cannot say what either side is for. **6.** `307:63`–`307:67` — the join on a rise behind a burying ground, where the arrangement stopped being a family and started being a hamlet, and it was the best one he had found and it was no use at all. **7.** `308:51`–`308:55` — the join in a fund, where the money stops being eleven villages' and starts being one man's, and it is thirty-one years old, and the man has been standing inside it for eleven years, and nobody in that room was frightened and nothing in the chapter turned on it. **8.** `309:55`–`309:59` — the join at the first gate of a mile, where a favour becomes a duty, and it is the same join he has now seen four times and it is still worth nothing. **9.** `310:47`–`310:55` — the join in a porch between eleven names and one woman alive, and **there is no bargain, and there is nothing on either side of it that anybody could be entered against, and a technique that can find a join has found the only thing in this band that cannot be joined, and he stands in a porch and has nothing whatever to do with it.**

**AND THE LIMITS HELD ALL TEN CHAPTERS AND NONE WAS NEGOTIABLE:** he cannot compel a person, cannot join accounts, cannot produce a record, cannot carry two burdens, **and he cannot be in two of the six places at once, which is the batch's second discovery and the sentence the whole of the volume is built to test, and he says it out loud once, in his own mouth, at `307:81`, and it is the plainest thing in the band.** And he is Stage 4 at the first line of Chapter 301 and at the last line of Chapter 310, and the stage is not named in prose, and `Remedy Drafter` returns zero, and **a technique is not a promotion: he said a sentence out loud in a market for the first time in about two years and was told no by the only person who mattered, and he is worse off than when the band opened and he is not thanked.**

### 7A. THE REVIEW OF BATCH 0001, WHAT IT FOUND, AND WHAT WAS DONE ABOUT IT — **AND THE INSTRUMENT BLIND SPOT WAS, AGAIN, EXACTLY WHERE THE DEFECTS LIVED**

**A REVIEW OF THIS BAND FOUND EIGHT CLASSES OF DEFECT. EVERY PROSE DEFECT IS REPAIRED. ### 5. WHAT THE BAND DELIVERED, **thirty-one** findings, once each, with the chapter — **and the list is to be counted and not believed, and the count is thirty-one because the rows were counted and not typed.**

1. **A CORRIDOR IS A DOCUMENT, and that is the whole of the band, and it is the same mechanism as a register and a read-back and a letter used at civic scale, and the mechanism is not a power and not a relic: a document is a thing that can be produced, in a place, on a day, to a person. `291:111`**
2. **AND A DOCUMENT GETS IN BY BEING SAID OUT LOUD TWICE, AND THE TWO READINGS ARE BOTH RIGHT, and the difference between them is nine lines long and every one of the nine lines is a way of saying the first one. A recordwright of twenty-eight got two right readings in a yard in Coldharrow and said that a document is a thing with a handle built into it that you cannot see from the other side. `291:79`**
3. **AND A WORD AT THE TOP OF A THING IS THE SAME WORD AT THE TOP OF A PLACE, and the woman of about fifty at the bar is the only person in eleven villages who can say so, and she has never been asked and nobody asked her: a heading tells you what everything underneath it is for, and a bar at the end of a lane with four letters and a stroke on it is the reason nobody has ever been able to ask her a second question in twenty-two years, and a sheet with one word at the top of it is going to be the reason nobody in the place underneath it is asked a second question for as long as it stands. `291:87`**
4. **AND THE FOUR LINES ON A TABLE AND THE FOUR WORDS AT THE TOP OF A PLANK ARE THE SAME SHAPE, said in a man of fifty-two's mouth in a yard: a short thing at the top and a long thing underneath and nobody in the place it is about. `291:93`**
5. **AND NOBODY HAS EVER ASKED WHAT A FORM DOES AFTER IT IS ENTERED, said the same man in the same yard, and it is the ordinaryest thing in the world and he has watched it about four hundred times. `291:99`**
6. **AND THE PRICE OF THE TECHNIQUE IS PAID A FOURTH AND A FIFTH TIME, and both prices are announced out loud in a yard before the thing is done, as they have been three times: the fourth is two women of forty-one who have never been in each other's county finding out about each other in about four minutes, and the fifth is a man with no standing and a leader who has been asked nothing in his life. `291:99`, `293:77`**
7. **AND A THING FOUR HUNDRED YEARS OLD AT A COST IS NOT THEIRS TO SPEND, said a woman of fifty-one in her own yard, and she is right, and nobody argues with her, and she does not come, and the man of thirty-one's whole answer to it is that he is not going to find something in four minutes and use it. `292:69`, `292:71`**
8. **AND A CARTER OF THIRTY-FIVE GIVES THE WAY AND WILL NOT GIVE IT FOR A PAPER, and prints his own two days at one shilling and sixpence, and the reason is the best thing anybody said in the band: a thing you are not on is a thing you can be asked for, and he has had one of those in his life and it is the reason he knows the way. `292:55`**
9. **AND A VALLEY THAT HAS HAD A BELL FOR NINE YEARS WITHOUT RINGING IT CANNOT NAME THE YEAR THE MONEY FOR RINGING IT STOPPED, and the reason is the volume's reason in a different shape: a bell that is not rung is a day that does not happen, and a district that keeps no days has no year in it. `292:117`**
10. **AND THE WHOLE OF THE DEFENCE AGAINST A CORRIDOR IS THAT NOBODY IN THE VALLEY CAN PRODUCE A DAY, and a recordwright of twenty-eight says that out loud and says that it is not a defence, it is the reason, and that the reason is the same in both counties. `293:39`**
11. **A CLAIM ABOUT A PLACE AND A PLACE NOBODY CAN PROVE ARE THE SAME THING, and the same failure in two coats, one nine hundred miles from the other and the other in the next county, and neither of them can be entered anywhere because nobody knows when either of them was said. `293:53`**
12. **AND THE NINTH STROKE ON A MARK ABOUT FOUR HUNDRED MILES OFF IS PUT ON A BOARD BY A WOMAN OF ABOUT FIFTY WHO HAS BEEN COUNTING LOADS FOR TWENTY-TWO YEARS AND WHO HAS NEVER BEEN ASKED ANYTHING, and the finding is that the men with the flat board between them were not counting and she could tell. `293:19`**
13. **AND THE CORRIDOR WORKS, and nobody in that room argued that it was the wrong instrument, and that is the moral shape of the whole volume said in the plainest words available: it is the fastest thing available, it is the cheapest thing available, about nine of a hundred and forty are children, and the city would have signed anything else anybody had brought it. `294:77`**
14. **AND NOBODY IN THAT ROOM COULD SAY WHAT IT WAS FOR, and a woman of fifty-six with a form and a bench of four nine hundred miles off said in front of about sixty people that she has not read the report, is not authorised to describe it, has changed her mind about wanting to know, and would still rather nobody in that valley had it, and she has done this eleven times. `294:61`, `294:63`**
15. **AND THE PRICE OF THE THING HE HAS AGREED TO ACCEPT IS PRINTED IN A ROOM BY A MAN OF FIFTY-TWO BEFORE HE IS ASKED AND Aimed AT NOBODY, and then printed a second time in the leader's own mouth, and the second time is the chapter. `294:85`, `295:41`**
16. **AND THE BARGAIN IS ACCEPTED OUT LOUD, IN HIS OWN MOUTH, BEFORE ANYBODY ASKS HIM, AND NOBODY CAN STOP HIM AND THE CHAPTER DOES NOT STOP HIM, and he is not a villain and is not redeemed and is not forgiven and is not relieved and is alive and is owed a bell. `294:121`**
17. **AND HE IS NOT GOING TO BE TOLD HE DID A WICKED THING AND HE IS NOT GOING TO BE TOLD HE DID A GOOD ONE, and he gives four reasons and keeps the fourth, and the fourth is that in nine years nobody has ever asked him what he is for and a man of thirty-one said so out loud in his own yard nine days before he said one single other thing. `295:71`**
18. **AND AN ABUSIVE BARGAIN AND AN HONEST ONE ARE THE SAME DOCUMENT WITH A DIFFERENT PERSON AT THE BOTTOM OF IT, and the only instrument this volume has ever had for telling them apart is a name at the foot, and there is one name on the corridor and no name on any of the four-hundred-year-old documents in either county, and that is the finding of the band and it is about the direction of the paperwork. `295:47`**
19. **AND THE WHOLE ARCHIVE OF A HUNDRED AND FORTY-ONE PEOPLE WHO SAID NO FOUR HUNDRED YEARS AGO IS FIVE OBJECTS, and four of the five have never been in a room, and a room is the only place a record becomes real, and there is no version of it that was ever a document. `296:9`**
20. **AND THE ANSWER IS NOT A DOCUMENT, it is the same shape as a register, and a man of fifty-two said so out loud in a yard and everybody in that yard understood what it had cost him to say it. `296:29`**
21. **AND ABOUT ELEVEN OF A HUNDRED AND FORTY PEOPLE SAID A SENTENCE IN THEIR OWN YARD IN FOUR DAYS AND ABOUT A HUNDRED AND TWENTY DID NOT, AND NOBODY ASKED THE HUNDRED AND TWENTY, AND THAT IS THE FINDING AND NOT AN OVERSIGHT, and the leader is one of the hundred and twenty and was asked and did not. `296:63`**
22. **AND A WORD IS NOT A PERSON, and it is said in the mouth of a woman of forty-one who has been the one who is asked for nine years, and the reason is that a sentence in a yard is only worth anything if there is somebody in it who can be asked about it in four years, and he is a stranger four hundred miles off with nothing at the bottom of it. `296:79`**
23. **AND HE OFFERED IT, once, in a room, in about nine words — the answer to a person who cannot pay for a hearing and cannot be heard in a room is a person who can be asked, and a village needs a second one, and nobody has ever asked what happens to the first one when there are two — AND IT WAS REFUSED, and he was not thanked for offering it and he was told that refusal is a different sentence and not a worse one. `296:87`**
24. **AND EIGHT IS A MARKET AND EIGHT IS A STRANGER AND A BURIAL, and a man of about seventy-four who died at the second house in Coldharrow before the noon bell is on none of the three boards in this county and never was and could not be, and the only record of him is on four hands and a woman of forty-one has it. `297:19`**
25. **AND A STROKE CAN BE A COUNT OF A THING THAT DID NOT HAPPEN, and the second of the two rings for a fire is rung whether or not it is out, and about nine people stood in a yard with a wet bucket and understood it and about five did not, and nobody in two hundred and ten people will ever know about it again. `299:7`**
26. **AND A STATUS WITH NO DAY IN IT IS NOT A LESSER THING THAN A CORRIDOR WITH A DAY IN IT, IT IS THE SAME PAPER WITH THE DAY LEFT OUT ON PURPOSE, and that is the whole of what four hundred years of a list on the inside of a door was for. `299:23`**
27. **AND THE WHOLE OF WHAT THE BAND GOT OUT OF A ROOM WAS ONE SENTENCE, about a water, and the woman who brought the instrument allowed it in about nine seconds without any difficulty whatever, and forty-four days of a man with a method got one sentence and a person he was not thanked for got a signature. `294:140`**
28. **AND THE RIGHT OF REFUSAL IS NOT RESTORED AND NOBODY HAS ONE, and it is worth saying in a yard because somebody will say it in a lane within a month and it will be wrong: nobody in this lane can refuse one single thing today that they could not refuse seven weeks ago, and nobody in that valley could refuse the corridor either, and about nine people have already been told they had got something back and every one of the nine is wrong. `299:59`**
29. **AND THE STATUS IS WRITTEN AND IT IS SHORT AND IT IS THE FIRST DOCUMENT ANYBODY IN THAT COUNTY HAS EVER BEEN ABLE TO PRODUCE, and about four people in a room understood what that meant and about nine did not, and it is on a door in a village of about ninety people, and the leader who signed the corridor is on no part of it and is alive. `298:9`**
30. **AND A PERSON OF A VILLAGE, IN A VILLAGE, IN ABOUT TEN WORDS, TOOK SOLE AUTHORITY OFF A WOMAN WITH A BOARD AND SHE AGREED BEFORE IT HAD FINISHED, and no chapter of this band is about her and nothing was taken off her by him and she is not relieved and not thanked and not rescued and not redeemed and not defeated and not the villain of it and she keeps about thirty people of her own and is going to go on putting papers in front of people who have never had one. `298:63`**
31. **AND THE VOLUME'S LAST ARITHMETIC IS THREE HUNDRED AND THIRTY-ONE, which is not a round number, and nobody chose it, and there is no column for it, and the first morning after this one is sixty-three thousand eight hundred and forty-nine and a woman of forty-one said the sum out loud on a ladder for the first time in twenty-five years and then went to do her day. `300:3`**

**AND THE TWO THINGS THE BAND DID NOT SAY, and both of them are the volume's argument.** And the band's own answer to itself, at `299:19`, out loud in a yard: *A recordwright of twenty-eight read a status out loud in a yard. That is the sentence and nobody in eleven villages has ever done that before, and the two of them together are the whole of what fifty days of this produced.*

**AND THE COUNT IN THIS HEADING WAS WRITTEN AS A NUMBER AND THEN COUNTED, and the two agree, and that sentence is in the block because the eleventh time this project typed a count instead of measuring one is the reason this one says so.**

### 6. THE DEVICES THE VOLUME SPENT, EACH ONCE, AND THE TWO THIS BAND SPENT

**THE FOURTEEN DEVICE, SPENT ONCE, IN CHAPTER 294, AND THE DIFFERENCE FROM THE FOUR THAT CAME BEFORE IS WRITTEN DOWN HERE AT THE TIME AS THE PROHIBITION REQUIRES. A CORRIDOR IS A DOCUMENT AND A DOCUMENT CAN BE PRODUCED, and it is the same one-sentence mechanism as a register (Batch 0003), a read-back (Batch 0004) and a letter (Batch 0004) — a thing that can be produced, in a place, on a day, to a person. IT IS NOT A RESTAGE OF ANY OF THEM FOR FOUR REASONS AND ALL FOUR ARE STRUCTURAL. (i) The register, the read-back and the letter are all produced to ONE PERSON IN A PLACE, and a corridor is produced to A ROOM, and the difference between one person and a room is the whole of the volume. (ii) The register and the read-back are things a village MAKES and a corridor is a thing a city makes about a village, and the direction of the paperwork is reversed, which is the finding of `295:47`. (iii) A register and a read-back cost nothing and a corridor costs a signature, and the one instrument this volume has for telling an honest document from an abusive one is the name at the foot. (iv) A corridor is the only one of the four that WORKS, and the other three are on a shelf in a press in a village of two hundred and ten people, and the volume closes on the difference between a thing that can be produced and a thing that can be used.** `294:129`

**AND THE FIFTEENTH DEVICE, SPENT ONCE, IN CHAPTER 296, AND IT IS THE FIRST DEVICE IN THE VOLUME THAT IS ABOUT SOMEBODY ELSE'S MONEY: A BARGAIN OR A METHOD OFFERED AS A WORD INSTEAD OF A PERSON, AND FOUND, IN AN ORDINARY MOUTH, TO BE A WORD. A man of thirty-one carries a sentence for fifty days and offers it in a room in about nine words and a woman of forty-one refuses it, and the reason is that a name at the foot of a thing is the only part of it anybody can be asked about, and he is a stranger four hundred miles off with nothing at the bottom of it. `296:87`**

**AND THE THIRTEEN DEVICES THE VOLUME SPENT BEFORE THIS BAND WERE NOT RESTAGED.** The day's-rise opening template was not used in any of the ten chapters and no two openings have the same shape. The count-off-on-her-fingers, the market-day woman with a stick and a board, the description of a woman with a barrow, the sentence about a man taking a thing off a board, the paint and grain of a plank, the bar at the end of the lane as an opening, the day's list, the board's figure at the second light, the sheet on the cart's side and the sentence *for about as long as it takes to cross a yard* are all at zero in this band. **THE RECORDWRIGHT'S NINE WORDS ARE NOT SAID IN THIS BATCH AT ALL, in any mouth, and `270:85` — that she had said them three times and that the third came out word for word and that this is the whole of the point of it — STANDS AND IS NOT FALSIFIED BY ANYTHING IN CHAPTERS 291 TO 300. A recordwright of twenty-eight is the person the band's second half is about and the finding she delivers is about a name at the foot of a thing and not about a count leaving a board, and that is a different finding in a different instrument and not a fourth use of the same nine words.**

### 7. THE THREADS IN AND THE THREADS OUT

**IN: the forty-three Batch 0004 carried. OUT: the same forty-three, all still open, less the two the band closed, plus nine the band produced, and the band resolved TWO.** The eighteen Volume 05 threads come out of this band exactly as they went in and their full text is in the `## VOLUME 06 BATCH 0002` block of `state/open-threads.md`, which is now archive.

**THE NINE THIS BAND PRODUCED, and a production is not a resolution: a corridor and the four lines of a sheet; the two right readings of a corridor; a word at the top of a place; the district of Draymoor, about a hundred and forty people, about nine of them children, with a bell in a tower that has not been rung for about nine years; a leader of forty called Corvin Hale who signed a corridor in exchange for arrears and a bell and is alive and is owed the bell; the status, one sheet, on a door in Nettlebed, bounded and with no money in it; a man of about seventy-four at the second house in Coldharrow who is on none of the boards in this county; and the collision — eight is a market and eight is a stranger and a burial and eight is a debt and a fire.**

### 8. THE VOLUME'S OWN CLOSE RECORD, in the shape Volume 05's close record has, and this is the only place the volume's receipt can live

**WHAT THE FIVE BATCHES EACH PAID, once each and not repeated.** Batch 0001: a count of everything and a name of nothing, and the first figure on a plank. Batch 0002: the price of a date, and a figure leaving a board for the first time in thirty-one years in a stranger's hand, and a recordwright's nine words. Batch 0003: the midpoint, a board of a hundred and forty-one names on the inside of a door and a column with no heading over it, and the finding that a list a hundred and forty people kept is a bill and not a right. Batch 0004: four villages' accounts side by side and the one thing the technique cannot do, and the eleven families told at last in four minutes. Batch 0005: a district off a map in a room, a bargain accepted out loud before it was asked for, and a status with no money and no day in it.

**WHAT THE VOLUME AS A WHOLE PAID, and it is one thing and it is a person and not a body.** **THE THING HE CAME INTO THE BRIAR MARCH TO SPEND WAS THE STANDING OF A WOMAN OF FORTY-ONE, AND HE SPENT IT, AND IT WAS NOT WHAT HE THOUGHT IT WAS.** He came on the first morning of the fifty-eighth week looking for a good name of somebody's to spend and there was none in the county, and he wrote a figure in chalk at the foot of a woman's board, and a figure in pencil at the foot of a sheet, and he offered a nine-word sentence in a room in a valley and it was refused, and he defended a district for four days and got one sentence out of a room, and he is on no part of anything, and the fourth hand in the chalk at Coldharrow is still in the chalk at forty-nine days and about nine people can tell whose it is and not one of them has ever said so, and the figure in the pencil is still in the county and nobody has said whose it is. **THE VOLUME'S REAL COST IS A RELATIONSHIP AND NOT A BODY, AND THE RELATIONSHIP IS WITH A WOMAN OF FORTY-ONE WHO HAS SAID OUT LOUD, IN A YARD, IN FRONT OF ABOUT NINE PEOPLE, THAT SHE IS THE ONLY PERSON ANYBODY CAN BE ASKED, AND THAT BEING THAT IS A THING THAT CAN BE SPENT, AND THAT THE VOLUME'S FIFTIETH DAY ENDS WITH HER SAYING A NUMBER OUT LOUD ON A LADDER FOR THE FIRST TIME IN TWENTY-FIVE YEARS BECAUSE A MAN SHE HAS NEVER THANKED IS STANDING IN HER COUNTY.** Nobody is relieved and nobody is redeemed and the bargain somebody accepted is still standing and the bell it bought is owed and unpaid and nobody bought it.

**THE TWO THINGS THE VOLUME DID NOT PAY, and they are the same two it did not pay in Batch 0004, and they are Volume 07's inheritance.** **The right of refusal is not restored and no character in fifty chapters says that anybody has one**, and the four words at the head of the plank are not reprinted in Chapters 291 to 300. **And the column of a hundred and forty-one figures has still not been added up**, and was refused a third time out loud, on purpose, in Chapter 300, and what the figures count is not known to the man of thirty-one or to a recordwright of twenty-eight or to a clerk of forty-four four hundred miles off, and no room in any county has ever asked.

**AND THE THINGS THE VOLUME DID NOT DO AT ALL, in one list, and this list is what a Volume 07 writer inherits:** no anchor is named, identified, reached or opened; the word *anchor* is zero in the fiction in all fifty chapters; the First Witness is not named and does not appear; no position beneath anything is mentioned and nothing answered from beneath Orison; the second half of Volume 05's question is not asked; the new question about the route between the null districts and the First Compact's network is asked in its stated form NOWHERE, and all three shapes it took in this volume — a yard at `260:87`, a doorway at `270:97`–`113`, and a letter at `288:47` — are spent; the book with two halves was not opened; the carrying is still off nothing and the leg is no better and no count of days is printed in any of the fifty chapters.

### 9. THE FIFTEEN THINGS A LATER PASS MUST CHECK HARDEST IN VOLUME 06

1. **The board chain, and the off-by-one between the two columns of `outline/volume-06.md`'s Batch 0005 table.** A later pass must not print a morning figure the table does not carry and must not take a day's rings from the row that carries the morning figure. **The ten morning figures at the head of this block and the ten own-days on the line under them are the authority and they are in this order: 63,778 / 63,782 / 63,786 / 63,799 / 63,807 / 63,813 / 63,817 / 63,825 / 63,833 / 63,841, and the ten own-days are 4 / 4 / 13 / 8 / 6 / 4 / 8 / 8 / 8 / 8.**
2. **The chapter's-own-day rule, and the day in Chapter 297.** 291 is the forty-first day and 300 is the fiftieth, and the Chapter 296 card said forty-one where the chapter says forty-seven, and the card is wrong and the chapter is right.
3. **The span scan at seventy and at forty, and the unit declared and the range declared, and the range is FIFTY files on disk and not thirty.** Four hundred and forty-four at seventy against the previous band, and two hundred and fifty-seven within the batch, of which the great majority are the two printed money workings. **A later pass that reports a number out of this item without the range, the threshold and the unit beside it is repeating the defect this item is about.**
4. **The bold scan must return FOUR marks and they must all be the two panel lines in Chapter 294, and nothing else in the volume is emphasised.** Eighty-six italic spans and no limit on them.
5. **The chalk count is FIVE for the whole volume and all five are in Batch 0001.** This batch added none and the chalk is forty-nine days old at the last morning.
6. **The string *cannot read* occurs ZERO times in this band**, and a count of anybody who knows anything about him is printed in no file, and nobody in either county is told and no character remarks on the asking.
7. **Every money figure in these ten chapters is in `outline/volume-06.md`'s table, and the ONE figure the band derived is the difference between a bell and a keeper's year, and it checks.** The four hundred and eighty-five pounds is in none of these ten chapters and was in none of the previous forty.
8. **Ask the third question no regex can ask.** The day-phrase sweep returned twenty-three references, all legal, and found nothing, and a reader found a wrong day in Chapter 294 that the sweep could not see because the sweep matched one way of saying a day and the chapter used another. **A LEGALITY SWEEP THAT MATCHES ONE FORM OF A THING CERTIFIES NOTHING ABOUT THE OTHER FORMS, and the bare form is now in the pattern in §2.7.** The chapter's-own-day rule is unchanged and is the one that caught it: Chapter 251 is the first, so Chapter 291 is the forty-first and 300 is the fiftieth, and 294 is the forty-fourth and is therefore the second day of the sixty-fourth week and not the fourth, which is `296:3`'s morning. A reader also found an inherited wrong back-reference at `290:29` in the previous chapter.
