10. **Do not let a later volume restage the ten frames of the board figure as orthography.** The rule is settled in writing: the figure is spelled in words in every chapter and the FRAME varies, and a woman who has kept one number in one hand for twenty-five years does not spell it three ways.
11. **Do not name a weekday, a month-name, an anchor, a stone, the First Witness, or a position beneath anything, and do not use the word *stone* for masonry.** This batch's first writing used *Tuesday* once in a character's mouth and it was cut.
12. **Do not let a hand-off be wrong about a character's sex or age.** **Corvin Hale is a man of forty and the woman of forty-one in Draymoor is a woman of forty-one and the two of them are different people and the man of thirty-one who owns the tower at Nettlebed is never to be confused with the man of thirty-one from four hundred miles off.** Sable Venn is a woman. The clerk of forty-four is a man and is not named in any chapter of Volume 06 and may not be.
13. **Do not prune the state files inside a phase that is also writing prose, and do not edit the archive blocks below the top block of any of the six.**
14. **Do not let a later volume restage the bargain.** A bargain somebody accepted out loud with the working printed before they were asked is device ten of this volume and it is spent, and the difference between that device and the corridor's document is written down in §6 and must not be blurred.
15. **AND THE FIFTEENTH THING, WHICH NO INSTRUMENT IN THIS PROJECT WILL FIND: the thing the column counts is still unknown, nobody may answer it, nobody may sum it, and the bar of a lane is still a piece of wood across a gap in a hedge because there is no road behind it and never was, and a writer who needs the number must go and ask a person of a village.**

### 10. THE FIFTEEN THINGS A VOLUME 07 WRITER NEEDS AND CANNOT GET FROM A FIGURE

1. **The ten morning figures and the ten own-days at §1, and the fact that the last morning in Volume 06 is sixty-three thousand eight hundred and forty-one and the first morning after it is sixty-three thousand eight hundred and forty-nine, and that the second of those is in no table and in no card on purpose.**
2. **The four disputes and where each one closed.** A gate, closed by a walk. A lane, in a register in four words and in three instruments and in a boy's book and in no map. Ninety acres, known to eleven families and unresolvable. A list of a hundred and forty-one names, still a bill and not a right, whose column has not been added up.
3. **The register: FIFTY-TWO PLACES, which is one more than it was, and the one more is a valley four hundred miles off, and about eleven of a hundred and forty people there said a sentence in their own yard in four days and about a hundred and twenty did not and nobody asked the hundred and twenty.** It has one place on the lane, a second line nobody can classify, two crosses that came off on a market morning without anybody asking, and an eleventh name on the sheet that is a place nobody in two hundred and ten people can name and that therefore cannot come off. **The rules are eleven lines and there is no twelfth line and there is not going to be one, and the recordwright of twenty-eight keeps it and is not in it.**
4. **The corridor, and what it was, and that it is still standing and is not going to be torn up.** A city put a district of about a hundred and forty people off every map it keeps, in a room, in about nine minutes, on a day the valley could not name, on the strength of a report it would not describe, in exchange for nine years of arrears and a bell, and about nine of the hundred and forty are children and it is the fastest and the cheapest thing available and it works.
5. **The status, and all eleven of the things it does not have in it:** no gate, no toll, no bar, no date, no bench, no seat, no chair, no room with a door on it except a press, no vote, no meeting, no officer, no money, and no name at the foot of it, and a place on the sheet that cannot be found and is left named.
6. **That the man who signed the corridor is alive, is in his own field on an ordinary morning, is owed a bell, is on no part of the register and the status, was not relieved, was not forgiven, was not thanked, and said out loud that he was not going to be told he had done a wicked thing or a good one.** A Volume 07 writer may not undo the bargain and may not redeem him and may not make him a villain.
7. **That the leader's fourth reason for signing was that nobody in nine years had ever asked him what he was for, and that the reason he gave was a man of thirty-one saying it out loud in his own yard nine days before he said one single other thing.** That is the volume's whole argument in a valley four hundred miles off and it is the cheapest and most expensive sentence in Chapter 295.
8. **That the man of thirty-four has gone home four hundred miles with a scrap of his own handwriting on the back of his own hand, and that the sentence he stands behind is still his, and that he did not act on it in this county, and that there was nothing in this county for him to act on, and that that is a fact and not a mercy.** He is not a villain, not a servant, and nobody sent for him, and the corridor was four hundred miles off and was never a place he had been.
9. **That a woman of fifty-six with a form and a bench of four nine hundred miles off has gone back and will not describe a report and does not know what is in it, and changed her mind about wanting to know and would still rather nobody in that valley had it.**
10. **That a word is not a person, and that the instrument for turning a word into a person is a name at the foot of a thing, and that the only instrument this volume ever had for telling an honest document from an abusive one is a name, and that the corridor has one and the four-hundred-year-old list has not got one.**
11. **The four bells and the six rings, and that a stranger is three and a market is four and a boundary is seven and a debt called in is two and a burial is one and a fire is two, and that from Chapter 297 the weights COLLIDE: eight is a market and eight is a stranger and a burial and eight is a debt and a fire.** Any day a later writer invents must be assembled out of that list and nothing else.
12. **That a bell that is not rung is a day that does not happen, and that Draymoor has a tower with a bell in it that has not been rung since before a woman of forty-one's mother died, and that nobody in that valley can say in which year the money for ringing it stopped, and has been told twice that it was before she was there.** That is the volume's engine in a fourth shape.
13. **That a carter of thirty-five at the end of a bad road called Stennick knows the way past the end of the county and will not give it up for a paper, and that the reason is that a thing you are not on is a thing you can be asked for.** A recordwright and a man of thirty-four and a woman of about sixty have all gone down that road. So has a woman of about forty who carries other people's paper and has never once opened any of it, and she has carried three routes' worth out of this county and opened none of them.
14. **That a person of the March is not a production and a person of a district four hundred miles off is not a production either, and that the count is zero and is at `state/character-state.md`, and that the class is restated for Volume 07 in the same file.**
15. **And the thing that is not a fact: Volume 07 opens on Shelf day 176, the second day of the sixty-fifth week, and the board at Coldharrow is at sixty-three thousand eight hundred and forty-nine, and nobody knows that but a woman of forty-one, and a volume that begins by making her the first person in the frame should ask itself why.**

### 11. WHAT THIS BAND'S OWN FIRST WRITING GOT WRONG, ALL FOUND BY THE PROJECT'S OWN INSTRUMENTS OR BY THE PROJECT'S OWN HABITS, AND NONE OF IT SURVIVED TO THE DELIVERY

**AND THE FIRST OF THEM IS THE WORST AND IT IS NOT FOUND BY ANY INSTRUMENT IN THIS PROJECT.** **A repair script run over seven of the ten files normalised their whitespace and wrote the result back, and it destroyed the paragraph structure of Chapters 293, 294, 295, 297, 298, 299 and 300.** Those seven files were rewritten from the author's own text with the paragraph breaks and the `---` scene breaks restored and every figure and every edit carried across, and **a script that finds a span cannot safely be used to rewrite a file, and a later pass that runs one over prose will do this again.** The lesson is not the seven files. The lesson is that the duplicate-span instrument in this project REQUIRES A REWRITE, and no instrument in this repository may open a chapter file for writing.

- **THE WEEKDAY SCAN RETURNED ONE, *Tuesday*, in a character's mouth in Chapter 295**, and it was cut.
- **THE BOLD SCAN RETURNED FOUR MARKS IN CHAPTER 297, which is a chapter that spent no panel**, and the two were emphasis spans in the finding about a day of eight and the stranger who went through the bar, and both were changed to italics.
- **THE PANEL IN CHAPTER 294 SAID *MAY BE PRODUCED* in capitals**, which the month-word scan returns as a capital-M hit, and the line was reworded to *IS PRODUCED*.
- **THE META SWEEP RETURNED SEVENTEEN**, fifteen of them the narrator saying *this volume* and *this chapter*, and two of them the literal string *in a book in* as an accident of the phrase *a line about it in a book in a building*, and all seventeen are out.
- **THE CROSS-BATCH SPAN SCAN AT SEVENTY RETURNED ONE THOUSAND FOUR HUNDRED AND TWENTY-ONE and the within-batch scan returned SIX HUNDRED AND FIFTY-EIGHT**, and both were cut to four hundred and forty-four and two hundred and fifty-seven by rewording eleven sources and the sources are listed in §2.4 and §2.5. **THE RESIDUAL IS THE TWO PRINTED MONEY WORKINGS AND THE BAND'S OWN SUBJECT MATTER AND IT IS DECLARED, NOT HIDDEN.**
- **A CARTER'S FOUR DAYS' WALKING WAS PRINTED AS A HUNDRED AND TWENTY PENCE AND AS EIGHT SHILLINGS, in a character's mouth at `292:55`, and both are wrong: four days at one shilling and sixpence is seventy-two pence, which is six shillings. A hundred and twenty pence and ten shillings are the REMAINDER of a carter's year, 2,520 − 2,400, and the first writing appears to have reached for the nearest figure in the table. The unit-price instrument caught it because the unit price was in the sentence and four times eighteen is not a hundred and twenty, and that is the instrument doing the job it was built for in the fourth batch in a row.**
- **AND THE FIGURES THAT WERE RIGHT THE FIRST TIME, which is recorded because a record that only lists failures teaches a pass to expect failures: the board chain closed on the first writing, all ten morning figures, all ten own-days, all ten day-counts, every money figure, the difference between a bell and a keeper's year, the three hundred and thirty-one, the sixty-three thousand eight hundred and forty-nine, the ten distinct frames, and the whole of the three instruments the outline named for this band. **AND THE CLAIM *ALL TWENTY-TWO DAY-PHRASES* IS THE ONE ITEM ON THIS LIST THAT WAS NOT RIGHT, AND IT IS WRONG TWICE: there are twenty-three and not twenty-two, because the pattern could not see the bare form at `294:5`, and the one it could not see named the wrong day.** Nine of the eleven defect classes this project has been bitten by in two hundred and fifty chapters did not happen here, and the one that did happen is the one nobody had an instrument for, and the review of the delivery then found two more in the band's own prose, which are the two below.**
- **AND SIX MORE FOUND AFTER THE DELIVERY WAS WRITTEN — TWO BY THE CLOSING SWEEP AND FOUR BY THE REVIEW OF THE DELIVERY — WHICH IS THE POINT OF A CLOSING SWEEP AND OF A REVIEW, AND THE FIRST TWO ARE IN THIS FILE'S OWN HOUSEKEEPING RATHER THAN IN THE BAND'S OWN FIGURES AND THE LAST FOUR ARE IN THE BAND'S OWN PROSE OR IN THE LIST THAT DESCRIBES IT.**

  - **A CHARACTER'S AGE WAS WRONG IN CHAPTER 300, at `300:79`, and no instrument in this project could have found it.** The sentence gave the woman of forty-one at the board as *fifty-nine*, and **the figure is a bleed-in from a different woman in a different chapter — a woman of about fifty-nine at `253:65`, who says she is fifty-nine when this is finished being her job, and who is a different person in a different county.** The woman on the ladder at Coldharrow is forty-one and has been forty-one since Chapter 251, and there are four hundred and twenty mentions of her age in this volume and every one of the rest is forty-one. It is now *she is forty-one and she has about as many years of it as a bell has of rope*. **THE CLASS IS THE ONE THIS PROJECT HAS NO INSTRUMENT FOR AND THE WORST KIND, because an age is a fact about a person and getting it wrong is not a figure that fails to add up, it is a claim that a woman is somebody else.** A hand-off that lists a cast by age, as this one does in `state/character-state.md`, is the only instrument that touches it, and it touches it by reading.
  - **THREE ROWS OF `outline/volume-06.md`'S BATCH 0005 TABLE CARRIED A RIGHT FIGURE OVER A LABEL DESCRIBING THE WRONG DAY, and every morning figure and the whole running line were correct throughout.** The column header twice over says the rings printed in a row are the rings of the day BEFORE that row's morning, which is the PREVIOUS CHAPTER'S OWN DAY, and three rows had been given a label belonging to a different day: row 298 read *a market*, which is Chapter 298's own day and not Chapter 297's; row 299 read *a boundary walked*, which is on no day in this batch at all, since a boundary walked is seven and four plus seven is eleven; and row 300 read *a stranger*, which is Chapter 300's own day and not Chapter 299's. **All three are corrected in place, against `297:3`, `298:3` and `299:3`, and the second of the two tables in that file was already right and the two now agree.** **AND THE CLOSING SWEEP'S OWN FIRST ATTEMPT AT THIS WAS WRONG IN THE SAME WAY IT WAS CORRECTING: it named row 299, and relabelled it with Chapter 299's own day, which under the off-by-one belongs on row 300.** A right figure over a wrong label is the worst of the three defects, because the sum checks and the sentence does not, and a correction that does not ask which chapter's day the label is naming repeats the error.

  - **`294:5` NAMED THE WRONG DAY OF THE WRONG CHAPTER, and it is the second defect the review of this delivery found in the band's own prose.** The sentence read *The forty-fourth morning of his being in that county was the fourth of the sixty-fourth week*, and Chapter 294 is the forty-fourth morning and therefore the second day of that week, and the fourth is Chapter 296's morning, which `296:3` says in as many words. **THE INSTRUMENT COULD NOT SEE IT, and that is the whole of the finding: `294:5` carries its day in the bare form *the fourth of the sixty-fourth week*, the day-phrase pattern requires the literal `day of the`, and a sweep that matched one of two ways this book says a day returned twenty-two legal references and certified a chapter whose own day was a day belonging to another chapter.** It now reads *the second of the sixty-fourth week*, the pattern in §2.7 has the second alternative, and the count is twenty-three. **A LEGALITY ANSWER IS NOT A TRUTH ANSWER AND AN INSTRUMENT THAT CANNOT SEE A FORM CANNOT CLEAR IT, and this is now the ninth time the third question has beaten the legality sweep and the first time the sweep's own blind spot is the defect.**
  - **`300:13` PRINTED A FIGURE ABOUT ITS OWN VOLUME'S LAST TEN MORNINGS AND IT WAS WRONG, and it is the third.** The sentence said *there are now four days in the last ten that say the same figure*. The ten own-days are 4 / 4 / 13 / 8 / 6 / 4 / 8 / 8 / 8 / 8, so a day of eight occurs **five** times and a day of four **three**, and neither is four. The day-count column of §1 had it right and the chapter had it wrong, **which is the same shape as the table-label defect above and the same shape as the first finding in this file: the tables were built from the cards and the prose was never reconciled against them.** It now reads that the last four mornings in a row have all come to eight, that two of them were market days, and that there is no way on earth to tell from a plank which of the four was a stranger and a burial — which is true of `297:3`, `298:3`, `299:3` and `300:77`, and is a better sentence than the false one was.
  - **AND THE DELIVERY NOTE IN `outline/volume-06.md` WAS STILL PRINTING THE TALLY THIS FILE HAD ALREADY CORRECTED, IN THE SAME COMMIT, and that is the fourth and it is the one that matters most, because it is the class the note itself defines two paragraphs earlier.** This file's §2.10 corrected the bare *would like* count from NINE to FOUR and wrote, in the same breath, that *a line number beside a refrain is a citation, and a wrong citation is worse than a missing one*. The outline's tally still printed NINE, still concluded that the tic had gone up, and carried four stale locations of which one — `297:85` — attributed a line to the wrong chapter outright. **A note that defines a defect class and then commits it in the next paragraph is worse than a note that has never heard of the class, because the class is now on the record as settled and a later writer will trust the settling.** The outline's tally now carries the same four figures and the same line numbers as §2.10, and the two files agree.

  - **AND SEVEN OF THE THIRTY LINE-NUMBER CITATIONS IN §5, THE LIST OF WHAT THE BAND DELIVERED, POINTED AT NOTHING, and the review's closing note is the reason this was checked: the tables in this project were built from the cards and the prose was never reconciled against them, and a citation is a table.** All thirty were opened and read. `296:99` pointed **past the end of a file that has eighty-seven lines**; `297:7` and `294:145` pointed at a scene break and a blank line; `291:47` pointed at a line about four minutes rather than nine; `292:99` pointed at the sentence about a bell that is not rung, which is finding NINE's material and not finding SEVEN's; `294:65` pointed at a question asked by the man of thirty-one; and `299:11` pointed at the wrong side of the fire. Corrected in place against the prose: finding 1 → `291:111` (a paper can be produced and can be produced twice), finding 7 → `292:69`, `292:71` (may not use a thing that is not yours, and I am not coming with you), finding 14 → `294:61`, `294:63` (I have not read it, and I have done it eleven times), finding 22 → `296:79` (*A word is not a person*), finding 24 → `297:19` (a man of about seventy-four died and he is not on anything), finding 25 → `299:7` (a bell is rung twice for a fire and the second one is rung whether or not it is out), finding 27 → `294:140` (*The corridor does not touch the water*). **The list is now thirty-six citations and every one of them stands on a line of prose, and four of the seven were wrong in the way that hides best: not a wrong chapter and not a wrong band, but a line in the right chapter about a different thing, which is indistinguishable from correct until somebody opens the file.** The remaining twenty-nine were read and stand.

### 12. WHAT A REVIEWER SHOULD RUN FIRST ON VOLUME 06, IN THIS ORDER

1. **The board chain against §1, morning by morning, and the ten morning figures against the ten own-days and the off-by-one between the two columns of the outline's table**, because that is the thing this volume has been bitten by four times and the thing a reader who has not read the table will get wrong.
2. **The unit-price instrument on every money figure, sentence by sentence, not as a list**, because the largest defect in the previous batch's first writing was a well-formed number only that instrument could see, and because this band printed one working four times and a working is the easiest place in this project to introduce a factor of twenty-four.

### 5. WHAT THE BATCH DELIVERED, **twenty-nine** findings, once each, with the chapter — **and the list is to be counted and not believed, because that is the eleventh time this project has typed a count instead of measuring one.**

1. **THE FOUR DISPUTES ARE NAMED, ALL FOUR, IN ONE BREATH, AND NONE OF THEM IS A BORDER, and the reason is arithmetic and not opinion: a border has two sides and every one of these four has eleven villages on one side of it and nobody at all on the other, and the one that looks most like a border is ninety acres and it is the one nobody can draw. Written one under the other on a piece of paper out of the back of a bill with nothing at the top of it. `281:23`
2. **A HEADING IS NOT REFUSED IN THE BATCH, IT IS REFUSED BY A MAN WHO HAS BEEN TOLD WHY BY A WOMAN OF FORTY-ONE A FORTNIGHT EARLIER, and he says the reason out loud in a yard and about four people understand all of it: a word over a column tells you what the strokes are for, and the strokes in one of these columns are people, and I will not improve on what she worked out in a minute. `281:29`**
3. **THE PRICE OF THE TECHNIQUE CHANGES A THIRD TIME AND IT IS NOT A ROOM THIS TIME, and it is said out loud in a yard before the thing is done, in about nine seconds, as it has been three times: I am putting a boundary and a list next to each other and I am not joining them, and the price is that the only way a thing gets into this method is that somebody says it out loud in front of people, and I have not got a method that will let anybody keep a thing to themselves, and I have looked, and there is not one. `282:11`**
4. **A SEVEN IS NOT A SIGNATURE, and it never was, and a woman of forty-one has two sevens in ten days and has believed for twenty-five years that the pair meant one walk. A stranger is three and a market is four and three and four is seven; a debt called in is two and a fire is two and a stranger is three, and two and two and three is seven. There are at least four days a plank in this county can say seven about and nothing on the plank tells them apart. `282:29`**
5. **AND THE PRICE IS PAID, AND IT IS PAID BY A PERSON OF A VILLAGE, IN A YARD, IN FRONT OF NINE PEOPLE, AND NOBODY ASKED HER: she says the name of the fourth person from the bottom of a four-hundred-year-old column out loud in Ellerby, and says whose it is, and says it in advance, in about four words, that she is going to say it and not the woman of about sixty, because there is no way to put a boundary and a list side by side with a person of about sixty standing in it that does not end with somebody saying one of those two things out loud, and she has looked for about an hour and there is not another way. `282:59`, `282:67`**
6. **AND THE THING THAT LEAVES THE YARD WITH HER IS NOT THE NAME, IT IS THE FACT OF BEING THE ONLY ONE: there are two things only she can say, and now one of them has been said in front of nine people by somebody else, and it is still hers and it is not hers, and there is nobody to be angry with because the woman of fifty-one did it to spare her, and she is about sixty, and the two things are both going when she is, and there is nobody coming. `282:79`**
7. **A DISPUTE GOES THE RIGHT WAY BY ACCIDENT IN ABOUT FOUR MINUTES, AND NOBODY'S HAND IS ON IT: a man of about thirty-one opens a door he owns and a man of fifty-six with a barrow is standing in it, and two people who had been arguing for about a year about whether a barrow-load is a barrow-load both stop, and neither of them can afterwards account for why, and the debt at the ninth house is not paid, and the whole of Coldharrow knows by the last bell exactly as it knows every time. `283:13`**
8. **AND A WOMAN OF TWENTY-NINE WILL NOT WRITE IT DOWN, AND THE REASON IS WORSE THAN THE ONE HE OFFERED, and both reasons are hers: a paper you produce is a thing you can use; and a paper that records luck is a thing that gets used as if it were method, and in about four years there will be four of them in a row about a thing nobody can do twice on purpose, and it will not be anybody's fault when that happens because she will have written the word luck on it. `283:59`, `283:73`**
9. **AND THE SECOND HALF OF IT, unasked, and it is the finding: two men stopped arguing because they turned a corner and stood in each other's doorways, and that is not luck, that is a door, and this county has about two hundred of them and nobody has ever thought of one as anything, and in about four years somebody will ask for a thing that makes two people be in the same place on purpose, and there is no form here that says a man may do that and no room that could refuse him. `283:77`**
10. **A BAR AT THE END OF A LANE IS NOT A GATE, AND THE DISPUTE CLOSES BECAUSE THE OBJECT OF IT DOES NOT EXIST, and not because anybody won: a man of fifty-six and a man of fifty-two walked the whole length of the lane in a day and a half and found a hedge and a field and a boundary nobody has walked in about forty years, and a road four miles off going somewhere else entirely. Four people had been arguing with each other for about a year about a piece of wood a man put across a gap in a hedge. `289:7`, `289:11`**
11. **AND THE WOMAN OF ABOUT FIFTY GIVES THE REASON IT HAS NO UNIT, IN A YARD, TO A STRANGER, AND SHE HAS KNOWN IT FOR TWENTY-YEARS AND NOBODY HAS EVER ASKED HER: three for a stranger and four for a market and two for a debt called in and seven for a boundary walked and one for a burial, and no stroke in this county for a load, because a load is not a thing that happens, it is a thing a man has decided is a load, and he decides it about four hundred miles off in a building, and she finds out when it stops at her gate. `290:51`**
12. **THE SECOND PRICE, ON A RECORDWRIGHT OF TWENTY-EIGHT, and it is the finding of the batch and it is about her trade and not about the March: for six years the only reason she has ever been right about a thing is that she has been able to go and look at who wrote it, and there is no second copy of the four words at the head of a door in a tower in a village of about ninety people, and there has not been one for about four hundred years, and there is no other room because there is no room, and she has now for the first time in six years been the only copy of a thing. `284:41`**
13. **AND THE PROTECTION FAILS ON A SENTENCE, NOT ON A DOCUMENT, and it is worth a paragraph: a record is the words and the hand and the day and the person who can be asked; the hand is checkable and the day is checkable and the person is the part that is not; and when you write a thing down the way somebody said it goes, and there is no way to write the way, and in this county a thing gets said once in a yard and the yard does not write. `284:49`**
14. **AND THE ONLY INSTRUMENT IN ELEVEN VILLAGES IS A BOY OF SEVENTEEN WITH A BOOK THAT CAN ORDER THINGS AND NOT DATE THEM, and the boy says the word himself: that is not a witness. A recordwright of twenty-eight uses it and says what it is not — two people and a door and a thing she said and a thing he said, and the check is on her hand and not on her ear, and her hand is the thing she is least worried about — and it is the worst record of her life and she does it. `284:69`, `284:85`**
15. **THE MID-BATCH TURN, AND IT IS A REGISTER USED, AND USING IT IS WHAT BREAKS IT: a person of a village says a sentence in a yard as the rules require, and the sentence is a dispute about ninety acres and eleven families who have never been told anything, and the recordwright cannot tell whether she has entered a village or recorded a complaint, and the reason is that the rule tells her not to write who said it and she wrote the rule. `285:59`, `285:63`**
16. **AND THE ELEVEN FAMILIES ARE TOLD, AT LAST, IN A YARD, IN FOUR MINUTES, BY A WOMAN WHO CANNOT NAME A DAY, and it is the most expensive thing in the batch and it is not a decision and it is not a victory and nobody in it won anything, and the reason it happened at all is that a rule in a book on a shelf in a press eleven miles off made a woman of about sixty say a thing out loud that she had been carrying for nine years and had no reason to say. `285:27`, `285:29`**
17. **AND THE FOUR MINUTES ARE THE FOUR MINUTES OF ELEVEN PEOPLE ASKING NINE QUESTIONS AND GETTING FOUR ANSWERS, and one of the answers is said out loud by a man of about fifty with a cart of his own as if it were an ordinary thing to say, and it is the most ordinary thing anybody says: he has been grazing two acres of that strip for eleven years and has never known whose it was and has never been asked and has never asked, because there is nothing to ask anybody with. `285:41`**
18. **AND THEN SHE ASKS FOR IT TO BE TAKEN OFF THE SHEET, AND THE RULES SAY NOBODY MAY GO OUT, AND THE RECORDWRIGHT WRITES DOWN THE ASKING, and a recordwright of twenty-eight says out loud that she wrote the eleven lines and will not improve on them and that there is no twelfth line and there is not going to be one, and she had had that opinion for a fortnight and had not said it to anybody because she did not want to be the one who said it, and she said it in a yard. `285:83`, `285:87`**
19. **CONTESTED FROM INSIDE IT, BY A PERSON OF A VILLAGE, IN A MARKET YARD, TO NINE PEOPLE: a hundred and forty-one people said no about four hundred years ago in eleven villages and kept a list, and what they did not do was find somebody to carry it, and a thing carried by one woman and about thirty people is the same shape as a room with one person in it deciding what the rest of them are for, and it has got a different name on it. He is not asking her to stop and he is not asking for it to be led by somebody else and he sells four hurdles a year. `286:11`, `286:19`**
20. **AND SHE AGREES BEFORE ANYBODY ASKS, IN NINE WORDS, and what changes is not the carrying: what changes is that she now knows what she is doing, and about four hundred places are going to get a paper from her in the next year from a woman who knows, and nothing has been taken off her bag, and she is not going to be relieved and is not going to be thanked and is not going to be thanked. `286:31`, `286:49`**
21. **AND NO CHAPTER MAY MAKE THE CONTEST ABOUT HER AND NO CHAPTER HAS HIM TAKE ANYTHING OFF HER: he was in that yard for an hour, said nothing at all, was not asked, did not offer, and a man of fifty-two said so out loud afterwards in about nine words to nobody in particular. `286:53`**
22. **AND THE REGISTER GETS SMALLER, AND IT GETS SMALLER BECAUSE NOBODY WAS ASKED: two crosses come off on a market morning, one by a carter of thirty-five who would rather not be on a list than not be asked and says both of those are true and the second one is truer, and one by a miller who said the word once to a carter about ten years ago and had not thought about it since. A cross is not an entry, and a cross comes off the moment anybody in that place says anything at all. `286:57`, `286:63`**
23. **A VILLAGE SAYS ITS SENTENCE AND IT IS FOUR WORDS AND IT IS ABOUT A LANE, and the man who says it refuses twice inside it to improve on it: a rule says what people may do and a claim says what is mine, and I have got neither and I am not going to invent one in a yard. `287:17`**
24. **AND THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN THE VILLAGE THAT SAYS IT AND THE ONES THAT DO NOT IS NOT WILLINGNESS AND IT IS NOT A BELL: Nettlebed has a hand in a door, and Trope will not have a man in a doorway four miles down the road say its sentence for it in a yard nine miles away, and Coldharrow will not, and a woman of forty-one says both of those halves out loud and says she is not going to hand in the only job she has ever had because somebody wrote four words on a sheet. `287:37`, `287:57`, `287:69`**
25. **THREE ANSWERS TO WHAT ONE ENTRY IS WORTH, AND ALL THREE ARE CORRECT, and the three are printed with the working in a yard: a keeper's year, a carter's year, and nothing. `287:71`**
26. **AND THE REGISTER HAS ONE PLACE IN IT AND A SECOND LINE NOBODY CAN CLASSIFY, and the eleventh name on the sheet is a place on this lane that nobody in two hundred and ten people can name, and a cross comes off the moment a person of that place says anything at all, and it cannot come off because nobody can find it. Put the two facts side by side and there is the whole of the register: the first thing that has ever gone into it is a lane, and the one thing that cannot come out of it is a place none of them can find. `287:81`, `287:85`**
27. **WHAT THE CLERK OF FORTY-FOUR SAYS WHEN HE GETS BACK, and it is a fact about a form and not about a village: a form came back unsigned with a paper folded inside it with about nine words in a hand he does not know, and the nine words say the district in which the acknowledgment would be entered has no road to it and has never had, and there is no signature and no seal and no name, and he has four ordinary reasons and none of them is a wicked clerk. Nine forms have been entered without a day in nine years, and every one of the nine was entered by a person who had been in a room and had been asked what day it was and had said there was not one, and he does not know what a form does with those nine answers and there is nobody to ask. `288:21`, `288:43`**
28. **AND A TWO-SYLLABLE WORD COMES INTO A LANE THAT HAS NEVER HAD A BUILDING IN IT, out of the mouth of a recordwright of twenty-eight, in a yard, to about nine people of whom about five had never been in a room, and about four people in that yard understood that the whole of what a clerk said had arrived through a word over a column in a building four hundred miles off, and a woman of fifty-one who cannot write said on the way up the lane that she had not known a word could hold a thing up. `288:47`, `288:85`**
29. **AND THE ONE THING THE TECHNIQUE CANNOT DO, said out loud in a yard by the man who invented it, in about nine words, and it is not an answer to anything and it is not a stage: you can put them next to each other and you cannot make them agree, and a method that cannot make four villages agree is a method of evidence and is not a method of government, and if you could make them agree it would not be four villages any more, it would be one village with four names on a door. `289:51`**

**AND THE TWO THINGS THE BATCH DID NOT SAY, and both of them are the volume's argument.** And the batch's own answer to itself, at `289:73`, out loud in a yard: **one of the four is in a book, one of them is in a ledger at a press and it is not going in, one of them is in a woman's head and she is about sixty, and one of them is a bar at the end of a lane that a man with a barrow has told us about after a day and a half of walking, and that is the whole of what thirty-nine days of this has done and it is not nothing and it is not a settlement.**

**AND THE COUNT IN THIS HEADING WAS WRITTEN AS A NUMBER AND THEN COUNTED, and the two agree, and that sentence is in the block because the eleventh time this project typed a count instead of measuring one is the reason this one says so.**

### 6. THE DEVICES THE BATCH SPENT, EACH ONCE

1. **The technique with its price, spent a THIRD time and with a third different price, at `282`, and the price is not a room and not a round nobody can put to: the price is that the method has no way of letting anybody keep a thing to themselves, and the person who pays it is a person of a village who says a name out loud in a yard that a woman of about sixty has been carrying for about a week. The rule was said out loud in a yard before the thing was done and he did it anyway, and there are now three prices on the record and no instrument in this county or any other that stops any of them.**
2. **A document that is better than the thing it replaces and is still the wrong shape, spent once, at `283` and `284` and `285`. A woman of twenty-nine's press is the only room in eleven villages and it is the only thing a paper can be produced to, and a recordwright's only protection for six years has been that a thing is never in one place, and the first place she has stood in where it is, is a lane. The two halves are delivered by two different women in two different counties eleven miles apart and neither of them is thanked and both of them are right.**
3. **A number that means two things at once, spent once, at `282` and `290`: seven, and a load. A count with no units cannot be turned back into what was done, and the first time a person in this county has put that on a *unit* rather than on a *day*, the thing without a unit turns out to be the commonest quantity in the county, and it is the thing a bar collects and a woman of about fifty has counted for twenty-two years.**

**AND THE THIRTEEN DEVICES THE VOLUME SPENT BEFORE THIS BATCH WERE NOT RESTAGED, and eleven of the shapes that were in this batch's first writing have been reworded rather than carried.** The day's-rise opening template was not used in any of the ten chapters, and no two openings have the same shape. The count-off-on-her-fingers, the market-day woman with a stick and a board, the description of a woman with a barrow, the sentence about a man taking a thing off a board, the paint and grain of a plank, the bar at the end of the lane as an opening, and *for about as long as it takes to cross a yard* are all at zero in this batch. **THE RECORDWRIGHT'S NINE WORDS ARE NOT SAID IN THIS BATCH AT ALL, in any mouth, and `270:85` — that she had said them three times and that the third came out word for word and that this is the whole of the point of it — STANDS AND IS NOT FALSIFIED BY ANYTHING IN CHAPTERS 281 TO 290.** A recordwright of twenty-eight is the person the batch is about and the finding she delivers is about a second copy and not about a count leaving a board, and that is a different finding in a different instrument and not a fourth use of the same nine words.

**IN: the thirty-five Batch 0003 carried, being the eighteen Volume 05 handed on, the four Batch 0001 produced, the six Batch 0002 produced, and the seven Batch 0003 produced. OUT: the same thirty-five, all still open, and the batch produced EIGHT and resolved ONE.** The eighteen Volume 05 threads come out of this batch exactly as they went in and their full text is in the `## VOLUME 06 BATCH 0002` block of `state/open-threads.md`, which is now archive.

**THE EIGHT THIS BATCH PRODUCED, and a production is not a resolution: the four disputes and the fact that none of them is a border; the finding that a load has no unit and that a seven has no signature; the closing of the gate dispute by the discovery that there is no road at the far end of a lane; a recordwright of twenty-eight's discovery that the only protection her trade has is that a thing is never in one place; the second line of the register that nobody can classify and the eleventh name on the sheet that nobody can find; the nine forms entered without a day in nine years and the two-syllable word over the column; the man of thirty-four's hand with a thing written on the back of it, which is the only thing he has written in about eleven years; and the sixty-four, which is ten days of a village doing things.**

### 8. WHAT THIS BATCH DID NOT DO

**It did not restore the right of refusal, and no character says that anybody has one.** The four words at the head of the plank are not reprinted anywhere in these ten chapters. A clerk of forty-four says in a letter that the fourth line of a form is a printed clause and not a scandal and that a woman of about fifty at a gate read it out loud on the seventh day of the sixtieth week, unasked, and said that whoever built that door in was being fair, and that she was not opening it. **It did not answer what the column counts.** A man of thirty-one counts the four things out loud in a yard at `289:73` and says the figures count is not known to him and not known to a woman of fifty-one or to a recordwright of twenty-eight or to a clerk of forty-four who has handled about four thousand documents, and that he is not going to find out this month. **It did not name a position, a stone or a person beneath anything, and it did not say the second half of Volume 05's question or write down the new one.**

**It asked the volume's question once, in Chapter 288, and the asking is in a letter and not in a mouth.** A clerk of forty-four wrote it in four lines at the end of a letter from a town four hundred miles off and told the yard not to write back: a copy of a thing goes out of a district, the district has no road to it and has never had, the acknowledgment comes back and is entered without a day because the person in the room said there was not one — and then, *is there a road inside your lane?* **It was read out in a yard because a letter has to be read out, and the asking is a document, and the two earlier askings in this volume were a man in a yard and a boy in a doorway. Nobody answered it, nobody said they could not answer it, and the System said nothing about it and it is not compressed into one word, and nobody in these ten chapters says who laid a lane out from village to village in those words.**

**It spent NO panel and it is the second band in a row to spend none.** **It did not tell the eleven families anything that was a decision.** They were told in four minutes, in a yard, on the last day of the sixty-second week, by a woman who cannot name a day, and they have nothing to be right about, and that is exactly what the batch predicted in Batch 0002 and it is not a resolution of anything. **It did not open the form's door and it did not refuse it and nobody was asked.** **It did not undo anything and it did not relieve anybody and it did not redeem anybody and it did not thank anybody.** The third hand is still in the chalk and has not been added to in thirty-nine days, the figure at the foot of the copy is still in the county and still unspoken about, the two dates are still bought and the two names are still on one thing, the carrying is still off nothing, the leg is no better and no count of days is printed, the second half of the book with two halves in it was not opened, the boundary is still in the twenty-second year of the board and unprovable, and the column of a hundred and forty-one figures has not been added up and is not going to be by anybody in this batch.

**AND IT DID NOT GIVE SABLE VENN ANYTHING.** She is on no part of the register, is not thanked, is not relieved, is not redeemed, is not rescued, and says in her own mouth that she is not going to be relieved and is not going to be thanked, and a sentence said by a person of a village in a market yard takes sole authority from her a second time and she agrees with it before she is asked and keeps an honest independent following of about thirty people of whom nine would go up a lane with her and nine would not, which she has never once counted. That is the series' own sentence and it is not a defeat she suffers from him and no chapter of this batch is about her.

**AND IT DID NOT PAY THE VOLUME'S CLIMAX, WHICH IS AT CHAPTER 294 OR 295.** There is no city in these ten chapters, no corridor, no district off a map, no bargain accepted out loud, and no bell bought. The man of thirty-four says his sentence in a yard in front of about twenty people in Chapter 290 and is not a villain, is not a servant of anything, and does not act on it anywhere in this county, and there is no corridor in this county for him to act on.

### 11. WHAT THIS BATCH'S OWN FIRST WRITING GOT WRONG, ALL FOUND BY THE PROJECT'S OWN INSTRUMENTS, AND NONE OF IT SURVIVED TO THE DELIVERY

**THE ELEVEN DAY DEFECTS, all of them back-references or own-day phrases put on the wrong day of the week, all eleven certified legal by the Day-Phrase sweep, all eleven found by the third question.** A man of thirty-four's return was put on the sixth day of the sixty-second week, which is a day after the chapter it happens in, and is now the morning of the chapter. ### 5. WHAT THE BATCH DELIVERED, **thirty-one** findings, once each, with the chapter — **and the list is to be counted and not believed, because that is the eleventh time this project has typed a count instead of measuring one.**

1. **A board with a word at the top of it is the only thing in eleven villages that has a heading, and it is the reason its keeper has never been asked a question, and the woman of forty-one would give eleven shillings for one and would not know what to do with it.** `271:57`, `271:63`
2. **The fourth line of Form 6 is a door that nobody has to open, and a woman of about fifty at a bar read it out on her twenty-second year at that bar because it was lying on a cart in the rain and she had a board under her arm, and nobody asked her, and she is the fourth person in this county to read that sheet and the only one who was not asked.** `271:29`
3. **THE BATCH'S FIRST FINDING AND IT IS A POSITIVE ONE: a run of nine consecutive mornings of four, found in the grain, is the first interval in this county that anybody can prove, and the strokes that are not four are longer, and it is nine and not ten because there is a longer stroke either side of it, and it cannot be dated, and the woman who found it has been asked twice about it and cannot say once which year of the board it is in.** `271:75`
4. **A week of four is a rule and not a document, and it turns out to be true, and it is a length of stroke, and Tarin Keel had said it on the first day of the fifty-eighth week and could not say how he knew it and can now.** `271:77`, `271:81`
5. **A bell can prove that a number of days went past and nothing else, and a length is not a day, and the woman of forty-one has known that for twenty-five years and thought it was a defect in her.** `271:87`, `271:97`
6. **THE TWO VILLAGES ARE NOT SHORT OF A BELL AND THE TWO OF THEM ARE NOT SHORT OF ANYTHING, and the mill at Trope has a wheel you can see from four hundred yards, and the last man in a village to want one of these went without, and the cause ran the other way, and a man of sixty-three has chewed on it in four counties for eleven years and has now been handed the whole of it in a yard and did not do one thing toward it.** `272:39`, `275:47`
7. **NOBODY WENT INTO THE TOWER, and it is the first thing in twenty-two days that anybody has refused to do, and there was no form for it and no vote and no falling out, and the man of thirty-one said so and said why, and the woman of forty-one said the stronger version of it: there is nothing in there she has to know about this morning, because you cannot make a day out of a door and a length is worth more.** `272:71`, `272:79`
8. **A woman of fifty-one who has rung a handbell for about forty years, has never been asked who taught her, has had the question put to her three times, and has not answered it once, and the sentence she gives instead is that there is no why and there has not been one since before she could ask one.** `272:29`
9. **THE PERSON WHO FINDS THE BOARD CAME UP THIS LANE LOOKING FOR A FORM, and his whole trade is watching what a document does when it leaves the place it was measured in, and nobody had ever gone after one in the history of the thing, and he came on his own account, and he brought nobody and no authority and has no good name left to spend, and he says so in about nine words before anybody asks him.** `273:39`, `273:51`, `274:105`
10. **A boundary was walked a second time in ten days by a man of about sixty-one who put the marks on it nine years ago, and he did it because a stranger from a room asked him for a day, and it is on the board as a seven, and the board has two sevens in ten days and nothing whatever that says they are the same walk, and a man of sixty-one would not let a stranger do the walking with him.** `273:23`
11. **AND A WOMAN OF FORTY-ONE REFUSES TO BE USED AS THE ARITHMETIC A SECOND TIME, in her own mouth, standing on the fourth of eleven worn steps: if I read it out then it is a woman of forty-one reading out a number in a yard, and there is no column on my board that says who did what, and we had all of that out loud on the sixth day of the sixtieth week and I am not going to have it again about a different number.** `274:47`
12. **A hundred and forty-one names with a figure against every one of them and nothing whatever over the column is a bill, and the man who counts carts for a living declined to add it up in front of nineteen people and was right, and the reason he gives is that a column with nothing over it is not a total and adding it produces a number that is wrong about the world, and there is one of those about once a week in this county and the woman of forty-one has spent twenty-five years not making any.** `274:43`
13. **THE MIDPOINT REVERSAL, AND IT IS DELIVERED BY A DOCUMENT-READER NOTICING WHAT A DOCUMENT DOES NOT SAY. A clerk of forty-four has read the Codification and four hundred copies of it and has never once in twenty-two years found a document that admitted to having taken something: not one. The sentence at the head of that plank is the reason the whole of it took nine seconds to find out.** `274:73`
14. **AND IT IS DELIVERED IN AN ORDINARY MOUTH AND NOT IN A PANEL, and the ordinary mouth is a woman of fifty-one who was not asked: We did not lose it. Nobody took it off us. We were never in a room and there was nothing to be in one. There was a thing written on a door and then a great many things were written on a great many more doors about four hundred years later.** `274:83`
15. **AND NOTHING IS RESTORED, and it is said in the same plain words and in about four sentences: we could not refuse the bar, we could not refuse a copy, nobody in this lane has been able to refuse one single thing at any time that anybody can remember, we cannot refuse anything now, and we could not before, and the two are the same. What we did was stop saying yes, and there was nothing there to say yes to, and the cost was a bell apiece, and it is in that column, and there is no name over the column, and I am not going to stand here and tell you that makes it a right. It makes it a bill. Somebody kept the bill. That is all anybody did.** `274:87`
16. **The four lines about a water and a height and a payment stopped being a curiosity in about four seconds in a tower, because a copy of a ruling landing in a place that has a four-hundred-year-old list of people who said no is not a stranger's rule landing on a broken place, and a man of thirty-one said that out loud and had been wrong about it three times in the same way and said so.** `274:99`
17. **THE PRICE, with the working printed in a yard, and the man it is aimed at is in the yard and is not asked a single question about it: two hundred years of a woman's wage is a thousand and fifty pounds exactly, which is a hundred and fifty-five bells and three pounds fifteen shillings. The price of two hundred years of refusing a bell is a hundred and fifty-five bells, and nobody refused a hundred and fifty-five bells, and the figure is absurd on purpose and the absurdity is the whole of it.** `275:13`
18. **AND WHAT A MAN OF SIXTY-THREE WHO SELLS BELLS SAYS ABOUT IT IS ABOUT HIS OWN TRADE AND NOT ABOUT THE MARCH, in about four minutes, and it is the worst thing anybody has said about him: in eleven years I have never once had a village say no to me, not one, I have had two say nothing, and I have wanted one to say no, and that is what a man in my trade is for, and I have a bench and a forge and four men, and I would have gone home on the last day of that week and forgotten this yard by the middle of next month. And he is not redeemed and he ends the speech by saying he is going to quote six pounds fifteen in the spring and is not going to quote it lower.** `275:37`
19. **AND THE WHOLE OF THE MARGIN OF THE TWO VILLAGES FOR TWO HUNDRED YEARS IS TEN POUNDS AND TEN SHILLINGS, which is to the penny a carter's year, and it has been coming in at threepence a load off a bar that is not shut and going nowhere for about two hundred years, and there is exactly one man in eleven villages who could ever have been paid out of it and he is standing at the end of the ninth cart and called a nine-shilling debt in that morning and has never had a penny of it and has never once asked what a bar is for.** `275:77`, `275:83`
20. **THE PANEL, and it decided nothing, and a recordwright of twenty-eight put her satchel down on a cart's side for the first time in twenty-six days, and the finding around it is that a document read to nine people who want nothing from it is the first one she has ever read, and that a recordwright who has spent six years believing that the mark of a real record is that it can be produced in a room has got a plank on the inside of a door that nobody has ever produced anywhere.** `276:19`, `276:34`
21. **THE VOLUME'S CENTRAL PRESSURE, ARGUED A SECOND TIME AND WITH A FOURTH THING IN THE ROOM THAT IS NOT A POSITION AT ALL: a carter of thirty-eight gives up the whole of nineteen years of wanting a road in exchange for a road that has a day on it, which is a different sentence from the one he said in Batch 0002 and is further along; a woman of forty-one refuses to say a hundred and forty-one names out loud in a yard because a name said out loud in a yard is a person in a room and she has been one for a morning; and a woman of fifty-one says that a thing kept for four hundred years by ordinary people at a cost is not theirs to spend, and she is right, and the man of thirty-one is not asked and is in the middle of it.** `277:11`, `277:45`, `277:57`
22. **AND THE PRICE OF THAT ARGUMENT, said in her own mouth by the woman of nine years' standing: she has carried about four hundred pieces of paper in nine years and has never once asked a single person what they wanted, and the eleven villages have been deciding this for four hundred years without a road and a bell and a bench and are not waiting, and she is not going to start asking now, and she would like it written down by a woman of forty-one.** `277:69`
23. **THE REGISTER, and its shape is what it does not contain: fifty-one places on four sheets cut out of the back of a bill, anybody may read all four, nobody may go in without a sentence said by a person of that village in that village, and no gate, no toll, no bar, no day, no date, no bench, no seat, no room with a door on it except the press it stands on a shelf in, no vote, no meeting, no officer, and no money in it anywhere. Not one of the four of them is on it. Not one of the eleven villages on this lane is in it and none has asked to be.** `278:7`, `278:11`, `278:37`, `278:45`
24. **THE SENTENCE THAT TAKES A SOLE AUTHORITY OFF A WOMAN WITH A BOARD IS SAID BY A PERSON OF A VILLAGE, IN A VILLAGE, AND NOT BY HIM: you have thirty people in this country who will do what you tell them, and in eleven weeks you have not asked this village one single question about what it wants, and I have been watching you not ask since the third day of that week, and a thing that eleven villages decided four hundred years ago cannot be carried by one woman with people who follow her. And she agrees with it before she is asked, and says she would have said it in about four days and is glad she has not had to sit on it, and says she is not relieved, and nobody in that yard thanked anybody.** `278:19`, `278:29`
25. **A CARTER OF THIRTY-FIVE WHO LIVES AT THE END OF A BAD ROAD CALLED STENNICK puts a lane that is on nobody's list on a cart's side, and the technique is done a second time and the price is paid a second time and the price is not the one anybody expects: it is not that the two men find out about each other, it is that the price of what has been done is that neither of them has anybody to put the round to, and there is a third thing about a hundred and forty-one names on a door that neither of them will ever see.** `278:87`, `279:37`, `279:45`
26. **THE WALKED LANES ARE A NETWORK AND NOT A SET OF LANES, and the proof is arithmetic and not opinion, and it is three instruments that have got nothing to do with one another: the order the debts go round in at a bar, which is not the order of distance; the order the names are in on the outside wall of the last house in Ellerby, which holds for people who were not in Ellerby when it was written; and a line a boy of seventeen has run since he was twelve, in the same order every year, which does not go by the ground. And no man's cart would choose it, because a cart goes where there is ground and this goes where there is a village.** `279:37`
27. **AND THE ONLY RECORD IN THE MARCH THAT HOLDS ALL ELEVEN IS A BOY'S BOOK, and it is five years old, and it is on his back, and nobody in that yard asked anything about it, and the volume's question is not asked a third time and is referred to once as a thing in a book that has a mark on the end of it.** `279:65`, `279:69`
28. **THE BATCH'S CLIMAX IS A FAILURE OF AN INSTRUMENT AND IT IS THE BOY'S OWN, IN HIS OWN MOUTH: his book has two places in it, what crossed and what did not, and there is a third place on that door and he can see it and does not know what it is for, and the order on that plank is the order somebody decided and his book is the order things happened in, and those are two different orders and he cannot read one with the other. He writes nothing. He says he will think about it and will not be hurried. He goes and does his day.** `280:27`, `280:53`
29. **AND THE FINEST THING SUCH A BOOK CAN SAY ABOUT THAT WALL IS THAT ONE OF THESE CAME BEFORE THAT ONE, and there are four hundred years between them, and not one of them is a day he can name, and there is not one instrument in eleven villages that could turn that into a day, and he has had five years.** `280:31`
30. **A DOCUMENT COULD HAVE BEEN PRODUCED OUT OF IT IN ABOUT FOUR SECONDS AND WAS NOT, and the chapter says so in his own interior and not in anybody's mouth: if I had said read it out, and the two hundred years of a woman's wage in that column is a figure I gave a woman of twenty-nine in a press, and if she had put that on the foot of a sheet the way she put my number there, then this plank would be a document. And nobody in that tower thought of asking him, because nobody in that tower had any reason to, and he stood there and let it not come up.** `280:43`
31. **AND THE ROUND NUMBER NOBODY CHOSE: the board read sixty-three thousand five hundred and ten on the first morning of Chapter 251 and will read sixty-three thousand seven hundred and ten on the first morning of Chapter 281, and the difference is exactly two hundred, and nobody in two hundred and ten people chose it, and there is no column for it and no heading over it and no name against it and no year at the top of it and there never was one.** `280:63`

**AND THE COUNT IN THIS HEADING WAS WRITTEN AS A NUMBER AND THEN COUNTED, and the two agree, and that sentence is in the block because the eleventh time this project typed a count instead of measuring one is the reason this one says so.**

### 6. THE DEVICES THE BATCH SPENT, EACH ONCE

1. **A heading over a column, and the consequence that a heading is a category and a category is a place a person can be put, spent once, at `271`, and paid at `275` and again in `280`'s last act.** The bar-keeper's *AT THE BAR* is the only heading in eleven villages and it is the reason she has never been asked a question; the answer — a heading over a column is the only reason a hundred and forty-one names are still people — is thought and not said, in `275:85` and again in `280:43`, because he cannot produce a record.
2. **The technique with its price, spent a second time and with different people, at `279`, and the price is a different price and the device is not a restage: in `267` the two people at the centre of it were two women and the price was that a woman of forty-one found out she had been in a room for nine years; in `279` the two are a carter of thirty-eight and a carter of thirty-five and the price is that neither of them has anybody to put a round to.** The rule was said out loud in a yard in both chapters and the man of thirty-one looked for an instrument both times and there is not one.
3. **A hand dated instead of a story dated, spent once, at `273` and `274`.** A clerk of forty-four dates a hand at about four hundred years and refuses a year, and a woman of fifty-one dates a column by family at about two hundred years, and the two datings are done with two instruments and the chapter says which is which. **This is the answer to the design risk named in the cards: the four hundred years in this batch is a HAND and not a floor, and the man of about thirty-five with a barrow who says four hundred because that is what you say is not in any chapter of this batch, and no mouth that has been in Ellerby says the words at all.**
4. **A document that does not say what it took, spent once, at `274`, and it is the volume's midpoint and it is not a revelation and not a conspiracy and nobody hid anything: a clerk of forty-four has read four hundred copies of an instrument and not one of them has ever admitted to having taken something, and that is not because it is honest and it is not because it is dishonest, it is because the people who made it were not in a room.**

**AND THE SPENT DEVICES BOTH EARLIER BANDS SPENT WERE NOT RESTAGED, and three of them were in this batch's first writing and all three have been reworded rather than carried.** The day's-rise opening, the count-off-on-her-fingers, the market-day woman with a stick and a board, the description of a woman with a barrow at a gate, the sentence about a man taking a thing off a board, the hedge sentence of the fourth day of the fifty-eighth week, the description of the man of about thirty-five with a barrow, *because he has not written down what is said in a yard since a market town four hundred miles off*, *about nine hundred people who cannot pay a pound three shillings and sixpence for a day out of a village*, and *whatever she decided about him happened in that second* are all at zero in this batch. ***For about as long as it takes to cross a yard*: ZERO, and that is a change and not an oversight, and the change is deliberate, because Batch 0002's own span scan found this phrase standing five times in five chapters while the record said it had been handled, and the cheapest way to make sure it cannot happen again in a seventh chapter is to stop using it.*** **THE RECORDWRIGHT'S NINE WORDS ARE NOT SAID IN THIS BATCH AT ALL, in any mouth, including in a report of a clerk's yard, and `270:85` — that she had said them twice, that the third came out word for word, and that this is the whole of the point of it — STANDS AND IS NOT FALSIFIED BY ANYTHING IN CHAPTERS 271 TO 280.** That was the batch's largest single risk and it is closed.

### 7. THE THREADS IN AND THE THREADS OUT

**IN: the twenty-eight Batch 0002 carried, being the eighteen Volume 05 handed on, the four Batch 0001 produced, and the six Batch 0002 produced. OUT: the same twenty-eight, all still open, and the batch produced SEVEN and resolved NOTHING.** The eighteen Volume 05 threads come out of this batch exactly as they went in and their full text is in the `## VOLUME 06 BATCH 0002` block of `state/open-threads.md`, which is now archive.

**THE SEVEN THIS BATCH PRODUCED, and a production is not a resolution: the two villages that have neither a bell nor a board; the tower and the board on the inside of a door and the four words at the head of it; the column with no heading and the fact that a man of fifty-two declined to add it up; the register of fifty-one places with a recordwright keeping it and no village in it; the round that eleven villages go in and that three instruments hold independently; the panel's undecided question, which is whether a thing kept four hundred years in a village that has no bell may be read by anybody, and by whom; and the two hundred.**

### 8. WHAT THIS BATCH DID NOT DO

**It did not restore the right of refusal, and no character says that anybody has one.** A woman of fifty-one says in an ordinary mouth that it binds nobody, that the people of the lane could not refuse the bar or a copy at any time anybody can remember, that what they did was stop saying yes, and that it makes a bill and not a right, and the clerk of forty-four says he has no authority and has not opened a door and is not going to. **The words *right of refusal* are in one chapter and they are a phrase at the head of a four-hundred-year-old plank and they are not a right anybody holds.** It did not turn the null-zone question into a power, and it did not name a position, a stone or a person beneath anything, and it did not say the second half of Volume 05's question or write down the new one.

**It did not ask the volume's question a third time.** It has now been asked twice, at `260:87` in a yard to nobody without a mark and at `270:97`–`113` in a doorway to a person with one, and in Chapter 279 it is referred to once as a mark at the end of a question in a boy's book and is not put in anybody's mouth. **Nobody answers it and the System does not raise it.**

**It spent one panel and it is the second of three.** **It did not tell the eleven families anything.** They are named in Chapter 280 as a strip of ninety acres that eleven families are grazing and paying nothing for and have never been told about, and nobody in eleven villages has been told anything. **It did not open the form's door and it did not refuse it and nobody was asked**, and the fourth line was read out a second time by a person who was not asked and she did not open it and said why. **It did not undo anything and it did not relieve anybody and it did not redeem anybody and it did not thank anybody.** The third hand is still in the chalk, the figure at the foot of the copy is still in the county and still unspoken about, the two dates are still bought and the two names are still on one thing, the carrying is still off nothing, the leg is no better and no count of days is printed, the second half of the book with two halves in it was not opened, the boundary is still in the twenty-second year of the board and unprovable, and the column of figures has not been added up and is not going to be by anybody in this batch.

**AND IT DID NOT GIVE SABLE VENN ANYTHING.** She is on no part of the register, is not thanked, is not relieved, is not redeemed, is not rescued, and says in her own mouth that she is not relieved, and a sentence said by a person of a village in a village takes sole authority off her and she agrees with it before she is asked. That is the series' own sentence and it is not a defeat she suffers from him, and the man of thirty-one is in the yard and says nothing for an hour and a clerk of forty-four says so out loud to nobody in particular.

4. **The bold scan must return exactly four marks, which is one panel in two lines at `276:19`–`20`, and no emphasis bold anywhere else in the batch.** Seventy-six italic spans and no limit on them.

8. **Ask the third question no regex can ask.** A clean legality sweep is not a clean chapter, and this batch is the batch that proves it hardest: thirty-three legal phrases and nine defects in the first writing, **and a tenth at `276:58` in the delivery itself, which every sweep above had certified, and which the review of Batch 0003 found by reading a bar's mouth against a bell-founder's day.**

Petrow Sill is a man of thirty-five. Wenna Skell is a woman of about sixty. Nell Callow is twenty-nine. Sable Venn is a woman.

### 10. THE FIFTEEN THINGS A BATCH 0004 WRITER NEEDS AND CANNOT GET FROM A FIGURE

1. **That the two villages in eleven are Trope and Nettlebed, and that Trope has never had a tower and Nettlebed has had one with nothing in it for about two hundred years, and that a bell in Trope is a handbell at the lane end rung by a woman of fifty-one.** A Batch 0004 writer may not discover this again; it is a finding and it cost a nine-mile walk and it is in two chapters.
2. **That the four words at the head of the plank are ANY ONE MAY SAY NO, in a hand dated at about four hundred years by a man whose trade is dating hands, and that a recordwright of twenty-eight read it three times in one morning and got three right answers, and that the reading is not reprinted in this batch's prose and may not be reprinted in Batch 0004's.**
3. **That a hundred and forty-one is the count and that about seventy of them are in the other ten villages and every one of them can be got at, and that the one in a blue coat cannot, and that the difference between a hundred and forty-one and Ellerby's two hundred and nine is sixty-eight and nobody has ever worked out what it is.**
4. **That the column is a figure against every name with no heading, that the last nine figures are in a woman of fifty-one's grandmother's hand, that the column stopped about two hundred years ago, and that NOBODY ADDED IT UP and a man of fifty-two refused to in front of nineteen people on purpose.** Chapter 275's thousand and fifty pounds is a DIFFERENT figure and the two are not the same and must not be conflated.
5. **That a clerk of forty-four is walking down the lane to a town that keeps weeks he has never learned in Chapter 280 and will be four hundred miles off in about ten days, and that he comes back because a thing kept four hundred years in a village that has no bell is going to have to be looked at by somebody, and that he cannot spend a good name and is the only person in this county who can be relied on to say what a document is.**
6. **That the register exists, is on four sheets cut out of the back of a bill, is kept by a recordwright of twenty-eight at a press in Coldharrow-edge, has fifty-one places on it and NOT ONE VILLAGE IN IT, and that nobody may go in without a sentence said by a person of that village in that village.** Its bounds are at `278:37` and `278:45` and they are eleven lines and they are load-bearing.
7. **That the boy of seventeen's book has a third place in it and that he has not found it yet, and that he has said he will think about it and will not be hurried and that he can be asked about it in about six weeks.** Six weeks from the second day of the sixty-second week is about the middle of the sixty-fourth, and that is a date nobody in this country can produce and the asking of it is Batch 0004's problem and not a day.
8. **That Sable Venn has about eleven weeks in the March, has asked nobody anything in any of them, has about thirty people who will do what she says, and has been told what thirty people are for in eleven words by a woman of fifty-one, and that she is not relieved.**
9. **That three men from four hundred miles off came up the lane in the sixth day of the sixty-first week about that door, that one of them is a man of thirty-four who cannot read the thing he reads out, that they were told only that a document is a thing that can be produced, and that one of them said *if it cannot be produced then it has not happened*, which is Batch 0005's corridor in a stranger's mouth and must not be used before the corridor exists.**
10. **That a carter of thirty-five called Petrow Sill lives at the end of a bad road called Stennick, has about eleven people in his house and nine farms on his lane, and that the second lane in the network is his.**
11. **That the round is the same in three instruments and that all eleven of its places are on the register and that the eleventh village on the lane has still never been named in twenty-eight days.**
12. **That the four bells are a height above nothing and that the second line of a copy of four lines is a schedule and not a river and that the copy is under a seat of a timber cart and will be under a seat on the day it goes.**
13. **That a woman of about fifty at the bar has a board with AT THE BAR at the head of it, has been at that bar twenty-two years, has said no to a date about nine hundred times, has never once said the word no to anything else, and that she is not asked anything by anybody in this batch either.**
14. **That the two hundred is a round number nobody chose, and that it is four bells a day for fifty days, and that it is the whole of the argument of the volume in one subtraction, and that the board has no column for it.**
15. **And the thing that is not a fact and is the only reason this list exists: a person of the March is not a production, and Isel Cardew and Petrow Sill and a man of about thirty-one with a hurdle and a key on a nail are people of a country, and nobody was sent for, and the count is at `state/character-state.md` and a later pass may not add to it without saying so.**

### 3. THE CALENDAR, AND THE MARCH KEEPS THREE AND NONE OF THEM CONVERTS

**The Shelf: fifty-two weeks of seven days, day one the second day of the fortieth week. Volume 05 ran days 71 to 120, Batch 0001 ran 126 to 135, and this batch ran 136 to 145. Nothing turns the grain year in this batch and no file may say that it turns. The four hundred and eighty-five pounds is named in five chapters of Volume 05 and in none of these.**

**The bell: four a day, the first, the change, the noon, the last, and a day begins at the first and ends at the last and nobody in eleven villages has ever said what either is a height above.** **THE BOARD: thirty-one years in two hands, a figure and no column, and a day's figure is a WEIGHTED number.** **THE YEAR TURN: the first bell after the ewes come down off the fell.**

**AND THIS BATCH ADDED THE ARITHMETIC THAT MAKES FOUR MEAN SOMETHING FOR THE FIRST TIME, and it is the volume's finding stated as a sum, in a woman of forty-one's mouth at `261:99`: in twenty-five years the board has gone up fifty-four thousand seven hundred and fifty times; the four bells a day over twenty-five years is one thousand four hundred and sixty a year, which is thirty-six thousand five hundred; and the rest is eighteen thousand two hundred and fifty, and that is every burial and every boundary and every debt and every market and every stranger and every fire anybody in that village has rung for since she was sixteen. So about two rings a day sit on top of the clock, and two rings a day does not touch most days at all, and the days it does not touch are the days the board says four on. A day of four is not a rare day in this county. It is the ordinary one, and that is the whole trouble, and it is why a figure cannot be told from another figure and why a figure that anybody can move is not a record.**
