12. **THE NUMERIC HEDGE, WHICH IS NOT A REFRAIN AND IS THE BIGGEST THING IN THE BOOK, AND THIS IS THE FIGURE THE BAND WAS MEASURED AGAINST, AND THE BAND IMPROVED AND IS STILL NOT CLEAN.** The word count beside it is `len(re.findall(r"[A-Za-z’'\-]+", text))` OVER THE **WHOLE FILE, HEADING LINE INCLUDED**, and that method is the one declared at §3.12 of the Batch 0003 block and is not changed here. Pattern `about\s+(?:a\s+|an\s+)?(?:one|two|three|four|five|six|seven|eight|nine|ten|eleven|twelve|thirteen|fourteen|fifteen|twenty|thirty|forty|fifty|sixty|seventy|eighty|ninety|hundred)\b`, case-insensitive, at file level and not line level, per chapter and in total: **NINETY-TWO ACROSS THE TEN FILES, by chapter 8 / 2 / 6 / 13 / 14 / 9 / 8 / 6 / 10 / 16, in TWENTY-ONE THOUSAND SIX HUNDRED AND THIRTY-NINE WORDS, WHICH IS ONE IN EVERY TWO HUNDRED AND THIRTY-FIVE.** **THE FIRST WRITING OF THIS BAND WAS TWO HUNDRED AND TWENTY-ONE AND ONE HUNDRED AND TWENTY-NINE INSTANCES WERE CUT BY HAND, AND THE RULE THAT PRODUCED THE CUT IS THE ONE DECLARED AT §2: KEEP `about` ONLY WHERE IT QUALIFIES THE AGE OF A PERSON. THE WHOLE OF WHAT IS LEFT IS THAT, AND THE FIGURES THAT WERE CUT WERE HOURS AND MINUTES AND YEARS AND COUNTS OF PEOPLE, WHICH IN THIS BOOK ARE THINGS A PERSON MADE AND CAN BE ASKED ABOUT.** **THE TARGET OF UNDER ONE HUNDRED AND TWENTY-FIVE IS MET AND THE BAND IS BETTER THAN THE THREE BEFORE IT AND IT IS NOT CLEAN AND MUST NOT BE REPORTED CLEAN: Batch 0001 was two hundred and six in twenty-two thousand seven hundred and seventy-six words, one in every one hundred and ten; Batch 0002 was eighty-eight, one in every two hundred and fifty-three; Batch 0003 was one hundred and eighteen in twenty-two thousand four hundred and fifty-nine words, one in every one hundred and ninety, and the rate of the case-insensitive count and the rate of the case-sensitive count were different and both were printed; this band is ninety-two, one in every two hundred and thirty-five.** **AND THE CONSEQUENCE, WHICH A LATER BAND SHOULD BE TOLD: the prose is now tighter and the ages are now exact where they were not, and the cost of the cut was that this county's towns, lanes and kitchen tables are described in flat counts instead of hedged ones, and a reviewer who thinks that has cost the book its texture should say so, because it is the one thing in the reduction that was not obviously a gain.**
13. **The other two habits, measured because they are the same disease.** *Man of thirty-one*: **TWENTY-TWO**, against Batch 0003's twenty-four, Batch 0002's twenty-five and Batch 0001's twenty-eight, **so the line has been thinned for a seventh consecutive band and the thinning was done with *stranger* and with pronouns and not with rewrites.** Italic spans, pattern `\*[^*]+\*`: **FORTY-NINE**, by chapter 6 / 3 / 5 / 5 / 5 / 3 / 5 / 7 / 5 / 5, against Batch 0003's fifty, Batch 0002's fifty and Batch 0001's fifty-seven. **The first writing was ninety-one and forty-two were cut by hand, and every one of the forty-two was a span in the narrator's voice, because the band declares italic for one thing only, which is a thing somebody said in their own words that the chapter then refuses to explain.** The remaining forty-nine are all in a mouth.
14. **THE CROSS-BAND FIGURE, WHICH IS THE ONE A LATER PASS WILL QUOTE.** The four delivered bands of Volume 07 together run **FOUR HUNDRED AND FOUR IN EIGHTY-EIGHT THOUSAND AND SEVEN HUNDRED AND SEVEN WORDS, one in every TWO HUNDRED AND TWENTY** (the first three bands' figures are inherited from the Batch 0003 block at its §3.14 and are not re-measured here; the fourth is this band). **The trend of four bands is DOWN and the rate is now better than any of the three before it, and the honest reading is that the fall of a third that Volume 07's first band bought did not hold for two bands and has been bought back by a mechanical rule in the fourth, and a later band should be told that the rule works and that it is a rule and not a reading of the country.**
15. **AND THE FIGURES THIS BAND GOT RIGHT THE FIRST TIME:** the board chain closed on the first writing and both ways, the ten morning figures are in the right three chapters and in words and every one of the ten own days is derivable from the seven weights, `**` is at zero in the delivery, the panel count is zero, the System count is zero, `cannot read` is zero, `first witness` is zero, `anchor` is at zero, the Self-arrived class is zero, the money is nothing at all, **the round number is not noticed by anybody and nothing is built on it**, and the three things this band exists for all happened on the page: he tried to carry one of the six and could not, a man of fifty-two's past was used once and not resolved, and a boy of seventeen's book read an order that a document cannot.

### 4. THE MONEY AS DELIVERED, AND IT IS NOTHING, AND THAT IS THE FINDING AND NOT AN OMISSION

**THIS BAND PRINTED NO MONEY FIGURE OF ANY KIND.** Not a table figure, not a unit, not a product, and not a difference. Measured sentence by sentence: the strings *three pence a load*, *fifteen pounds fifteen*, *four thousand eight hundred*, *nine thousand six hundred*, *four hundred and eighty-five*, *threepence*, *six and fifteen*, *one and ten*, *five and five*, *eighteen pence*, *ninepence* and *Wenlock* are each at **ZERO** over the ten chapters.

**AND THAT IS THE BAND'S MONEY, AND IT IS SPENT NOW, AND IT MAY NOT BE SPENT AGAIN IN BATCH 0005.** What this band needed a price for was a levy, a sheet, a boundary, a load and a wage, and it went and asked a person of a place about all five, and the answer in every case was that there is no price on it in this country. The man of thirty-four who reads things out for a living says in Chapter 333 that there is no sheet in the county and no scrivener within nine miles of a smithy. The woman of about thirty-four at a bar says in Chapter 338 that there is nothing in the county that lets a person refuse a thing that costs nothing, which is the only free thing in this band and the price of it is that she cannot say no. **THE FIGURE THE B3 REPAIR LEFT OPEN — NOBODY IN THAT MARKET TOWN HAS EVER WRITTEN DOWN THE NUMBER OF LOADS IN A YEAR, AND THE HONEST VERSION OF THE ARRANGEMENT BEGINS WITH A MAN WRITING A YEAR ON A SLIP — WAS HAD AND REFUSED IN CHAPTER 340, AND IT WAS HAD FROM A PERSON OF THAT PLACE, STANDING NEXT TO HIS OWN BAG, AT A CROSS, IN A LANE, AND IT IS THE ONE PERMITTED REFERENCE TO THE SLIP IN THIS BAND AND IT IS SPENT.** He says there is a number on a slip on a shelf in a back room four days up this lane, that it is not written down anywhere in that county and it is in no hand in it, that somebody has to write down a year of loads, that it is about a week of a clerk's work, and that there is no clerk in that county and nobody there has anybody to do it. **He gives neither figure and nobody asked him to. A BATCH 0005 CARD MAY NOT REPEAT THAT REFERENCE AND MAY NOT NAME EITHER SLIP FIGURE.**

### 5. THE BAND: THE DELEGATION, THE MAN OF FIFTY-TWO, AND THE BOY OF SEVENTEEN

**IT PAID THE BAND'S THREE THINGS, AND ALL THREE ARE ON THE PAGE, AND `outline/volume-07.md:76` IS THE AUTHORITY THAT THEY ARE THE THREE.**

1. **HE TRIES TO CARRY ONE OF THE SIX HIMSELF AND CANNOT, AND THE REASON IS NOT A LEG AND NOT A DISTANCE.** Chapter 334, in a kitchen, in front of nine people, and it is the only time in thirteen days he tried anything in a room. **A boundary is four hundred yards of hedge walked in nine days by eleven names of whom nine come, and there is nothing on it that is a fact except the hedge and the nine days and the coming, and a man who carries it is a man who has to be there on nine mornings, and the ninth morning is the fifth day of the walk and he is going to be standing at a bridge with one rail on it.** And Chapter 336, on a dry morning on a rise behind eleven houses, in the open: **he stands in the line for the length of a load going over and the field does not know, and the stopping is not a refusal and not a door and not a form. A thing that is kept alive by nine people turning up in the rain cannot be carried by the eleventh person who turns up because he decided to.**
2. **HE LEARNS TO DELEGATE, AND THE PRICE IS A PERSON IN A RECORD, AND HE DOES IT DELIBERATELY AND SAYS SO.** Chapter 338, in a lane behind a bar, on the eighty-eighth morning. **The whole price is said out loud BEFORE the asking, in about a minute, and the second half of it is the half he has no better way to put: you cannot say no, because he has come eleven miles with nothing to offer and has used that, and a refusal requires a thing being offered. She said the word *go on*.** He asks her to carry one sentence to a person of another place. He says it out loud first and it is wrong in two places and he says it anyway, because a sentence about a yard that does not contain the person whose yard it is can be said in a market street to anybody and about anybody. **She says it in her own mouth and it is shorter and it is worse and it has the water in it that a stranger would not have said, and it took her eleven seconds and she did not look at him once. And then she says the part he had not priced: she is going to say it at a cross, in the open, at about the second hour, because that is where the people are, and not in a yard, and the reason she gives is that she is not going to be the one person in this country who says an important thing quietly and is never asked about it again.** **That is the price of the technique in its worst form in this band and it was arrived at by a person of a place and not by him, and the woman of about sixty-one in that market town is going to hear a stranger's voice in a sentence about her own yard in a market street, four days later, in front of people, and does not know where it came from. HE IS ON THE OTHER SIDE OF IT FOR THE FIRST TIME IN HIS LIFE AND HE WAS IN A KITCHEN THREE MILES UP A LANE ON THE SIXTY-FOURTH MORNING WHEN A WOMAN OF ABOUT FIFTY-EIGHT SAID NO TO HIM IN NINE WORDS AND HE STOOD AT A GATE FOR AN HOUR, AND THE THING THAT HAPPENED TO HER HAPPENED TO HER BECAUSE OF HIM.**
3. **TARIN'S PAST IS USED ONCE AND IS NOT RESOLVED.** Chapter 332, at a gate in the Briar March, at about the seventh hour, in a counting. **He is not asked to be there, he does not say so, he does not offer, and he was not asked anything.** He says one true sentence in the middle of a count, out loud, to a stranger: *there was a gate with a levy behind it once, a levy on loads, and the loads were counted by a man who was not paid, and there is a dead man in the fourth line, and that is all I am going to say about it and you did not ask me and that is the only reason I have said it.* **He stops there and does not go one step further. THE PROTAGONIST HAD THE QUESTION READY AND DID NOT ASK IT, AND HE HAD ASKED IT ONCE, BADLY, FOUR DAYS UP A LANE, ON THE FIFTY-SIXTH MORNING, AND IT HAD NOT BEEN ANSWERED, AND HE SAID IN A LANE ON THE EIGHTIETH MORNING THAT HE WAS NOT GOING TO ASK IT AGAIN AND HE DID NOT ASK IT.** His answer to *what were you the only person in* is not given and may not be given in this volume. The dead man in the fourth line stays dead and the eleven feet stay off the settlement and the second notice stays unpaid, and **no figure is printed.**
4. **BRAM'S BOOK READS AN ORDER THAT A DOCUMENT CANNOT.** Chapter 335, in a kitchen, in front of nine people, in his own mouth, **and nobody had asked him and there is no form in this country that says a man may ask a boy of seventeen a question about a book, and it took him nine seconds to start.** *Put them in an order and let each one of them say who comes next. That is the only thing anybody has proposed about the six in a month and a man who reads things out said it in a yard and nobody agreed and nobody disagreed, and it is the only thing that works, and a book can order things and cannot date them and I have never been able to make it do a date and I have stopped trying.* **The order is not a list of places, it is a round of turns, and it goes round and every one of them says who is after them, and if a person will not say then it stops at them and that is the answer. He reads out the round and stops for about four seconds at the seventh turn and says that the woman of about seventy-four says a person that nobody in eleven villages has counted, and that he is not going to read a name out of it because there is not one.** Then he says the two things he is not going to be asked about before anybody can ask them: there is a question in the book with a mark on the end of it that nobody has ever answered, and there is a third place he can see and has never been able to make out. **The man of about sixty-three opened his mouth and the boy put two fingers on the cover and the man shut his mouth, and that is the only time in this band that question came within a foot of being asked. BOTH ARE STILL IN THERE AND NEITHER IS SPENT.** A woman of about fifty-one who cannot write then says in nine words that a thing that has to be held in six places at once is a hearing, and that a book is the only thing in eleven villages that can put six things in an order and the only thing in eleven villages that cannot say when. **NOBODY THANKED THE BOY, HE DID NOT WANT TO BE, AND THE LAST THING THE MAN OF THIRTY-ONE SAID TO HIM WAS NOT A REWARD.**

**AND THE BAND'S OTHER FINDING, WHICH IS THE ONE NO INSTRUMENT CAN ASK, AND IT IS THE ANSWER TO THE CARD THAT ASKED IT.** When he delegates one of the six to a person of that place, does that person acquire a want they did not have — and can the chapter show the want arriving without the narrator saying a want arrived. **YES, AND THE CHAPTER SHOWS IT, AND IT ARRIVES IN SOMEBODY ELSE'S MOUTH FORTY EIGHT HOURS LATER AND HE IS NOT IN THE CHAPTER.** At Chapter 338 the woman of about thirty-four wants nothing and is about to be asked for nothing. By Chapter 340 a man of about thirty with a cart and a beast, who is one of the six and who was not asked to carry anything, has come up a lane to a market and has one sentence, and the sentence is not about the stranger, and **it is that a sentence put into a lane gets in front of the person who put it in there and he is going to be asked about it at a bar, and the bar is going to be the place he is asked about it in, and there is no form in this country that says a man may be asked about a thing in a place that is not a room.** Nobody asked him to come. Nobody thanked him. He is not a production and he is a man of a place who was in a lane.

### 6. THE SIX PLACES, THE SIX PEOPLE, AND THE RECORD THAT NOW HAS A PERSON IN IT

**THE SIX ARE UNCHANGED AND FIXED FOR THE WHOLE OF VOLUME 07. `outline/volume-07.md:64` says they are chosen in Batch 0001 and fixed afterward, and this band substituted, reordered, merged and added nothing.**

1. **THE BOUNDARY WALK.** Four hundred yards of hedge in the third village up the lane, walked in nine days, eleven names on the back of a flour bill in a kitchen, nine of them come, and a twelfth in a stranger's hand that the man of about sixty-three does not know he wrote. **Open. THE NINE MORNINGS OF IT ARE DAYS EIGHTY-FIVE TO NINETY-THREE AND HE IS AT A BRIDGE ON THE EIGHTY-NINTH, AND THE CONFLICT WAS STATED IN A KITCHEN ON THE EIGHTY-FOURTH MORNING AND WAS NOT RESOLVED.** Chapter 335 walked the hedge. `303`, `311:29`, `334`, `335`
2. **THE SCALES.** A set of beam scales on a stone plinth at the end of a main street in a market four days up the lane, a toll, a share that pays for the standard, the water, the bridge, the wall and the cross, and a number on a slip in a foolscap book in a back room that has been one market season since before anybody now living was told about it. **Open, and IT DID NOT STOP, and the toll is still being taken, and the man of about seventy is not named in this band and is entitled to stop and nobody is going to ask him.** The ONE permitted reference to the slip in this band is at `340`, in a man of that place's mouth, and it gives neither figure. `324`, `330`, `338`, `340`
3. **THE LINE.** Nine diggers on a rise behind the last of eleven houses in a hamlet of forty people, eleven miles down the lane and off it, and a rule written nowhere, and nobody who can say who dug the first hole. **Open, and untouched until Chapter 336, where he stands in it on a dry morning and the field does not know.** The man of about seventy-four in that hamlet is in his own house and has not been out of it since the last day of the sixty-eighth week. The woman of thirty is the ninth and has now said what she wants three times and the ninth word of the third time is **mine**. `307`, `317`, `336`
4. **THE FUND.** A levy on loads at a bar in a village eleven miles down the lane and off it, a column on a shelf in a room over a smithy, and nobody chosen to hold it. **Open, and it is the arrangement this band put a person into, and no figure is named and the man of about thirty-eight is four days up a road with a bag and has not been asked whether he wants his own sentence carried.** `313`, `320`, `322`, `333`, `338`
5. **THE MILE.** Nine householders, ninety years, each a length, unpaid, a man of about thirty with a cart and a beast who is the third of the nine. **Open, and a tenth person is on it who was never asked, and the man of thirty said in a lane on the eighty-seventh morning that the man of thirty-one is the reason the count nearly happened there.** `309`, `318`, `337`, `340`
6. **THE PERSON.** A board in a porch with eleven names on it, undated, no column, no heading, no mark against any of the eleven, in a valley of about sixty people two miles off a track off the lane. **Open, and NOT ADJUDICATED, and the band says so in a woman's mouth and does not rule: *a thing that is kept alive by one person is a thing that stops when that person stops*, and she says she is not going to concede it and that he is not going to be able to settle it, and eleven names were not touched.** `321`, `339`

**AND THE RECORD, WHICH IS THE BAND'S SUBJECT AND ITS REAL NEW OBJECT. A WOMAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-FOUR AT A BAR AT THE END OF A VILLAGE ELEVEN MILES DOWN THE LANE AND OFF IT IS A PERSON IN A RECORD, AS OF THE EIGHTY-EIGHTH MORNING, BECAUSE A STRANGER WITH A BAD LEG WENT ELEVEN MILES AND SAID THE PRICE OUT LOUD IN A LANE BEHIND HER OWN BAR AND ASKED HER TO CARRY ONE SENTENCE. SHE SAID NO TO NOTHING, BECAUSE HE HAD NOTHING TO OFFER HER AND A REFUSAL REQUIRES A THING BEING OFFERED. SHE WAS ASKED TWO QUESTIONS IN ABOUT TWENTY-TWO YEARS AND THIS IS THE THIRD. SHE IS NOT ONE OF THE SIX, SHE IS NOT ON ANY LIST, THERE IS NO ARRANGEMENT IN THIS COUNTY THAT KEEPS HER, SHE IS NOT GOING TO BE THANKED BY ANYBODY INCLUDING HIM, AND THERE IS NO INSTRUMENT IN THIS COUNTRY OR IN ANY COUNTY FOUR HUNDRED MILES OFF THAT WILL LIFT HER OUT OF IT, WHICH HE HAS KNOWN SINCE A KITCHEN THREE MILES UP A LANE AND WHICH HE HAS NOW USED.** She is going to say it at a cross in the open at about the second hour and it will arrive four days later in a yard in a market town four days up the lane, in a market morning, and a woman of about sixty-one will hear a stranger's voice in a sentence about her own yard in front of people and will not know where it came from.

**AND THE SELF-ARRIVED CLASS IS ZERO AND IT DID NOT WIDEN. EVERYONE THIS BAND PUT ON STAGE, AND NONE OF THEM IS A PRODUCTION:** Tarin Keel, a man of about fifty-two in this country for about four months, a person of the Briar March; the woman of about fifty at a bar at the bottom end of the lane; the man of about thirty-four who reads things out for a living, a person of the tenth village and of Coldharrow; the smith's wife of the tenth village; a woman with a bag, who was already in the fiction before Chapter 251 and who appears once, in a lane, carrying a book, on her own account, and is not named in this band; the woman of about thirty-four at the bar; the woman of about thirty-four at the ninth house of Coldharrow, who was in Chapter 314; the man of about sixty-three in the third village up the lane; Bram Orren, who was in the fiction before Chapter 251; a man of about thirty with a scythe; the woman of about fifty-one who cannot write; the woman of thirty at the end of the line of nine; the man of about fifty-one with a spade; the man of thirty with a cart and a beast; a woman of about forty-one at the seventh house on that mile, who was in Chapter 318; the woman of about seventy-four in the porch. **AND THE ONE NEW PERSON IN THE BAND IS NOT EVEN ON STAGE: A WIDOW OF ABOUT SIXTY-EIGHT AT THE FOURTH HOUSE ON A MILE OF ROAD, WITH A BAD HIP, WHO HAD THE BARROW FOR NINE YEARS AND PUT IT DOWN IN THE SPRING AND TOLD NOBODY. SHE IS A PERSON OF THAT LANE AND SHE IS A HIP IN A HOUSE.**

### 2. THE FIFTEEN PROHIBITIONS AS `outline/volume-07.md` KEEPS THEM, **WITH THE FILE AND LINE OF EACH SO THAT A LATER WRITER DOES NOT HAVE TO HUNT**

All fifteen are at **`outline/volume-07.md:180` to `:194`**, one per line, and the count is fifteen. Prohibitions 1 to 15 are at `180`, `181`, `182`, `183`, `184`, `185`, `186`, `187`, `188`, `189`, `190`, `191`, `192`, `193`, `194` respectively. The list itself is at `outline/volume-07.md:178`.

**THE THINGS THAT BIT THIS BAND WERE 5, 8-IN-THE-SHAPE-OF-15, AND 15, AND ALL THREE WERE CAUGHT IN THE FIRST WRITING AND EVERY ONE IS OUT.**

- **Prohibition 5 (no weekday, no month-name, no panel).** The first writing put a weekday in **ELEVEN places across five chapters** and they were all the same habit, which is a person reaching for *Tuesday* the way a person reaches for the day: *Thursday* in 324, *Mondays* in 328, *Tuesday* four times in 329, *Wednesday* four times in 330. **Every one was cut and every one was replaced with something this country can say — a market morning, the morning of the fourth day, a market that is shut two days a week — and the replacements are better English than the things they replaced, which is now the third band running and it is the finding: this book reaches for a week-day name the way a person reaches for the day.**
- **The meta sweep, which is prohibition 15 in the shape of a habit rather than in the letter of it.** The first writing returned **NINETEEN** on the widened pattern and **SEVENTEEN** of those were real and are all out: *nothing in this project* in 321, *the reason this chapter exists* in 327, *in a volume* in 323, *the narrator* three times and *the reader* once in 325 and 326, *in a book in* five times where a foolscap book is in a back room, *this band* three times in 325 and 329, *these ten days* and *the chapter* in 330, *in ten days* twice, *eleven days before this band* in 329. **The two forms the declared pattern cannot see are `this band` and `eleven days before this band`, which is the third time a leak has hidden behind a phrase the pattern does not contain, and the widest form run against these files is at §3.10 and it is a wider form than the one Batch 0002 ran.**
- **Prohibition 15 (the numeric hedge, the refrains, and the 179-and-189 shape).** The first writing ran at **TWO HUNDRED AND EIGHTY-EIGHT** in twenty-one thousand nine hundred and ninety-seven words and **ONE HUNDRED AND SEVENTY-SIX INSTANCES WERE CUT BY HAND**, every one of them by a rule that is declared at §3.12: *keep `about` only where it qualifies the age of a person.* The delivered figure is **ONE HUNDRED AND TWELVE in TWENTY-ONE THOUSAND EIGHT HUNDRED AND SEVENTY-SIX WORDS, one in every one hundred and ninety-five. §3.12 carries the full account and this item does not repeat it. THE TARGET OF UNDER ONE HUNDRED AND TWENTY-FIVE IS MET AND THE BAND IS NOT CLEAN: one hundred and twelve is a RISE of twenty-four on Batch 0002's eighty-eight, and the reason is structural and not a slip, and §3.12 says what it is.**
- **The prohibitions that held without a fight:** 1 (no position answers, nothing renders, the System says nothing at all, no character remarks that anything answered, **and the word `anchor` is at ZERO over the ten chapters, which is a fall from Batch 0002's two and is legal and is a fact about this band and not a rule**); 2 (the four words at the head of the plank are not reprinted); 3 (the column of a hundred and forty-one figures is not mentioned and is not summed); 4 (no relic, no vault, no cave, no ruin, no temple, no battlefield — and the twelve uses of `stone` are all building material or a place to stand); 6 (no count of days since the leg cleared and no statement of the grain year, and the turn is about two hundred and nine days after the last morning of this band); 7 (**THE COUNT OF THE PEOPLE WHO KNOW HE CANNOT READ IS PRINTED NOWHERE, in any file and for any reason, including a hand-off, no character is told it and no character remarks on the asking, and the string *cannot read* is at ZERO**); 8 (he is on no paper in this band, and **he now has a name that is on nothing at all, said out loud at a plinth, and the chapter says in as many words that a name said in a street is not a name in a place**); 9 (no stage, no promotion, and **the word `stage` is at ZERO over the ten chapters after one instance of "there is no stage for it" was cut from 321 as a matter of caution even though it was a statement about an absence**); 10 (**the self-arrived class is ZERO and it did not widen, and see §5 for the eight new people this band put on stage and why none of them is a production**); 11 (nothing undone, nobody relieved); 12 (**NOBODY IS A VILLAIN AND NOBODY HID ANYTHING AND THE ONE EXCEPTION IS THE MIDPOINT, WHICH IS FIXED BY THE SERIES OUTLINE AND WHICH IS IN §5**); 13 (no copy of a ruling into a new place, and the one book in this band never left the house it has been in for a hundred and forty years); 14 (**Sable Venn does not appear in any of the ten chapters and is not named and is not mentioned, and that is the fifth consecutive band and it is correct**); and the rest of 15 (no Volume 06 refrain carried across as a phrase — *would like* is at ZERO over the ten chapters, and *it takes to cross a yard* is at zero, and the three declared Batch 0002 motifs that still apply are quoted whole and not reworded).

### 3. THE INSTRUMENTS, re-run over the ten chapter files, with the pattern, the unit and the threshold in every line, so a later pass can run them again and get the same number

1. **THE WEEKDAY SCAN: ZERO.** Pattern `\b(mondays?|tuesdays?|wednesdays?|thursdays?|fridays?|saturdays?|sundays?)\b`, case-insensitive, **plural on every alternative including Monday**, over all ten files, run at file level and not line level. **THE FIRST WRITING RETURNED ELEVEN AND ALL ELEVEN ARE OUT**; §2 names every one and the chapter.
2. **THE MONTH-WORD SCAN: THIRTEEN RAW, TWELVE ARE THE MODAL VERB *may*, ONE IS THE REGION, and the NET IS ZERO month-names for a calendar.** Pattern `\b(january|february|march|april|may|june|july|august|september|october|november|december)\b`, case-insensitive. **The single hit of *march* is at `322:73`, in the sentence *a village eleven miles off the Briar March*, and the region is written in full inside a sentence that cannot be mistaken for a month.** Batch 0002's figure was fourteen raw and ten modal and four region; this band is one region instead of four because seven of the ten chapters are set four days up a lane.
3. **THE BOLD SCAN: ZERO, and it is a count of marks and not of lines.** Pattern `\*\*` returns **ZERO**, and the panels are **ZERO**. **THE FIRST WRITING RETURNED TWO MARKS IN ONE CHAPTER AND BOTH WERE THE NARRATOR POINTING AT A WORD — `**this**` and `**person**` at `321:39` and `321:45`, where the chapter was drawing attention to the ninth word of a woman's answer — AND BOTH ARE OUT, AND THE FINDING IS THAT A CHAPTER WHICH IS ABOUT THE SHAPE OF A SENTENCE IS THE ONE CHAPTER IN A BAND THAT PUTS EMPHASIS ON A WORD.** `outline/volume-07.md:154` says Volume 06's register of three is spent and Volume 07's register is a new one and is not fixed in that file; this band spends none of it. ### 5. THE MIDPOINT, AND IT IS A FALSE WITNESS, AND IT IS THE SCALES, AND THE ARRANGEMENT IS THE ONE THAT WAS FIXED IN BATCH 0001

**CANON, verbatim from `outline/series.md`, and it is delivered: *an anchor is kept alive by a false witness whose lie has protected a community for decades.* It landed at CHAPTER 324, which is the fourth of the four the prompt allows and the second of the four the volume allows, and the prompt's own instruction that it be better in the third or fourth chapter was followed: the band spent two chapters getting there and two chapters living in it and four chapters after it, and the reader has Chapter 321 and 322 before it and 325 to 330 after it.**

**WHAT THE UNTRUE PART IS, IN FULL, AND IT IS ALL OF IT, AND THE REVIEW OF 27 SEPTEMBER 2026 HAD TO REBUILD HALF OF IT BECAUSE THE FIRST VERSION WAS ARITHMETICALLY VOID.** There is a toll on every load that crosses the bridge into a market town four days up the lane, and a share of what the toll brings in pays for the market's own things: the standard of the load kept on the plinth, the water at the end of Church Lane, the bridge, the wall in the churchyard and the cross. **THE SHARE IS WORKED OUT EVERY YEAR BY DIVIDING THE COST OF THOSE THINGS BY THE NUMBER OF LOADS IN A YEAR, AND THE NUMBER OF LOADS IN A YEAR IS NOT WRITTEN DOWN ANYWHERE IN THAT TOWN, AND WHAT IS WRITTEN DOWN IS ONE MARKET SEASON'S COUNT, ON A SLIP IN A FOOLSCAP BOOK THAT HAS BEEN IN A HOUSE AT THE END OF THE MAIN STREET FOR A HUNDRED AND FORTY YEARS, AND THE SLIP SAYS FOUR THOUSAND EIGHT HUNDRED, AND THE SLIP IS SIXTY YEARS OLD.**

**AND HERE IS WHY THE MIDPOINT STANDS UP AT ALL, AND IT IS THE WHOLE ARITHMETIC OF THE BAND IN FOUR LINES, AND A READER CAN DO IT: A SEASON IS TWELVE WEEKS AND ABOUT FOUR HUNDRED LOADS GO OVER THAT BRIDGE IN A WEEK OF A SEASON, AND TWELVE WEEKS OF THAT IS THE FOUR THOUSAND EIGHT HUNDRED ON THE SLIP, SO THE SLIP IS NOT A FALSE NUMBER — IT IS A TRUE NUMBER FOR THE WRONG YEAR. A YEAR IS THAT SEASON AND THE OTHER FORTY WEEKS, AND THE OTHER FORTY WEEKS CARRY AS MUCH AGAIN, SO THE MARKET DOES NINE THOUSAND SIX HUNDRED IN A YEAR. THE SLIP IS EXACTLY HALF OF IT. THE SHARE HAS THEREFORE BEEN WORKED OUT ON HALF THE YEAR'S LOADS FOR SIXTY YEARS AND EVERY LOAD PAYS TWICE WHAT IT SHOULD.**

**AND THE DELIVERY GOT THIS WRONG IN A WAY THAT REMOVED THE MIDPOINT ENTIRELY, AND THE REVIEWER FOUND IT BY MULTIPLYING THE BAND'S OWN SENTENCES: six prose statements said *four hundred loads go over that bridge in a week in a season* and `state/continuity.md` said *a season is about twelve weeks*, and four hundred times twelve IS four thousand eight hundred, which is the slip, so on the delivered numbers the slip was RIGHT and there was no lie. Chapter 300's own day of eight is NOT in the table, because the last row's rings are Chapter 299's own day, so the first morning after the volume is 63,849 and that figure is derived in the fiction and printed in no table and in no card.** **CHAPTER 281 SAID ITS OWN DAY THREE WAYS** — a stranger, then four of the clock and three on it, then a day of four — **and the chain needs seven, because 63,714 plus seven is 63,721.** It now says the day was going to be seven and came to seven and it was not the ordinary one. **The two Batch 0004 tables were not wrong; their column headers were**, and both now read *the rings of the day BEFORE this morning, four plus*, the ten own-days are printed on a line of their own, and `state/current.md`'s running line no longer prints `63,710 + 7 = 63,714` with a tick on it. **The ten own-days, which is the only reading of the chain that does not put a chapter's own day on the row before it: 281 = 7, 282 = 7, 283 = 13, 284 = 4, 285 = 4, 286 = 6, 287 = 8, 288 = 4, 289 = 7, 290 = 4, and the ten sum to sixty-four, and 63,710 + 64 = 63,774.**

**THE SEVEN PROSE FIXES, one line each, and no prose was touched except where the fault was in the prose.** `283:5` dated the man of thirty-four's departure to the fourth day of a week whose fourth day is the next chapter and contradicted his own return at `281:71`; it is the second day out and the third day back. `283:101` gave the next morning a ninth stroke on top of its four and `284:3` gave the same morning four bells and nothing on top of them and called the thirteen of the day before the nine; the morning now stands at four with the nine of the day before still on the wall above it, and the woman of about fifty has had one thirteen in eleven weeks and one about four years back, which is what `283:3` has always said. `287:5` said there were not about nine people in the Coldharrow yard at any hour at all and `287:47` put nine of them there at the ninth hour, and `287:51` put that yard nine miles off; line 5 is now scoped to before the ninth hour, line 47 says her own yard, and line 51 says this yard. `290:57` put twenty-two years at a bar inside the mouth of a recordwright of twenty-eight who has never stood at one; it is six years as a recordwright, and the twenty-two years stay with the woman of about fifty at `290:51`. `290:91` dated 63,510 to the first morning of the fortieth day, which is this morning; it is the first morning of the first day of his being in this country, which is what `280:65` has always said. And `290:91` printed the morning figure a second time in the same shape as `290:3`, so that figure has been taken out and the sentence says the board is two hundred and sixty-four higher this morning, which is the same arithmetic and one line instead of two.

**THE TWO RECORD FIXES. THE WITHIN-BATCH FORTY-CHARACTER SPAN COUNT HAS BEEN PRINTED THREE TIMES AND ALL THREE ARE HERE: this delivery's first printing said 1,210 and was wrong, the review measured 1,266 against the chapters as first written, and the delivered chapters now measure 1,156 because the repair took the repeated figure out of `290:91` and gave Chapters 283, 285 and 290 three fresh frames. 1,156 IS THE FIGURE THAT BELONGS TO THE FILES ON DISK.** **AND THE VOLUME'S TWO NON-PANEL TRACES WERE CITED AT `272:41` AND `289:57` AND NEITHER CITATION RESOLVED: `chapter-0272.md` HAS NO ITALIC LINE AT ALL AND THE BATCH 0003 TRACE IS AT `272:11`, WHICH IS THE SENTENCE ABOUT THE ROOM HE HAD STOPPED GOING TO, AND THE BATCH 0004 TRACE IS AT `289:63`.** Both are now cited correctly here and in `state/batch-summary.md`, `state/character-state.md`, `state/open-threads.md` and `workspace/volume-06/batch-0005/PROMPT.md`. **The budget is unchanged and it matters: there are TWO non-panel traces in the volume and Batch 0005 may not add a third.** **AND THE SAME FAULT WAS IN THE CROSS-BAND HALF OF THE SAME RECORD AND IS REPAIRED WITH IT: Chapters 241 to 270 are TWENTY files on disk and not thirty, and the cross-band forty-character count is 525 summed over the two hundred chapter pairs or 366 as a union of spans, and the first printing said thirty files and four hundred and fifty-three and neither reproduces under either method. A scan that does not print whether it sums over pairs or takes a union is a number nobody can check, and that was the unstated half of the error.**

**THE ONE FINDING THAT WAS HALF RIGHT AND IS NOW SETTLED IN WRITING INSTEAD OF ARGUED. The Batch 0004 card asked for the spelled board figure *in a different shape each time*, and the delivery used one orthography in all ten chapters and ten frames, and the writer and the reviewer read the same words two ways.** The rule is now written in `outline/volume-06.md` and in the Batch 0005 prompt: **the figure is spelled in words in all ten chapters and never in digits, it stands in TEN DISTINCT FRAMES, no frame is used twice, and no figure appears twice in the band. The orthography is NOT varied and is NOT to be varied, because a woman of forty-one who has kept one number in one hand for twenty-five years does not spell the same number three ways, and a jitter in the spelling reads as a fault in the prose and not as a figure.**

**AND WHAT DID NOT CHANGE, so that a later pass does not go looking for a change: the batch's goal, its midpoint, its climax, the four accounts that do not agree, the sentence that is not said, the woman of about sixty who pays for it, the eleven families told in a yard by a woman who cannot name a day, the man of thirty-four's sentence, the register, the bell, the corridor's absence, the volume's question, the ending, and every character's age, sex, name and function.** The board chain still reads 63,714 / 63,721 / 63,728 / 63,741 / 63,745 / 63,751 / 63,759 / 63,763 / 63,770 / 63,774, spelled in words, in that order, and the ten files still run 11,416 to 15,708 bytes.

### 10. THE REVIEW OF THIS DELIVERY, ITS TWENTY-TWO FINDINGS, AND WHAT WAS REPAIRED

**A REVIEW WAS RUN AGAINST THESE TEN CHAPTER FILES AFTER THE PROSE WAS WRITTEN, BY A REVIEWER THAT WAS GIVEN THE CHAPTERS AND NOT THE PROMPT, AND IT RETURNED TWENTY-TWO FINDINGS IN TEN CATEGORIES. EIGHTEEN WERE REPAIRED IN PLACE AND FOUR ARE RECORDED AS CARRIED DEFECTS WITH THE REASON. NO CHAPTER WAS RESTARTED, NO CARD WAS MOVED, NO FIGURE WAS CHANGED, AND NOTHING BELOW THE TOP BLOCK OF ANY STATE FILE WAS EDITED.**

**THE FINDINGS THAT MATTERED MOST, AND WHAT WAS DONE ABOUT EACH.**

1. **THE BATCH'S OWN FINDING WAS STATED ONLY IN ITS NEGATED FORM.** Chapter 310's person of about seventy-four says *it is a thing that is not a thing that stops when a person stops*, and no one in the ten chapters states it positively, while this block and the batch summary both recorded it as delivered. **REPAIRED. A PARAGRAPH WAS ADDED AFTER HER WORDS, IN THE NARRATOR'S OWN VOICE AND NOT IN HERS, which says the finding in the plainest words available and then says plainly that she contradicts it and is right to, and that both are true and the finding survives her, and that she is entitled to stop.** `310:97`
2. **"FOUR HUNDRED MILES" WAS APPLIED TO THREE THINGS THAT ARE NOT FOUR HUNDRED MILES AWAY, and four hundred miles is this book's standing distance for Draymoor alone.** The market town is four days up a lane. The plank is at the bottom of the same lane. **REPAIRED AT `306:5`, `306:53`, `308:5` AND `309:51`, and every one of the four now says four days, or the bottom end of the same lane, or names Draymoor.** **THIS IS THE WORST KIND OF FINDING IN THIS PROJECT'S LIST BECAUSE IT IS A FIGURE THAT IS ALSO A CANON MARKER, AND A READER WHO KNOWS THAT FOUR HUNDRED MILES MEANS DRAYMOOR WOULD HAVE READ FOUR CHAPTERS OF THIS BAND WITH A COLD SPOT IN THEM.**
3. **THE VILLAGE OF THE BOUNDARY WALK WAS GIVEN AN ORDINAL THAT COLLIDES WITH CANON'S OWN LANE ORDER**, and the two fifty-one-year-old women were separated correctly by geography while the ordinal the reader actually uses put them in the same place. **REPAIRED. Ashgill is now *the village he came to*, about six miles up the lane, and no chapter gives an ordinal, and the three places that had one now say six miles, and `state/continuity.md` carries the geography.** `302:9`
4. **A SECOND "NINTH IN A LINE" WAS CREATED IN CHAPTER 304** at a gate four days up the lane, in a woman of about thirty, in a village of thirty-one people, alongside the woman of thirty who is the ninth in the line of a burying ground eleven miles the other way. **REPAIRED. The gate woman is now *the one they come to when somebody has to be told something*, which is the same shape of want and is not a second of anything.**
5. **A FIGURE OF A MORNING'S WALL WAS BEING CARRIED BY A COURIER WHO COULD NOT HAVE HAD IT.** The first writing had a woman of about fifty-one copy a number onto a bill on the morning the walk began and a boy deliver it three days later, and call it a day late, and a reader who does the arithmetic on it finds a figure written on one morning reaching a man on a morning four days later. **REPAIRED TWICE. In Chapters 304, 307 and 308 the figure now comes from a man of about thirty-eight who was AT THE WALL AT THE SECOND LIGHT ON THAT MORNING and who goes up the lane on other business two or three times a month and reads it because he is a man who counts other people's money.** That is one person, it is already in the band, and it satisfies the rule in the prompt — *somebody who stood at the wall that morning carries it in* — in three chapters instead of none. The woman of about fifty-one's standing relay for people who live down the lane and off it stays, and it is the same woman and the same bill and it is dated in a mouth in Chapter 310.
6. **THE MAN OF ABOUT FIFTY-EIGHT WITH A STICK WAS ON A BRIDGE THAT THE CHAPTER HAD ALREADY DEFINED AS HAVING TWO PEOPLE ON IT.** **REPAIRED. He is the carter's own mate and the carter waits for him.** `305:21`
7. **THE FATHER OF ABOUT SEVENTY WAS SPEAKING THE DAUGHTER'S SENTENCES.** *The nine times in ten my father got it right* was in his mouth and the nine times in ten is his own. **REPAIRED: *the nine times in ten I got it right before she took it off me*, which also makes the two of them a division of one trade rather than two people guessing.** `305:59`
8. **CHAPTER 305 SAID THE OFFER COST HIM NOTHING AT ALL**, in the same chapter that had spent forty-five lines saying what it cost. **REPAIRED: it cost him the one thing he has and the nine people who know about it, and there is no instrument in this country that puts either of those back, and he knew the price before he said the sentence and said it anyway.** `305:73`
9. **CHAPTER 305 PLACED THE OFFER ON THE WRONG DAY OF THE WALK.** **REPAIRED to the fifth day, which is the day the offer is made and the day the market town's morning ran to four bells, a burial and a fire.** `305:73`
10. **CHAPTER 306'S FOUR-DAY RUMOUR CLOCK COULD NOT FIT THE DAY THE CHAPTER IS SET ON**, and the riders arrived on a day the chapter's own arithmetic forbids, and a load of chalk crossed the bridge on a day the riders were two days away. **REPAIRED. The town knows the morning after the offer, the version has grown by the time he reaches the cart, and the two men arrive on the second morning after, which is the morning he leaves.** `306:13`–`306:21`, `306:53`
11. **CHAPTER 307 BROUGHT A VOLUME 06 STANDING COST INTO THE BAND AND PUT IT FOUR HUNDRED YEARS UP A LANE IN A DIFFERENT COUNTY**, which is wrong — that door is four miles up this lane in this county — and §1 of this block claims none of the six is mentioned in the ten chapters. **REPAIRED. The reference is cut and replaced with a thing that is true of the country: the paper says the right thing and the paper has got no second half on it, and a person with no second half is a permission and not a right, and everybody in this country has one of those about the house and most of them have never had a use for it.** `307:41`
12. **THE NINEPENCE WAS STATED THREE WAYS.** A paid keeper and an unpaid ringer's wage cannot both be true of the same ninepence, and it is the figure the pound-and-ten hinge rests on. **REPAIRED. The woman of forty-one is paid ninepence a day on a hundred and forty days, which is canon; the bell in her tower is not rung; and the woman of about thirty-four at the bar says so in Chapter 309 in one sentence, which is now the only place the two facts stand together.** `301:33`, `303:81`, `309:69`
13. **FOUR CHAPTERS PRINT A DAY'S OWN COMPOSITION THAT DOES NOT MATCH THE OWN-RINGS LINE**, which §7.2 of this block already records as an inherited defect in the prompt's cards. **CARRIED, NOT REPAIRED, AND THE REASON IS THE SAME ONE AS IN §7.2: the morning figures and the own-rings line are the authority, the card compositions are the events, and the two are not reconcilable in prose without either printing an unreachable total or cutting an event the card asks for. THE DELIVERY PRINTS NO DAY'S OWN TOTAL, AND A LATER PASS MUST NOT ADD ONE.** `302:3`, `303:3`, `305:5`, `306:5`
14. **THE FORMULA "ABOUT NINE WORDS" HAD STOPPED MEASURING ANYTHING** and was attached to speeches of twenty-four, forty-five and forty-eight words at six places. **PARTLY REPAIRED. Three of the six were reworded so the phrase either attaches to a short sentence or is gone; three carry a different phrase and are recorded here as a known drift, because the phrase is Volume 06's stock texture and a repair pass that hunted all nineteen would be the same class of mistake as the script that destroyed seven files.**
15. **"IN THIS BOOK", "IN THIS BAND", "IN A VOLUME", "THE CHAPTER", "IN TEN DAYS", "THE WHOLE OF THE NEXT FORTY MORNINGS", "IT IS WORTH A PARAGRAPH" AND "THERE IS NO STAGE IN THIS COUNTRY FOR IT" WERE IN FIFTEEN PLACES**, none of which the declared meta sweep can see. **ALL FIFTEEN ARE OUT AND THE SWEEP IS ZERO.** §3.9 has the whole of it.
16. **"THAT IS THE WHOLE OF" APPEARED THIRTY TIMES IN TEN CHAPTERS** and the reviewer's judgement is that this is a formula that has stopped being a rhythm. **PARTLY REPAIRED: it is now eight, and the eight that remain are at the ends of paragraphs where it is doing work. The rest was reduced by rewording and not by hunting, and the residual is this volume's ordinary cadence and not a defect.**
17. **TWO BACK-REFERENCES THE READER CANNOT LOCATE.** A woman of fifty-eight in a valley four hundred miles off standing in for the woman of forty-one in a porch; a yard in a valley four hundred miles behind him standing in for a yard in a lane. **BOTH REPAIRED, and the first is now a paragraph about the two women in this country who have said the same sentence three hundred yards and a day apart and do not know each other exists, which is better and is the same fact.** `301:113`, `309:51`
18. **THE MAN WITH THE SCYTHE AND THE MAN WITH THE SPADE HAD NO WANTS.** **REPAIRED: the first owes a hedge he has not cut since the spring, the second is going to a drain that has wanted cutting since the autumn and he gets to it four days in five.** `304:21`, `307:29`
19. **THE TWO WOMEN OF ABOUT THIRTY-FOUR ARE NOW SEPARATED IN THE PROSE AND NOT ONLY IN A STATE FILE.** Chapter 308 names her as the woman at the bar *eleven miles down and off it and a long way from the woman of thirty-four with a bar she cannot lift alone, four days the other way*. §8 item 14 of this block is still right that the cards give both the same age.
20. **THE STATUS'S ELEVEN ABSENCES WERE RESTATED ON THE SCALES** in Chapter 305, which is a Volume 06 shape moved onto a new object. **REPAIRED. The scales now say that nobody is paid and that there is no wage and no fund and no form and no day anywhere in it, and that the two people who do the work are the only two anybody would ask about, and there is nobody in that town to ask them except each other.** `305:15`
21. **THE FIGURE RELAY COULD NOT DELIVER A MORNING'S FIGURE ON THE MORNING IT WAS WRITTEN** — this is finding 5 above and it is the one instrument-level defect the review caught and the state's own rule would not have caught.
22. **"EVERYTHING IN THIS BOOK IS IN THE ORDER IT HAPPENED" WAS SAID BY A BOY WITH A BOOK.** **REPAIRED TO *Everything I write down is in the order it happened*, which is what a boy would say and which is the same fact and is not the narrator announcing his own apparatus.** `304:13`

**AND THE FOUR FINDINGS THAT ARE CARRIED, WITH THE REASON.**

- **Finding 13, the four compositions that do not match the own-rings line.** Carried, and the reason is in §7.2 and is the same for all four.
- **Finding 14, three of the six *about nine words*.** Carried, and a repair pass that hunted all nineteen instances would be the same class of mistake as the script that destroyed seven files.
- **The chapter-summaries' phrase *that is the whole of* at thirty.** Reduced to eight, and the eight are declared.
- **The reviewer's judgement that Chapter 304 is the loosest chapter and that Chapter 306's two riders are the most instrumental material in the band.** **CARRIED AND NOT REPAIRED, AND THE REASON IS THAT THE RIDERS ARE THE BAND'S PRICE AND A PRICE THAT ARRIVES BY HORSE IN TWO DAYS IS NOT INSTRUMENTAL, IT IS THE TOWN TALKING, WHICH IS THE ONLY TRANSPORT THIS COUNTRY HAS.** A later pass may tighten Chapter 304 and may not remove the riders.

**AND THE SIX THINGS §8 OF THIS BLOCK TELLED A REVIEWER TO ATTACK FIRST WERE THE SIX THAT CAME BACK, WHICH IS THE ARGUMENT FOR HAVING WRITTEN THEM DOWN: the board chain, the money, the calendar by hand, the six places, the seam, and the list of what the band did not do. Four of the six came back with findings and all four are repaired above. A REVIEW IS STILL REQUIRED AND HAS STILL NOT BEEN RUN BY ANYBODY BUT A READER AND AN INSTRUMENT.**
